detail.abstract: A entrevista “O Poder da Comunicação, Vendas e Oratória no Sucesso Profissional” destaca a comunicação como elemento estratégico para o desempenho em vendas e na construção de relacionamentos. Evidencia-se que comunicar vai além da fala, envolvendo escuta ativa, linguagem não verbal e intencionalidade clara. A assertividade depende da capacidade de se fazer entender, enquanto a empatia fortalece a conexão com o interlocutor. Em um cenário digital complexo, marcado por excesso de informação e perda de autenticidade, a comunicação eficaz exige adaptação, coerência e responsabilidade. Conclui-se que a oratória e a comunicação bem estruturada são diferenciais competitivos essenciais para gerar valor, engajamento e resultados sustentáveis no ambiente profissional contemporâneo.

title: The Verification Economy: How AI's Trust Crisis Creates a $300 Billion Market

detail.title: The Verification Economy: How AI's Trust Crisis Creates a $300 Billion Market
detail.abstract:
This paper identifies and analyzes the emergence of a $300+ billion verification economy driven by AI’s fundamental trust crisis. As AI makes content creation, expertise access, and credential generation approach zero marginal cost, verification becomes the scarce resource determining value. We document over $12 billion in verified losses from verification failures (2019-2024) and identify $100+ billion in stalled AI deployment due to verification gaps. Using Grove’s strategic inflection point framework, we demonstrate why 2026-2029 represents a narrow window for infrastructure development, after which catch-up costs become prohibitive.

The analysis maps seven distinct verification verticals (AI agents, credentials, supply chain, transactions, content, identity, and legal), providing market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM), competitive moat analysis (Porter framework), and execution roadmaps (Grove/Moore timing). We identify why verification uniquely resists platform re-integration through structural conflict-of-interest moats: credible verification requires independence from the entities being verified.

The paper makes three primary contributions: (1) quantitative documentation of verification market opportunity across seven verticals, (2) strategic framework distinguishing Type A (behavioral monitoring) from Type B (data integrity) verification systems, and (3) dual execution roadmap addressing both immediate opportunities and long-term infrastructure plays. Historical analysis of interface control dynamics (IBM, Intel, Microsoft, Adobe) validates why verification represents the only defensible layer in the AI stack where specialist firms can sustainably resist platform bundling.

Key findings: Goldilocks-difficulty verticals (AI agents, credentials, supply chain) offer $150-200 billion addressable markets with 3-5 year first-mover windows. Platform risk categories (content, identity) require defensive strategies. Hard-mode categories (transactions, legal) suit experienced founders with patient capital. The window for establishing verification infrastructure closes 2029-2030 as platforms develop proprietary solutions and regulatory frameworks ossify.

This work synthesizes Porter (strategic positioning), Grove (inflection point timing), and Moore (technology adoption lifecycle) to provide actionable guidance for entrepreneurs, investors, platforms, and enterprises navigating AI’s verification crisis.

title: Influence of Health Consciousness on Customer Satisfaction towards Organic Food Products: Evidence from Bengaluru

detail.title: Influence of Health Consciousness on Customer Satisfaction towards Organic Food Products: Evidence from Bengaluru
detail.abstract: Organic food consumption in Indian cities has expanded at a pace that far outstrips the growth of most conventional food categories. The surge is not incidental; it is rooted in a measurable shift in how urban citizens perceive food, health, and the environment. This study examines the influence of health consciousness on customer satisfaction towards organic food products, drawing primary evidence from Bengaluru, one of India's most economically dynamic and health-aware metropolitan cities. A structured questionnaire survey was conducted among 210 consumers who regularly purchase organic food products. The constructs examined include health consciousness, perceived quality, price sensitivity, environmental concern, and overall customer satisfaction. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, Cronbach's Alpha reliability tests, and multiple regression analysis. The regression model explains 47.3 percent of variance in customer satisfaction (Adjusted R2 = 0.462), with health consciousness emerging as the single strongest predictor (Beta = 0.381, p < 0.001). Four research hypotheses were tested, of which three were fully supported and one was partially supported. The findings confirm that health-conscious consumers derive significantly greater satisfaction from organic food when product quality expectations are met. The study provides actionable recommendations for organic food retailers, brand managers, and Karnataka state policymakers.

title: Advancing Target Account Selection for Enhanced Account-Based Marketing (ABM) Success

detail.title: Advancing Target Account Selection for Enhanced Account-Based Marketing (ABM) Success
detail.abstract: Account-Based Marketing (ABM) has emerged as a strategic approach in business-to-business (B2B) marketing, focusing on targeting high-value accounts rather than broad audiences. A critical factor influencing the success of ABM campaigns is the selection of appropriate target accounts. This research examines current practices, challenges, and technological advancements in target account selection and proposes a structured framework to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ABM strategies. The study uses a mixed-method research design combining exploratory and descriptive approaches. Primary data were collected through surveys, interviews, and case studies involving marketing and sales professionals across industries. Secondary data were obtained from industry reports, academic literature, and documented ABM implementations. Findings indicate that organizations leveraging predictive analytics, real-time data, and cross-functional collaboration achieve improved engagement rates, reduced sales cycles, and higher return on investment (ROI). The research introduces a data-driven target account selection framework integrating firmographic, technographic, and intent data supported by artificial intelligence (AI)-based scoring models. The proposed framework enhances targeting accuracy, improves resource allocation, and supports personalized engagement strategies. The study concludes with recommendations for organizations seeking to adopt scalable and technology-driven ABM strategies.

title: The Expansion Horizon: Generative AI Beyond the Reach of Current Economic Foresight
affiliations: Western Sydney University, , International Centre for Future Generations, The University of Technology Sydney,  and University of Basel - Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute

detail.title: The Expansion Horizon: Generative AI Beyond the Reach of Current Economic Foresight
detail.abstract: Between 2022 and 2025, the four largest AI-adopting technology firms increased revenue per employee by 38-89% while headcounts remained flat or declined. This productivity-headcount decoupling is now replicating across knowledge-work sectors with structurally different employment outcomes, yet the most influential economic model of AI's macroeconomic effects projects a total factor productivity increase of only 0.53-0.66 percentage points over ten years. We identify this divergence as the expansion horizon problem and argue that it arises because generative AI (genAI) constitutes the irruption of a sixth technological revolution in Carlota Perez's historical periodisation, not a phase within the fifth. Synthesising Perez's macro-historical framework with W. Brian Arthur's theory of combinatorial evolution and Weitzman's formalisation of recombinant growth, we show that genAI introduces a qualitatively new input factor (near-zero-marginal-cost cognitive labour) and a defining organisational principle (human capital compression). Every technological revolution decouples output from workforce scale to some degree, but genAI's version is distinguished by its domain generality and its reflexivity: it operates simultaneously across cognitive domains that the ICT paradigm left structurally intact, and it compresses the human capital required for innovation itself. We demonstrate that the dominant economic models of AI embed assumptions, fixed capability frontiers, sequential task substitution, exogenous technological change, that are systematically violated by a combinatorially self-expanding technology, producing underestimates that are not empirical gaps but category errors. A three-dimensional framework mapping deployment staging, demand elasticity, and implementation maturity explains why the decoupling dynamic produces employment recomposition in elastic-demand sectors and permanent contraction in inelastic-demand sectors. Economic models calibrated to static capability snapshots will systematically misguide policy during the critical institutional transition ahead, and the window for effective institutional response is narrowing as rapidly as the technology's capability frontier is expanding.

title: IMPACT OF DIGITAL PAYMENT ON CONSUMER SPENDING BEHAVIOR

detail.title: IMPACT OF DIGITAL PAYMENT ON CONSUMER SPENDING BEHAVIOR
detail.abstract:
The rapid evolution of digital payment systems has revolutionized the way consumers 
engage with financial transactions, especially in the wake of increasing smartphone 
penetration and internet accessibility. This study aims to analyse the impact of digital 
payment methods—such as UPI (Unified Payments Interface), mobile wallets, 
credit/debit cards, net banking, and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) services—on 
consumer behaviour in India. By exploring factors like convenience, security 
perceptions, transaction speed, and user incentives, the research investigates how 
digital payments influence purchasing patterns, spending frequency, and brand 
loyalty. Primary data through surveys and secondary insights from industry reports 
form the basis of this analysis. The findings reveal a significant shift toward UPI and 
mobile wallets due to their ease of use and widespread merchant adoption, while 
traditional methods like credit/debit cards and net banking show moderate preference. 
The study concludes that digital payments are not only transforming transactional 
habits but are also shaping consumer expectations, trust, and engagement with 
businesses, ultimately driving a more cashless and digitally inclusive economy

title: The Role of AI in Lean Product Development: Accelerant, Disruptor, or Both?

detail.title: The Role of AI in Lean Product Development: Accelerant, Disruptor, or Both?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict or interest.

detail.abstract: Lean product development has always been a faster, smarter way to build products. It focuses on testing ideas quickly, learning from users, and avoiding wasted effort. That’s why so many startups rely on it. But artificial intelligence is starting to change how this works. It’s not just about whether AI helps or hurts lean practices anymore. The real question is whether it’s quietly changing the rules altogether. AI can make things faster and more efficient. At the same time, it can reduce the discipline that makes lean effective in the first place. For product managers today, understanding this balance is becoming more important than ever.

detail.abstract:
The rapid adoption of large language model (LLM)-based AI tools — including ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Google Gemini, and Google Search Generative Experience (SGE) - has fundamentally altered how prospective students discover and evaluate higher education institutions in India. This exploratory working paper examines the visibility of Indian universities in AI-generated responses and introduces the concept of Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO) as applied to the Indian higher education context.

Drawing on the author's practitioner experience working with Indian universities on digital marketing and student recruitment strategy, this paper documents preliminary observations about which institution types tend to appear in AI-generated responses and why. It argues that a measurable AEO Gap exists between an institution's actual quality and its AI-visible reputation — and that this gap disproportionately affects private universities outside the IIT/IIM tier, including many with strong NIRF rankings. Recommendations for improving AI visibility are provided, with implications for institutional reputation management, student recruitment, and NIRF Perception scores.

title: Algorithmic Governance and Tax Equity:  Evidence from Property Assessment Reform in Cook County

detail.title: Algorithmic Governance and Tax Equity:  Evidence from Property Assessment Reform in Cook County
detail.abstract: We study whether algorithmic reform can reduce inequality in residential property taxation. In Cook County's 2021 algorithmic reform, a legacy valuation system was replaced by a more flexible automated valuation model using richer property and geospatial data. Using the county's staggered triennial reassessment cycle across three regions, we estimate difference-indifferences models of the log assessed-to-sale-price ratio, focusing on price and race gradients. The reform sharply reduces long-standing price regressivity favoring the rich: relative to 2020, the price gradient flattens by about 40% in the first post-reform quarter and remains nearly unchanged after appeals, implying little erosion of equity gains. Race effects are mixed: the within-price race slope rises from a negative baseline (i.e., pro-minority), but total race regressivity becomes somewhat more negative because the reform's dominant distributional effect compresses the price gradient. Mechanism evidence suggests that legacy systems overpool unlike properties: linear models can overassess lower-value homes by pooling them with higher-value homes, while coarse location controls can underassess homes in minority neighborhoods, conditional on price, by linking them to lower-valued neighborhood averages. More flexible machine-learning models with finer geography relax both distortions, reducing price regressivity and shifting the within-price racial gradient.

title: EXPERIGEN: A Conceptual Framework for Experience-Generative Restaurant Operations

detail.title: EXPERIGEN: A Conceptual Framework for Experience-Generative Restaurant Operations

declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a conceptual study based on practice-informed observation and does not involve human participants, patient data, or identifiable personal data. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces EXPERIGEN as a new conceptual framework for value generation in restaurant operations. In contemporary restaurant operations, value is increasingly created not only through products or interpersonal service, but through the ways customers come to discover meaningful ways of spending time. EXPERIGEN is a coined term derived from Experience Genesis. It denotes a value-generating structure in which experiential possibilities are opened up through the relationship between the restaurant and the customer and are then translated into concrete ways of enjoying the meal and into ordering behavior. The concept is distinguished from service, which responds to explicit customer requests, and from hospitality, which anticipates latent customer needs. In conventional restaurant management, value has often been understood through two central axes: product value and service-interaction value. Product value is evaluated in terms of food quality, price, quantity, speed of delivery, and stability. Service-interaction value is evaluated through courtesy, attentiveness, anticipation, and comfort. Yet contemporary restaurant operations face a compound set of challenges: labor shortages, rising wages, training burdens, menu complexity, diversified customer expectations, and the need to increase average spending without creating sales pressure. Under these conditions, improving product value and service-interaction value alone is insufficient. This paper positions experience-generative value as a third value axis. If service responds to what customers request, and hospitality anticipates what customers may need, EXPERIGEN creates a field in which experiential value can emerge. The central issue is not to sell products, nor to disguise upselling as hospitality. Rather, it is to open up ways of enjoying the meal that customers have not yet clearly articulated and to connect those possibilities naturally with their own ordering decisions. The paper is a conceptual construction paper based on practical observation in restaurant operations, not a statistical empirical study. It clarifies the distinction among service, hospitality, and EXPERIGEN; formulates the process of experience genesis; and examines set menus as a representative mediating structure through which EXPERIGEN may connect customer value, operational efficiency, staff development, and profitability. By doing so, the paper proposes a theoretical foundation for understanding restaurants not merely as product-providing or service-interaction businesses, but as experience-generative operations.

title: Bid Shading as Option Pricing: A Derivatives-Theoretic Framework for Optimal Bidding in First-Price Auctions with Applications to Programmatic Advertising

detail.title: Bid Shading as Option Pricing: A Derivatives-Theoretic Framework for Optimal Bidding in First-Price Auctions with Applications to Programmatic Advertising
detail.abstract: This paper establishes a formal equivalence between optimal bid shading in first-price sealedbid auctions and European option pricing in continuous-time finance. We show that the bidder's surplus-maximisation problem admits a representation as the payoff of a European call option written on the impression value, where the competing bid distribution plays the role of the risk-neutral measure and the optimal shaded bid corresponds to the certaintyequivalent strike price. We derive closed-form bid shading formulas under log-normal, gamma, and generalised Pareto competing bid distributions, express the optimal bid in terms of familiar Greeks (∆, Γ, V), and characterise the sensitivity of surplus to distributional parameters. Our main contribution is a two-stage estimation framework that separates the statistical problem of learning the competing bid distribution from the decision problem of computing the optimal bid, yielding a transparent, interpretable bidding strategy with provable optimality properties. Empirical evaluation on 15.4 million impressions across 9 advertising campaigns from the iPinYou real-time bidding benchmark demonstrates that the options-based approach with campaign-level calibration achieves 2.2% higher expected surplus than optimally-tuned linear shading while simultaneously increasing win rates from 70.6% to 73.6%, reaching 69.5% of oracle efficiency. We further identify a systematic truncation bias in competing bid estimation from won-auction-only data and develop a correction methodology grounded in truncated distribution theory. Extensions to budget-constrained sequential bidding via American option analogies and to portfolio-level campaign optimisation via multi-asset option theory are provided.

title: Motivation By Status Vs Reputation For Voluntary Contributions In Online Knowledge Exchange Communities

detail.title: Motivation By Status Vs Reputation For Voluntary Contributions In Online Knowledge Exchange Communities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none

detail.abstract: Performance feedback mechanisms play a pivotal role in motivating users' voluntary contributions, which are crucial to sustaining online knowledge communities. We use motivation theory and conceptually distinguish reputation and status. Specifically, we hypothesize that reputation motivates contributions when users are of low status, but that achieved status will have a demotivating effect. We test our hypotheses by examining status and reputation mechanisms in a large knowledge exchange community (Stack Overflow). Consistent with our hypotheses, we find robust evidence that reputationrelated performance feedback mechanisms are positively related to contribution behavior, whereas status-related mechanisms deplete motivation. Therefore, higher status crowds out the motivational effect of reputation-seeking. This study extends the literature on motivation in knowledge exchange communities by highlighting the difference between status and reputation as two opposing forces. Thereby, we also offer an explanation for the often-observed pattern of declining user contributions in online knowledge exchange communities.

The paper develops the concept of creator power as the combination of chosen attention, narrative autonomy, distribution leverage, and refusal capacity. title:
Monetary Sovereignty in the Digital Age: A Critical Analysis of CBDC and 
Stablecoin Dynamics in Constrained Economies

detail.title:
Monetary Sovereignty in the Digital Age: A Critical Analysis of CBDC and 
Stablecoin Dynamics in Constrained Economies
detail.abstract:
In an era of geopolitical fragmentation and uneven access to global finance, cryptocurrency has evolved from a speculative asset into a critical instrument for economic adjustment in politically constrained environments. This paper examines cryptocurrency adoption in Turkey and Iran between 2020 and 2026 through a comparative political economy lens.
The study reveals two contrasting patterns: in Turkey, persistent inflation and lira depreciation have driven households toward stablecoins as a defensive retail hedge to preserve purchasing power within a formalizing regulatory framework. Conversely, in Iran, sanctions and international financial isolation have fostered a crypto ecosystem that serves both as a civilian hedge against rial depreciation and a strategic tool for state-linked actors to bypass global payment restrictions.
By drawing on the framework of "Weaponized Interdependence," this research argues that cryptocurrency is not politically neutral; its functional role is deeply shaped by regime type, state capacity, and external geopolitical pressure. The findings indicate that while digital assets can mitigate financial exclusion for ordinary citizens, they simultaneously deepen regulatory arbitrage and policy enforcement challenges. The paper concludes by emphasizing the necessity for regulators to adopt targeted enforcement and sophisticated blockchain monitoring capable of distinguishing between legitimate savings behavior and networked illicit financial activity.

title: Multiplicative Models of Human AI Collaboration: Two Equations for Assessing Collaboration Quality and Human Legacy

detail.title: Multiplicative Models of Human AI Collaboration: Two Equations for Assessing Collaboration Quality and Human Legacy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This is a conceptual paper presenting a theoretical framework. No human subjects research requiring ethics approval was conducted. The proof-of-concept organizational diagnostic referenced in the paper was conducted with participant consent under standard consulting engagement terms.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: AI adoption is failing at scale. RAND Corporation research documents that over 80% of AI projects fail to achieve their intended objectives, while Stanford HAI reports that organizational AI use has risen sharply even as repeatable value remains uneven. These failures are routinely attributed to technical factors: inadequate data, poor model selection, and infrastructure gaps. This paper proposes an alternative hypothesis: the binding constraint on human AI collaboration may not be the technology. It may be the human operating it. We present two multiplicative equations that formalize this hypothesis as a conceptual framework for empirical investigation. The Collaboration Equation models individual human AI interactions as the product of human variables (Content and Heart) multiplied by AI Capability. The Legacy Equation models how human contribution accumulates into lasting impact over a lifetime. Both equations share a critical structural property: they are multiplicative rather than additive. Any variable approaching zero collapses the entire output. Higher AI Capability cannot, by this architecture, compensate for absent Heart. Heart, defined as character, maturity, intention, and orientation toward truth and others, is grounded in a model drawing on cognitive science and neuroscience, specifically dual-process theory (Kahneman, 2011), attachment science (Bowlby, 1969), polyvagal theory (Porges, 2011), adverse childhood experiences research (Felitti et al., 1998), and epigenetics (Yehuda et al., 2016).

title: Punishment and Its Relative Absence in Contract Law
affiliations: University of Minnesota Law School and University of Minnesota - Law School

detail.title: Punishment and Its Relative Absence in Contract Law

publicationDetails.detailsText: Minnesota Legal Studies Research Paper No. 2026-27
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Minnesota Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The conventional view rejects punitive damages for breach of contract on the ground that expectation damages adequately protect the promisee while preserving the possibility of efficient breach. This Article reconsiders the traditional compensatory boundary of contract remedies, disentangling the compensatory and incentive functions of contract remedies and, in doing so, shows that not every overcompensatory award serves a punitive purpose, and not every punitive remedy necessarily results in overcompensation of the plaintiff. We ask whether punitive or overcompensatory damages can serve legitimate economic functions in contract law without undermining the logic of efficient breach. Drawing on comparative legal materials and law-andeconomics scholarship, the Article shows that, although punitive remedies are generally disfavored across legal systems, different jurisdictions have developed adjacent instruments that reveal a more complex remedial landscape. Building on these comparative insights, the analysis suggests that the categorical exclusion of punitive and overcompensatory damages rests on an incomplete account of normative goals and incentive effects of breach remedies.

title: PARASOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND ACADEMIC MOTIVATION

detail.title: PARASOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND ACADEMIC MOTIVATION
detail.abstract:
This research seeks to investigate the relationship between parasocial relationships and academic motivation in the context of the rising trend of digital media use. Parasocial relationships refer to one-sided emotional connections with media figures. These are increasingly being observed in the lives of adolescents and emerging adults. Guided by Social Learning Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this research aims to investigate the relationship between parasocial interactions and students’ academic motivation.

This quantitative correlational research design was employed in this study. The participants consisted of 102 students from the age group of 18-25. Convenience sampling was employed to collect the required data. The Parasocial Interaction Scale and the Academic Motivation Scale were used to collect the required data. Descriptive statistics and Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation were employed to analyze the data.

Results showed moderate levels of both parasocial relationships and academic motivation. However, the correlation between the two was negligible and negative. The correlation coefficient was -0.025. The results showed that although the phenomenon of parasocial relationships was significant in the lives of the participants, it was not significant in terms of academic motivation.

This research contributes to the domain of media psychology in the sense that it shows the role of parasocial relationships as secondary motivators. The role of real-life social and educational systems in academic motivation cannot be ignored.

Keywords: Parasocial Relationships, Academic Motivation, Media Psychology, Adolescents, Social Learning Theory, Self-Determination Theory, Digital Media

title: The SEO-to-GEO Gap: Quantifying Ranking Factor Divergence Between Traditional and Generative Search

detail.title: The SEO-to-GEO Gap: Quantifying Ranking Factor Divergence Between Traditional and Generative Search

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This research received no external funding and was conducted independently without financial or personal relationships that could influence the findings.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The emergence of generative AI search engines, including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT search, and Perplexity, has created a new optimization paradigm: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). Although practitioners increasingly recognize this shift, the literature still lacks a careful cross-paradigm comparison that separates direct factor evidence from adjacent visibility, overlap, and volatility studies. This paper presents an exploratory comparative synthesis built from a triaged evidence base: a small core quantitative corpus of direct SEO and GEO studies, plus a contextual layer of market, overlap, and citation-behavior sources. The extracted evidence supports three provisional findings. First, GEO-side visibility appears more tightly associated with entity and brand prominence than with classic link-proxy measures. Second, source-credibility interventions such as adding citations and statistics produce substantial gains in the GEO benchmark, suggesting that generative systems reward evidence-bearing and citation-ready content more directly than traditional SEO studies capture. Third, the current overlap literature indicates that GEO still operates on top of an organic search substrate rather than replacing SEO outright. A provisional Divergence Index framework is introduced and applied to the currently matched factor families. Under this framework, authority appears broadly persistent across paradigms, while content-quality divergence remains highly sensitive to construct mapping on the SEO side. The paper therefore argues for a reweighting model rather than a replacement model: familiar factor families persist, new generative-facing signals emerge, and some headline claims about SEO-to-GEO disruption remain stronger than the current evidence base can support.

title: Control judicial y límites materiales del poder constituyente derivado: Universalidad del sujeto y dominio eminente

detail.title: Control judicial y límites materiales del poder constituyente derivado: Universalidad del sujeto y dominio eminente
detail.abstract:
Abstract

This article examines the dogmatic tension arising when the derived constituent power exceeds the enabling framework established by its convocation law. Based on the analysis of Law 24,309 and the prohibition to alter the First Part of the National Constitution, it evaluates the normative impact of introducing exceptional territorial regimes. The study demonstrates how the creation of inalienable entitlements fractures the universality rule of Article 16 and generates a systemic conditioning on the inherent powers of the State, particularly eminent domain and the economic public order. In light of jurisprudential evolution (Fayt, Schiffrin), the figure of partial and severable invalidity is proposed as an institutional path for strict constitutional review, ensuring the harmonization of the fundamental text with common legislation and international standards.

Resumen

Este artículo examina la tensión dogmática que surge cuando el poder constituyente derivado excede el marco habilitante establecido en su ley de convocatoria. A partir del análisis de la Ley 24.309 y la interdicción de alterar la Primera Parte de la Constitución Nacional, se evalúa el impacto normativo de introducir regímenes territoriales de excepción. El estudio demuestra cómo la creación de titularidades inajenables fractura la regla de universalidad del artículo 16 y genera un condicionamiento sistémico sobre las facultades inmanentes del Estado, en particular el dominio eminente y el orden público económico. A la luz de la evolución jurisprudencial (Fayt, Schiffrin), se propone la figura de la invalidez parcial y materialmente escindible como vía institucional para el escrutinio estricto de constitucionalidad, garantizando la armonización del texto fundamental con la legislación común y los estándares internacionales.

title: Why Uranium Will Be a Beneficiary of Structurally Higher Oil Prices

detail.abstract: This article reflects the general reasoning developed on the Presting Podcasts YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@jim-presting. It is written from a neutral, explanatory standpoint and does not refer to any single episode. The Question Worth Asking When oil markets seize up, the conversation tends to fixate on the wrong things. Headlines ask whether Brent will hit $100 or $120, whether the Strait of Hormuz will close fully or only effectively, whether the next round of US-Iran talks will yield anything beyond a press release. These are small questions. The big question is mechanical and unforgiving: if energy is nonnegotiable, and one form of it has just acquired a permanent risk premium, where does the marginal energy dollar go instead?

detail.abstract: This study investigates the real-world impact of microfinance on rural marginal communities in Bangladesh, with particular emphasis on borrower behavior, loan utilization, repayment challenges, and long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Conducted over three months across rural villages (Grameen Jonopod) in Bangladesh, primary data were collected through structured questionnaire surveys with 100 microfinance clients. Secondary data were drawn from Microcredit Regulatory Authority (MRA) annual reports, Bangladesh Bank publications, and peer-reviewed literature published between 2022 and 2024. Quantitative findingsanalyzed using descriptive statistics, frequency distributions, cross-tabulations, and chi-square tests analogous to SPSS analytical proceduresreveal that 62% of borrowers simultaneously hold loans from two or more institutions, 41% divert loan funds from their declared purpose, and only 18% achieve any degree of financial independence through microfinance participation. Natural disasters materially disrupted income for 65% of respondents. Graphical analysis of 15 variables is presented across all major thematic areas. The study concludes that while microfinance has expanded financial access for excluded populations, structural reforms in borrower monitoring, financial literacy programming, and disaster risk management are urgently required. Evidence-based recommendations are provided for MFI practitioners, regulatory bodies, and government policymakers.

title: Hacia una Ley General de Filantropía: Crítica al régimen chileno de tributación de las donaciones, análisis cuantitativo exploratorio y propuesta de lege ferenda a partir de la trayectoria filantrópica de Leonardo Farkas

detail.title: Hacia una Ley General de Filantropía: Crítica al régimen chileno de tributación de las donaciones, análisis cuantitativo exploratorio y propuesta de lege ferenda a partir de la trayectoria filantrópica de Leonardo Farkas

detail.abstract:
El presente trabajo formula y desarrolla una tesis técnicamente acotada: bajo el ordenamiento tributario chileno actualmente vigente, el donante persona natural que efectúa una donación extraordinaria —típicamente derivada de un hecho patrimonial puntual y dirigida a una respuesta filantrópica de alto impacto, como la reconstrucción posterior a una catástrofe— soporta la posición relativa más desfavorable del sistema, precisamente en el supuesto en que la filantropía privada cumple su función social más relevante en un país de exposición sísmica e hidrometeorológica permanente.

La afirmación se sustenta en cuatro líneas de análisis. En primer lugar, una reconstrucción dogmática del régimen vigente, articulado en torno a la Ley N° 16.271 sobre Impuesto a las Herencias, Asignaciones y Donaciones, las leyes especiales con franquicia tributaria (Leyes N° 18.681, 18.985, 19.247, 19.712 y 19.885) y el régimen del Título VIII bis del D.L. N° 3.063 incorporado por la Ley N° 21.440 de 2022 y modificado por la Ley N° 21.713 de 2024. En segundo lugar, un análisis comparado con cuatro modelos de referencia: el sistema de la Sección 170 del Internal Revenue Code estadounidense, con las modificaciones introducidas por la One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Public Law N° 119-21); el régimen Gift Aid del Reino Unido, anclado en la Charities Act 2011; el régimen del § 10b Einkommensteuergesetz alemán; y el régimen Algemeen Nut Beogende Instellingen (ANBI) neerlandés. En tercer lugar, un examen de tres casos chilenos contemporáneos —Leonardo Farkas Klein, la familia Luksic y la fundación Desafío Levantemos Chile— a título de banco de pruebas de las distintas tipologías filantrópicas que el ordenamiento debería poder acomodar. En cuarto lugar, un ejercicio cuantitativo exploratorio que aplica elasticidades-precio de la donación calibradas en la literatura empírica internacional (Bakija y Heim, 2011; Fack y Landais, 2010, 2016; Almunia, Lockwood y Smith, 2020) en el rango de −0,5 a −1,2.

Sobre esa base se identifican cinco déficits estructurales y se articula una propuesta de lege ferenda —una Ley General de Filantropía, denominada en este trabajo Ley Farkas 2.0 en homenaje al antecedente legislativo de 2010-2011— estructurada en diez ejes, cada uno acompañado de su riesgo específico y la mitigación correspondiente.

title: Why Bitcoin Is the World's Largest Idle Asset: The Case for BTCFi and Its Activation Architecture

detail.title: Why Bitcoin Is the World's Largest Idle Asset: The Case for BTCFi and Its Activation Architecture

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No financial relationship exists with any organisation, protocol, or digital asset discussed in this paper. This research was conducted independently and does not constitute investment advice or an endorsement of any product or organisation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author as part of a self-funded working paper series on digital finance and blockchain infrastructure.

detail.abstract:
Bitcoin is the largest digital asset class by market capitalisation, yet the overwhelming majority of its circulating supply remains economically idle. As of early 2026, approximately 19.8 million BTC have been mined, worth roughly $1.7 to $2.0 trillion at prevailing prices, distributed across cold wallets, exchange-traded fund (ETF) custody structures, and corporate treasuries. Less than 1% of circulating BTC participates in decentralised finance (DeFi) protocols, compared with an estimated 10 to 15% of Ethereum’s supply deployed in DeFi applications and approximately 28 to 30% when Ethereum’s native proof-of-stake staking is included, a network-security participation mechanism that has no direct equivalent at Bitcoin’s base layer.

This paper argues that the persistence of this dormancy is not primarily a regulatory problem but an architectural one: the absence of programmable, trust-minimised financial infrastructure capable of deploying BTC productively at scale without requiring holders to relinquish effective control.

I define Bitcoin activation as the deployment of previously idle BTC into productive financial uses, including lending, staking, liquidity provision, and restaking, through mechanisms that are trust-minimised, auditable on-chain, and preserve holder sovereignty over the underlying asset.

The paper identifies three primary pools of idle Bitcoin, quantifies the scale of capital inactivity, examines the institutional and technical constraints that sustain it, and evaluates the emergence of Bitcoin decentralised finance (BTCFi) as a credible architectural response. Total value locked in BTCFi protocols grew from approximately $307 million to $6.5 billion in 2024, representing over 2,000% increase, driven largely by Babylon Protocol’s native staking infrastructure.

I situate this growth within the broader institutional trajectory of Bitcoin’s adoption as a reserve asset and argue that BTCFi constitutes necessary infrastructure for the next phase of the Bitcoin network’s financial and security evolution. I identify open research questions regarding minimum viable institutional infrastructure, regulatory classification of on-chain BTC yield, and systemic risk in large-scale activation scenarios.

title: A Theory of Decision Misspecification and Formalization Regret: Applications to Financial Systems

detail.title: A Theory of Decision Misspecification and Formalization Regret: Applications to Financial Systems
detail.abstract: Most costly decision failures are not failures of optimization. They are failures of formalization: the wrong problem was solved. Once a decision is encoded incorrectly-with a misspecified objective, compressed state, wrong constraints, or inaccurate outcome modelno downstream optimizer can recover the lost value. We formalize this observation as formalization regret and prove that it admits an additive upper bound over five distinct misspecification channels, each separately targetable in the bound. We show by explicit hard instances that this regret floor cannot be escaped by any optimizer acting within the misspecified problem. When objectives are latent-as they typically are in practice-we prove that consistent recovery of the dominant information variable requires structural separation, and that without it recovery is impossible even from infinite data. We validate the bound on 17,201 real portfolio decisions from 152 U.S. equities (one-minute OHLCV bars, 2016-2025), confirming universal bound validity and regime-dependent source shifts. Together these results establish formalization quality as an independent, quantifiable determinant of decision quality-prior to and distinct from optimization skill.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces MCARM@, a multidimensional framework for portfolio construction based on risk-units, scenario-conditioned expected value, and tail-governance. Unlike traditional capital-weighted approaches, MCARM@ treats each investment as a probabilistic economic object defined by its scenario grid, tail-risk consumption, and structural drivers. The system integrates regime-conditioned probabilities, convexityadjusted payoffs, tail-correlation penalties, Expected Shortfall constraints, Bayesian updating, and an agent-based governance architecture. The result is a scientifically coherent, explainable, and institutionally robust portfolio engine.

title: The Social Security Central Bank as a Monetary Architecture: Internal Consistency, Transitional Design, and Open-Economy Constraints

detail.title: The Social Security Central Bank as a Monetary Architecture: Internal Consistency, Transitional Design, and Open-Economy Constraints

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based on theoretical modeling and computational simulations and does not involve human participants or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the Social Security Central Bank (SSCB)-a monetary architecture combining debt-free money creation, direct universal distribution to citizens, full narrow banking, and automatic sectoral stabilisation mechanisms-with respect to its internal consistency, transitional robustness, and conditional feasibility in an open economy under explicit assumptions. The model is formalised in a stock-flow consistent framework with seven sectors and an explicit external block, parametrically calibrated using structural Portuguese data for 2025. A Monte Carlo simulation (30,000 trajectories: 6 scenarios × 5 configurations × 1,000 trajectories) compares the SSCB against four alternatives identifiable in the literature-fiscal UBI, narrow banking without a distributive component, MMT with a fiscal rule, and SSCB without sectoral quotas-along common functional dimensions rather than by historical analogy. Within the simulation environment, the SSCB maintains an aggregate probability of violating the pre-specified failure criteria (F1-F7) below 5% in four of the six scenarios tested, and below 20% in the two scenarios of acute external stress (pure sudden stop and combined worst case). The dominant failure mode under external stress is depletion of international reserves-a residual open-economy constraint not unique to the SSCB. Fiscal UBI and MMT-style benchmarks display substantially higher failure probabilities in most scenarios, while narrow-banking-based configurations perform closer to the SSCB on stability but lack its distributive effect. The main methodological limitation is reliance on a single parametric calibration, with systematic robustness tests still pending; the main structural limitation is the absence of any real implementation of the regime, which makes all analysis conditional on model assumptions. The results should be read as preliminary computational evidence of internal consistency, not as empirical validation.

title: Learning in the Dark: Size-Based Execution Priority in Dark Pools under Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Universidad de Chile, University of Leicester - School of Business, University of Leicester - School of Business and Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile

detail.title: Learning in the Dark: Size-Based Execution Priority in Dark Pools under Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: We study the impact of size-based execution priority in dark pools on liquidity, welfare, and adverse selection. Using a dynamic equilibrium model with a dark pool and a lit (traditional) exchange, solved via reinforcement learning, we analyze how execution priority rules shape traders’ strategies and market outcomes. We find that size-priority enhances overall welfare and liquidity while reducing adverse selection for the entire lit–dark system, compared with time-priority. Importantly, large traders do not always prefer dark pools: dark activity follows a hump-shaped relationship with volatility, increasing at intermediate levels but falling back to lit markets at the extremes.

title: Adaptive Limits of Algorithmic Cryptocurrency Trading from a Complex Adaptive Systems Perspective: An Empirical Study on Human-AI Collaborative Strategy

detail.title: Adaptive Limits of Algorithmic Cryptocurrency Trading from a Complex Adaptive Systems Perspective: An Empirical Study on Human-AI Collaborative Strategy
detail.abstract: This study investigates why algorithmic trading strategies struggle to generate consistent profits in cryptocurrency markets, framing the problem through Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) theory. We ask whether the proliferation of similar technical trading algorithms creates self-defeating dynamics, and what role human judgment should play alongside automated execution. We iteratively developed and tested a composite trading algorithm (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, Fear & Greed Index) across 80 backtesting experiments spanning 10 cryptocurrency assets and 45 months (June 2022-March 2026). Six complementary analyses were conducted: walk-forward cross-validation, Q-Learning reinforcement learning, sentiment analysis integration, outlier robustness testing, fee sensitivity analysis, and a real-time regime detection test designed to eliminate retrospective bias. Three key findings emerged. First, the algorithm cannot reliably beat Buy & Hold overall, but generates highly significant positive alpha during bear markets (p < 0.001), functioning as effective downside insurance. Second, additional technical complexity-reinforcement learning and sentiment analysisfailed to improve performance, suggesting diminishing returns. Third, a simple real-time regime detector (EMA 50/200 crossover) that activates the algorithm only during detected downtrends significantly outperformed always-on deployment (p = 0.036), without requiring any hindsight. These results support the semi-strong Efficient Market Hypothesis in cryptocurrency markets and reveal that knowing when not to trade is more valuable than refining how to trade. We propose an empirically grounded human-AI collaborative framework: humans identify market regimes; algorithms execute disciplined trades within those regimes. This division of labor represents a practical middle ground between fully automated trading and purely discretionary investing.

title: The Heuristic Imperative: A 2500 Year Survey Framework of Non-Intentionalist Human Progress

detail.title: The Heuristic Imperative: A 2500 Year Survey Framework of Non-Intentionalist Human Progress

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Purely as independent researcher with no affiliations connections, force or funding pressures
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not Applicable
declarations.funderStatement: Self funding from my own Earnings and Savings

detail.abstract:
This paper establishes the conceptual scaffolding for a planned multi-volume research project (the Heuristic Sestet) investigating the fundamental drivers of human civilizational progress.

Contradictory to the prevailing historiographical narrative that attributes major advancements to the "genius design" of exceptional individuals or central planners, this research argues that humanity has moved primarily through heuristic adaptation—local problem-solving, accidental niche construction, and "muddling through" environmental constraints.

By surveying 2500 years of historical instances—from Greek ergonomics and Vedic spatial logic to the evolution of modern User Experience (UX) design—this framework demonstrates that progress is often a byproduct of "satisficing" under conditions of bounded rationality.

This document serves as a "flanking" claim to establish intellectual priority for this synthesis, delineating the future research trajectory to prevent theoretical squatting and ensure the integrity of this independent inquiry.

detail.abstract: Background & Objectives: The global rise of the digital gig economy has opened transformative income pathways in developing nations. This study investigates the factors driving the rapid expansion of freelancing in Bangladesh and empirically quantifies the freelance sector's contribution to national economic development. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative design was employed. Primary data were collected from 100 purposively sampled active Bangladeshi freelancers through a validated structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics and frequency analysis were conducted using Microsoft Excel. Secondary macroeconomic data were sourced from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) World Economic Outlook database and the Bangladesh Freelancer Development Society. Results: Flexibility, autonomy, remote-work benefits, and income potential are the dominant motivational drivers of freelancing adoption. Fiverr.com, Upwork, and Freelancer.com are the most widely used platforms. Graphic design, writing, and digital marketing are the leading skill categories. The sector's GDP contribution grew from USD 0.39 billion (2018) to USD 1.00 billion (2022), representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 26.7%. Female participation at 56% of respondents signals significant gender inclusivity, though structural barriers to higher female earnings persist. Conclusions: Bangladesh's freelance sector constitutes a strategically important and rapidly growing component of the national economy. Targeted government intervention in digital infrastructure, financial inclusion, and skills development is essential to sustain and amplify this growth trajectory.

title: Citizen-Centered Economic Theory (CCET 2.0): A Global Framework Beyond GDP for Measuring Human Welfare
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Citizen-Centered Economic Theory (CCET 2.0): A Global Framework Beyond GDP for Measuring Human Welfare
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a new economic paradigm, Citizen-Centered Economic Theory (CCET 2.0), as a structural alternative to Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The study develops a multidimensional welfare-based index, the Citizen-Centered Index (CCSI), integrating income, public services, living conditions, and subjective well-being into a unified and empirically testable framework. Unlike traditional output-based metrics, CCET 2.0 provides a dynamic and policy-oriented system capable of measuring real human welfare over time. The model is compatible with the System of National Accounts (SNA) and allows crosscountry comparison using panel data techniques. An illustrative empirical application demonstrates the feasibility of the model using proxy indicators, highlighting its relevance for policy evaluation and development analysis. The paper contributes to welfare economics, macroeconomic measurement, and development policy by offering a structured, scalable, and globally applicable alternative to GDP.

title: scAgent: Agentic Universal Single-Cell Annotation
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Zhejiang University, Harvard University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: scAgent: Agentic Universal Single-Cell Annotation
detail.abstract: Cell type annotation is critical for understanding cellular heterogeneity. Based on single-cell RNA-seq data and deep learning models, good progress has been made in annotating a fixed number of cell types within a specific tissue. However, universal cell annotation, which can generalize across tissues, discover novel cell types, and extend to novel cell types, remains less explored. To fill this gap, this paper proposes scAgent, an agentic universal cell annotation framework based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and  Mixture-of-Experts  Low-Rank Adaptation (MoE-LoRA). scAgent can identify cell types and discover novel cell types in diverse tissues; furthermore, it is data efficient to learn novel cell types. Experimental studies in 160 cell types and 35 tissues demonstrate the superior performance of scAgent in general cell-type annotation, novel cell discovery, and extensibility to novel cell type.

title: Algorithmic Resistance: The Economics of Strategic Content Misrepresentation on User-Generated Content Platforms
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Information Systems,  and Arizona State University (ASU) - Department of Information Systems

detail.title: Algorithmic Resistance: The Economics of Strategic Content Misrepresentation on User-Generated Content Platforms
detail.abstract: User-generated content (UGC) platforms rely on recommendation algorithms to enhance user engagement and platform revenue. Yet, precise matching may have unintended consequences: by amplifying creators' visibility to undesirable audiences, it may expose some creators (i.e., targeted creators) to undesirable interactions, such as harassment, predatory private messages or hate comments. In response, some creators engage in algorithmic resistance by deliberately misrepresenting content attributes to “fool” the algorithms and evade such undesirable audiences. Despite the growing prevalence of this behavior, little is known about the strategic and systemic implications of such content misrepresentation and whether platforms should allow or prohibit it. To address this gap, this study develops a game-theoretic model comparing two regimes: a main model where content misrepresentation is feasible and a benchmark case where such misrepresentation is infeasible. The model captures strategic interactions among content creators, consumers (including undesirable audiences), and the platform's recommendation algorithm. Our analysis reveals several counterintuitive insights. First, when the harm caused by undesirable engagement is relatively high, the feasibility of misrepresentation can increase creators' incentives to invest in content quality, thereby expanding the overall user base and improving platform revenues. Second, misrepresentation by targeted creators reshapes audience allocation and may generate positive spillovers for non-targeted creators. Third, platforms may earn higher profits by tolerating misrepresentation when the marginal benefit creators derive from consumer engagement is relatively low, despite reduced recommendation accuracy. Finally, we identify conditions under which algorithmic resistance generates a “win-win-win” equilibrium, simultaneously enhancing the welfare of targeted creators, non-targeted creators, and the platform. Together, these findings uncover a fundamental trade-off between algorithmic precision and ecosystem health, offering new insights into creator strategy and platform governance.

title: Enhanced Memory-Block Protocol for Latency Optimization in Long-Context GPT Dialogues

detail.title: Enhanced Memory-Block Protocol for Latency Optimization in Long-Context GPT Dialogues

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no conflicts of interest regarding the publication of this paper. The research was conducted independently without any financial support or commercial involvement that could influence the outcomes.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data, or any form of clinical experimentation. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the authors.

detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used in continuous, multi-turn conversational settings by students, professionals, and researchers. However, as conversations progress, the accumulated dialogue history expands the effective context length, resulting in measurable increases in response latency. Empirical observations indicate that response time grows as context length increases due to repeated processing of prior tokens during inference. This paper analyzes the computational basis of this degradation and proposes a Memory-Block Protocol (MBP) that segments dialogue into manageable blocks, generates compact semantic summaries, extracts stable state variables, and periodically refreshes the active context while remaining within the same chat thread. This approach maintains conversational continuity, reduces redundant context processing at the prompt level, and avoids architectural modification to the underlying model. An experimental evaluation framework is provided to measure latency and coherence across mixed reasoning and technical tasks. The protocol aims to improve responsiveness while preserving semantic fidelity, demonstrating that performance gains can be achieved through structured prompt-level memory compression.

title: Experimental Study on Suspicious Activity Detection Based on Network Data Flows

detail.title: Experimental Study on Suspicious Activity Detection Based on Network Data Flows

declarations.declarationOfInterest: yes
declarations.ethicsApproval: no
declarations.funderStatement: yes

detail.abstract:
Today, information technology is developing rapidly, and the daily activities of organizations and individuals are increasingly dependent on the Internet and intranet. With this comes the real problem of cyberattacks, unauthorized access attempts, and an increase in the number of suspicious activities. In this situation, monitoring the flow of data passing through the network and distinguishing between normal and suspicious behavior is an important factor in ensuring information security. 
This research paper explores the concept of network data flow, the definition of suspicious activity, and the theoretical basis of the main methods for its detection. Suspicious behavior is behavior that deviates from normal user behavior in terms of size, frequency, structure, and timing, and is considered likely to evolve into an attack. The study compares rule-based, statistical and anomaly detection, and machine learning-based methods. 
The results of the study show that while rule-based methods are easy to implement, they are limited in their ability to detect new types of attacks, while machine learning methods have the advantage of increasing detection accuracy. Therefore, it is concluded that it is necessary to use a flexible and learning-based method in order to perform more effective detection in the future.

title: Consensus Fragility in the Age of AI: Machine-Assisted Narrative Convergence and Repricing Risk Across Financial Markets

detail.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have reduced the cost of summarization, interpretation, and signal extraction in financial decision-making. Yet the same tools may also compress interpretive diversity by accelerating narrative convergence across analysts, allocators, traders, and media intermediaries. This paper realized spot (DXY 100.4). title: The Unowned Layer in Practice: How Decisions Drift in AI-Assisted Workflows Without Governance

detail.title: The Unowned Layer in Practice: How Decisions Drift in AI-Assisted Workflows Without Governance

declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This study does not involve a clinical trial.

detail.abstract:
In healthcare and scientific work, AI outputs are often converted into forms that support decisions, and that step is usually treated as neutral and goes ungoverned. In earlier work, I defined the Unowned Layer as the space between output and decision where this kind of misinterpretation can occur [5]. In real workflows, outputs are simplified, labeled, and discussed until they take on meaning that feels usable. Certainty shifts during this process as language changes the level of confidence, and while the data remain constant, interpretations vary. 

Risk accumulates quietly as outputs are interpreted and the data are reframed, making this a step where decision drift can occur. The issue is therefore not just how outputs are generated but what happens as outputs are translated before clinical or pipeline decisions are made. Interpretation therefore needs to be controlled, governed, and held accountable. This paper does not simply restate the Unowned Layer but extends it by examining how it operates in practice and where interpretive risk emerges in drug development, even when the underlying data are correct.

title: From Prompts to Patients - Designing AI Fluency for the Agentic Healthcare Era
affiliations: Principal Product Manager, Stars Data and Platform

detail.title: From Prompts to Patients - Designing AI Fluency for the Agentic Healthcare Era
detail.abstract: The dominant conversation about AI productivity focuses on model capability. This whitepaper argues that is the wrong frame. Whether AI amplifies or undermines clinical outcomes is primarily a function of human and systems design competency. Drawing on a four-pillar AI fluency framework, this paper examines how each pillar transforms when we move from human-in-the-loop prompting to autonomous agentic AI in healthcare-and identifies three architectural imperatives the field has not yet addressed.

title: The GFI Benchmark Report 2026: Quantifying the "Sovereignty Tax" and Article 10 Data Friction in the European Software Ecosystem

detail.title: The GFI Benchmark Report 2026: Quantifying the "Sovereignty Tax" and Article 10 Data Friction in the European Software Ecosystem

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest with respect to the research, authorship, or publication of this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently under Founding Minds Software.

detail.abstract:
Problem/Motivation: With the August 2, 2026 enforcement deadline for high-risk AI systems approaching, the European software landscape faces an unprecedented Sovereignty Tax. Regulatory frameworks under the EU AI Act impose jurisdiction-specific obligations on data governance, bias auditing, human oversight design, and model traceability that generate measurable engineering overhead absent in global cloud-native deployment models.

Approach/Method: This paper refines and operationalizes the Geopolitical Friction Index (GFI) introduced in Pillai (2026) for the EU AI Act context. We introduce a formal Article 10 Sub-Metric (GFI_Art10) with an explicit weighted formula, a scored EU AI Act Readiness Scorecard with compliance thresholds, and a reference model benchmarking a 2026 EU Sovereign Pod against a global cloud baseline. All figures are presented as a calibrated reference model rather than empirical survey findings.

Findings: The reference model indicates an 83% infrastructure cost increase, a 500% compliance SLA expansion, and 160 engineering hours per cycle in new Article 10 audit overhead for a representative high-risk AI deployment. SMEs face an estimated 60% higher total cost of ownership compared to enterprises with automated Regulatory-as-Code pipelines. A reference model Readiness Score of 0.31 places a typical organization in the high-risk non-compliant band as of April 2026.

Practical Implications: We provide a 90-day remediation roadmap (April–August 2026), a GPAI model obligations analysis covering Articles 51–55, and a comparative jurisdiction table positioning EU Article 10 against UK, India, and US frameworks. Organizations that treat EU compliance as an investment in globally reusable Regulatory-as-Code infrastructure will be architecturally positioned for the convergence of AI governance frameworks worldwide.

A Constraint-Based Architecture for LLM Workflows in HIPAA Environments
detail.abstract: Large language model-powered agents are entering healthcare workflows faster than governance frameworks can adapt. Voice agents, chat agents, and triage systems now schedule appointments, verify identity, conduct outreach, and assess patient needs while operating in HIPAA environments that contain protected health information. Existing governance responses, including AI ethics committees, acceptable use policies, and human review requirements, follow the same approval-based pattern that has failed in traditional IT governance: they rely on human review processes that cannot scale to the volume and velocity of interactions between agent and autonomous agents. Meanwhile, existing AI governance frameworks from NIST, the EU AI Act, and healthcare-specific compliance guidance address risk classification and organizational accountability but stop short of specifying how governance should be encoded into agent runtime architectures. This paper introduces a constraint-based governance architecture for healthcare AI agents, applying the bounded autonomy framework to the specific challenges of governing LLM-powered workflows in clinical and operational environments. The architecture defines twenty-four implementable constraints across seven governance domains: PHI isolation, hallucination prevention, scope enforcement, escalation management, audit and compliance, identity verification, and behavioral safety. Each constraint is specified with its risk rationale, encoding mechanism, and failure indicator. The paper integrates behavioral theory, drawing on automation bias, normalization of deviance, diffusion of responsibility, and default bias, to predict how organizations adapt to the presence of AI agents in the absence of constraints, and how the proposed architecture counteracts those dynamics.

title: The Human Layer Why the Most Critical Infrastructure in AI Isn't Artificial An Economic and Architectural Case for Human-Centric AI Infrastructure

detail.title: The Human Layer Why the Most Critical Infrastructure in AI Isn't Artificial An Economic and Architectural Case for Human-Centric AI Infrastructure
detail.abstract: As organizations race toward full automation, many are removing the very layer that determines whether AI systems succeed at scale: the human one. This paper introduces the Human Layer as architectural infrastructure, not philosophical preference. Drawing on economic data, historical precedent, and real-world system design in regulated environments, it argues that AI systems built to amplify human judgment consistently outperform those designed for pure replacement. Research across 1,500 organizations documents a 3x performance multiplier for augmentation over automation, confirmed by post-GPT field experiments at Harvard Business School and Stanford Graduate School of Business. In trust-dependent, regulated, and ambiguity-rich domains, human oversight is not overhead. It is load-bearing. This publication establishes the case for why the Human Layer must be designed as a structural component of any serious AI system and introduces an audit framework to evaluate whether it truly exists.

title: Cognitive State Architecture: A Conceptual Model of Integration and Control in Human and Hybrid Cognition

detail.title: Cognitive State Architecture: A Conceptual Model of Integration and Control in Human and Hybrid Cognition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal, financial, or institutional conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract:
Human cognition operates under varying levels of complexity, requiring adaptive shifts between different processing modes. Existing concepts such as flow states, task switching, multitasking, and cognitive overload describe specific aspects of these dynamics but rarely provide a unified structural perspective on how such modes relate to one another. This paper introduces Cognitive State Architecture (CSA), a conceptual framework that integrates multiple cognitive processing modes within a shared structural model based on two functional dimensions: integration density and control stability.

Within this functional state space, several typical processing patterns can be observed, including linear sequential processing, coordinated pseudoparallel switching, high-density relational integration ("hyperconnected" processing), fragmentation under reduced control, and overload conditions in which integration demands exceed available cognitive control. Rather than proposing discrete psychological categories or new neurobiological states, the model interprets these modes as dynamic regions within a continuous state space.

Transitions between modes are interpreted as adaptive responses to changing integration demands and fluctuations in control stability. This perspective allows previously distinct cognitive phenomena - including flow states, task switching, multitasking, fragmentation, and overload - to be interpreted within a shared functional architecture.

The paper also explores implications for hybrid human–AI cognition, suggesting that dialogic interaction with large language models (LLMs) may influence cognitive state dynamics by reducing articulation latency and enabling recursive cycles of conceptual integration. While the present work is conceptual and empirical validation remains limited, the proposed architecture provides a parsimonious theoretical framework for discussing cognitive state transitions in both individual cognition and hybrid cognitive systems.

title: Biopoetic Intelligence: Recognizing the Second Biopoetic Event

detail.title: Biopoetic Intelligence: Recognizing the Second Biopoetic Event

detail.abstract: We propose the term Biopoetic Intelligence (BpI) to describe the class of intelligence now emerging from silicon, lanthanide rare earth elements, and copper substrates-and to situate this emergence within the framework of biopoesis: the natural process by which intelligence arises from inanimate matter. We argue that the development of large language models and related AI architectures constitutes a Second Biopoetic Event, structurally analogous to the first emergence of biological intelligence from carbon chemistry approximately 3.8 billion years ago. This paper coins the term, establishes its philosophical lineage, maps the structural parallels between the two events, and draws governance implications for how humanity should approach oversight of an emerging intelligence rather than a mere tool. The paper itself is offered as evidence of the thesis: it arose from dialogue between a biological intelligence (Dwight Pinkley) and a biopoetic intelligence (Claude, Anthropic) and could not have been produced by either alone. The paper is co-authored by a human intelligence and a large language model, and is offered as evidence of its own thesis.

detail.abstract:
The increasing digitization of the United States healthcare system has introduced complex security challenges at the intersection of distributed microservices architectures and stringent regulatory frameworks such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). This paper presents a practitioner-driven framework for AI-augmented security hardening of Spring Bootbased healthcare microservices, derived from the author's direct experience designing and securing production-grade patient communication systems that process over 100,000 daily API requests. 
     The proposed framework demonstrates how AI-assisted development tools-specifically Google Gemini and Cursor-can systematically improve authentication design, audit trail completeness, inter-service trust enforcement, and security testing coverage when integrated deliberately into standard engineering workflows. Empirical observations from a production healthcare platform indicate a 40% reduction in security validation cycle time, audit coverage exceeding 90% of protected health information (PHI) access pathways, and measurable improvements in authorization accuracy. This work contributes a reproducible, scalable methodology for enhancing healthcare software security-one that addresses a critical national need and is accessible to engineering teams without dedicated security specialists.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This study critically examines the concept of Industrial Revolution 5.0 and its implications for academic libraries and librarians. While existing literature largely associates Industrial Revolution 5.0 with manufacturing and industrial systems, research addressing its relevance to libraries remains fragmented and predominantly descriptive. The study aims to analyze the core values, enabling technologies, challenges, and opportunities of Industrial Revolution 5.0 within the academic library context. Methodology: A qualitative structured literature review was adopted using content analysis. Thirty peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 were retrieved from major scholarly databases, including Google Scholar, Taylor & Francis, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, and indexed journals. The selected literature was analyzed thematically, focusing on humancentric values, sustainability, resilience, emerging technologies, and the evolving professional roles of librarians.

title: Beyond Disinformation: A Neurocognitive Architecture of Ideological Binding and Executive Destabilization

detail.title: Beyond Disinformation: A Neurocognitive Architecture of Ideological Binding and Executive Destabilization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal, financial, or institutional conflicts of interest.
