publicationDetails.detailsText: Chapter 9, In: A.K. Ghosh (ed.), Status of Environment of West Bengal: A Citizens' Report. ENDEV. Kolkata (2008)

detail.abstract: Sacred groves and sacred ponds constitute one of the traditional institutions for conservation of biodiversity, protected by the local animistic culture. Consecrated by a local deity or ancestral spirit, sacred groves and ponds of West Bengal are the last habitats of many rare and endangered life forms, some of which have been documented by the author in the southwestern districts of Bengal. With the advent of industrial modernisation, many of these ancient sacred habitats are rapidly disappearing. Most of the biodiversity in these habitats is threatened by the erosion of older belief systems, the replacement of the cultural value with the commercial value of biodiversity (e.g., trees of the grove and fish of the ponds), and urban-industrial encroachments into these habitats, as documented in this chapter.

title: The Mathematics of Slippage: When Latency Arbitrage Stops Paying

detail.title: The Mathematics of Slippage: When Latency Arbitrage Stops Paying
detail.abstract: Latency arbitrage in over-the-counter foreign exchange has been a profitable retail and small institutional strategy for over two decades. Its profitability rests on three measurable quantities: the trader's latency edge 𝜀 relative to a slower counterparty, the volatility of the price process between signal and execution, and the cost structure imposed by the broker. We formalize the relationship between these quantities and derive a closed-form break-even condition for the strategy. We then extend the model to 𝑁 competing latency arbitrageurs and show that the equilibrium dispersion of latencies determines the long-run profit margin available to any individual participant. Calibrating to retail EUR/USD tick data for 2025-2026, the break-even latency floor 𝜏 * sits in the 5-25 millisecond range depending on volatility regime, and the addition of a fourth competitor at equal latency reduces individual expected profit by approximately 75% relative to the monopoly case under our baseline calibration. The paper also discusses how broker-side execution adjustments-the anti-arbitrage plugin family-interact with the model and shift the effective break-even latency upward by roughly 50% in typical retail conditions. We conclude with practical implications and open research questions.

title: The $1.27 Lecture: How Tip-Chasing and Cold Pizza Destroyed 30 Years of Brand Loyalty

detail.title: The $1.27 Lecture: How Tip-Chasing and Cold Pizza Destroyed 30 Years of Brand Loyalty
detail.abstract: This paper examines how branded in-house delivery models in franchise pizza chains systematically generate worker-customer conflict. Drawing on a detailed real-world customer case study, it analyses an incident in which a long-term loyal customer paid a substantial delivery fee plus a standard 10% tip, only to endure a 10-minute aggressive tip lecture from an in-house driver, cold food, and a condescending moral inversion. The firm's decision to retain in-house drivers-publicly justified as delivering superior "personal service" and brand consistencyfunctions primarily as a margin-extraction strategy. By fully internalizing the delivery fee while externalizing labor costs, vehicle expenses, and income volatility onto drivers, the model creates direct and unbuffered brand liability. Unlike outsourced third-party platforms, in-house delivery transfers reputational damage straight to the franchise, accelerating the erosion of decades-long customer loyalty. The paper develops a behavioral labor-economics model integrating incomplete contracts, cost externalization, loss aversion, and reciprocity norms. It explores broader implications for franchise operations, brand equity, and the gigification of traditional service jobs in Canada.

title: Natives' internal migration in Switzerland: A reaction to immigrants' presence?
affiliations: , Université de Lille and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Natives' internal migration in Switzerland: A reaction to immigrants' presence?
detail.abstract: This article investigates whether native residents adjust their internal migration behavior in response to the presence of immigrants in their place of origin and in surrounding areas, and whether ethnic diversity at potential destinations also shapes their relocation choices. The analysis is based on Swiss register-based data (STATPOP) covering the period 2011-2019. In order to address both incomplete information on local contexts at the time of migration and substantial cantonal heterogeneity in Switzerland, we estimate a nested multinomial logit model. Migration is conceptualized as a hierarchical decision-making process. First, agents decide whether to move or not. Then, they sequentially determine a destination canton, and a municipality within that canton. Our results confirm the nested structure of native internal migration decision and show that responses to immigration vary by geographic scale, immigrant origin, type (established stocks versus recent inflows), and by stage of the migration decision. At the municipal level, consistent with intergroup contact theory, higher local immigrant stocks are associated with reduced native out-migration, whereas greater concentrations in broader employment areas increase mobility-particularly in response to culturally distant immigrant groups, reflecting perceived competition or social distance. Conditional on canton choice, natives are attracted to municipalities with greater ethnic diversity but avoid at the same time municipalities located in high-immigrant employment areas, highlighting persistent macro-level sensitivities. Overall, our findings reveal a cumulative, spatially stratified logic of native internal migration: natives exhibit microlevel attraction to ethnic diversity in some cases but demonstrate near-systematic macro-level avoidance of immigrants. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that these results are largely robust, with some nuances: intercantonal movers and men are slightly more sensitive to immigrant presence, while older individuals respond more strongly to nearby immigrants but less to distant immigrant concentrations.

title: Ekonomi Gig dan Transformasi Masa Depan Pekerjaan: Analisis Naratif terhadap Dinamika Global, Ketidaktentuan Pekerjaan, dan Cabaran Tenaga Kerja di Sabah, Malaysia

detail.title: Ekonomi Gig dan Transformasi Masa Depan Pekerjaan: Analisis Naratif terhadap Dinamika Global, Ketidaktentuan Pekerjaan, dan Cabaran Tenaga Kerja di Sabah, Malaysia
detail.abstract:
Perkembangan ekonomi gig telah mengubah secara signifikan landskap pekerjaan global dengan memperkenalkan model kerja fleksibel yang dimediasi oleh platform digital, sekali gus mencabar struktur pekerjaan tradisional dan mekanisme perlindungan buruh sedia ada. Transformasi ini bukan sahaja melibatkan perubahan teknikal dalam organisasi kerja, malah mencetuskan ketidaktentuan pekerjaan serta redefinisi hubungan antara pekerja dan majikan dalam ekosistem ekonomi digital. Artikel ulasan naratif ini bertujuan untuk menyintesis literatur sedia ada berkaitan ekonomi gig dengan memberi tumpuan kepada implikasi terhadap tenaga kerja serta cabaran struktural dalam konteks negeri Sabah, Malaysia.

Menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif, kajian ini meneliti pelbagai pangkalan data akademik utama termasuk Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar bagi mengenal pasti trend global, faktor penyumbang, serta dinamika sosioekonomi yang membentuk penyertaan dalam ekonomi gig. Analisis tematik digunakan untuk mengkategorikan dapatan kepada empat tema utama, iaitu landskap konseptual ekonomi gig di peringkat global, realiti penyertaan tenaga kerja di Sabah, kapasiti institusi dalam mengawal selia pasaran buruh digital, dan keberkesanan kerangka dasar serta perundangan.

Dapatan kajian menunjukkan bahawa walaupun ekonomi gig membuka peluang pekerjaan alternatif dan meningkatkan fleksibiliti tenaga kerja, ia juga memperluas jurang ketidaktentuan pendapatan, menghakis perlindungan sosial, dan mewujudkan ketidakseimbangankuasa antara platform digital dan pekerja. Dalam konteks Sabah, kekangan infrastruktur digital, ketidakseimbangan pembangunan wilayah, dan dominasi sektor tidak formal memperburuk lagi cabaran ini. Artikel ini menegaskan keperluan mendesak terhadap reformasi dasar yang komprehensif serta kolaborasi strategik antara kerajaan, industri, dan institusi latihan bagi memastikan kelestarian tenaga kerja dalam era ekonomi digital.

Kata Kunci: Ekonomi gig, tenaga kerja, fleksibiliti pekerjaan, ketidaktentuan, Sabah, pendigitalan pekerjaa

title: A Comprehensive Review of Statistical Methods in Quantitative Finance: From Classical Inference to Machine Learning Frontiers

detail.title: A Comprehensive Review of Statistical Methods in Quantitative Finance: From Classical Inference to Machine Learning Frontiers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. No human or animal subjects were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This comprehensive review provides a rigorous, graduate-level synthesis of statistical methodologies essential for modern quantitative finance. We present a systematic framework spanning measure-theoretic probability, advanced statistical inference, financial time series analysis, volatility modeling, portfolio optimization, stochastic calculus, extreme value theory, Monte Carlo methods, high-dimensional statistics, and cutting-edge machine learning applications. Each topic is treated with mathematical depth, emphasizing both asymptotic theory and finite-sample implementation. The review covers classical approaches such as ARIMA-GARCH frameworks and factor models, alongside modern developments including random matrix theory for covariance estimation, sparse precision matrices via graphical LASSO, copula-based dependence modeling, and deep learning architectures for sequential data. Special attention is devoted to the unique challenges of financial data: heavy tails, volatility clustering, non-stationarity, microstructure noise, and the pervasive low signal-to-noise ratio. Advanced topics include Lévy processes, realized volatility estimators, high-frequency econometrics, Bayesian nonparametrics, causal machine learning, and reinforcement learning for trading. Model validation, multiple testing corrections, and robust inference are discussed throughout. This synthesis serves as both a pedagogical resource for doctoral students and a research compendium for practitioners, bridging the gap between statistical theory and quantitative finance practice.

title: The Informal Settlement Space: A Network and Spatial Approach to Land Formalisation Policy in Urban Latin America

detail.title: The Informal Settlement Space: A Network and Spatial Approach to Land Formalisation Policy in Urban Latin America
detail.abstract: Land formalisation programs in Latin America have achieved significant scale, yet their aggregate effects remain uneven and insufficiently understood. Existing evaluations primarily assess plot-or household-level impacts, treating each settlement as an isolated unit and disregarding the broader urban system. This concept note introduces the Informal Settlement Space, a framework that models informal settlements in Metropolitan Lima as nodes within a spatial network and applies methods from network science and spatial econometrics to examine how a settlement's network position influences both the direct benefits of formalisation and the spillovers generated for neighbouring informal settlements. Leveraging the staggered rollout of COFOPRI's formalisation program across approximately 3,715 settlements in Metropolitan Lima between 1996 and 2020, and integrating remotely sensed outcomes (built-up density, road paving, night-time lights) with administrative data on settlement characteristics and infrastructure, the study estimates a difference-indifferences model that interacts treatment with pre-formalisation centrality indicators and dynamic neighbour-formalisation rates. This framework enables identification of whether hub or peripheral settlements benefit more from formalisation, the existence of critical-mass effects in the share of neighbouring settlements formalised, and the extent to which infrastructure connectivity amplifies or attenuates spillovers. By integrating network science, spatial econometrics, and the land formalisation literature, this project introduces a new diagnostic and policy-design tool for slum upgrading programs, with direct implications for sequencing and targeting strategies. To the best of the author's knowledge, this constitutes the first application of settlement-level network complexity methods to the causal evaluation of land formalisation programs in Latin America.

title: Real-Time Industry News and the Predictability of Market Returns

detail.title: Real-Time Industry News and the Predictability of Market Returns
detail.abstract: This paper examines how shocks to industries' input-intensive and extensive human capital-as well as shocks to their outputs, including production, sales, and inventories-predict the market values of U.S. NAICS sectors and the aggregate market. I assume that industries' market values are linked through input-output connections in a static network, which I estimate directly from the data. Modeling each sector's expected return as a linear function of its network-connected inputs and outputs, I find that the framework explains 40% of the monthly variation in aggregate market returns and, on average, 34% of the variation across sectors, in sample. Out of sample, the model delivers approximately 5% predictive R 2 for the aggregate market. Predictability is strongest for upstream sectors, such as manufacturing and mining, which transmit shocks broadly, and weaker for downstream sectors, such as retail and construction.

title: Pricing the Left Tail: Consumption Skewness and Expected Returns
affiliations: University of Oxford, Saïd Business School and University of Cambridge

detail.title: Pricing the Left Tail: Consumption Skewness and Expected Returns
detail.abstract: Downside risk to aggregate consumption growth predicts equity returns. We estimate the conditional distribution of U.S. consumption growth using quantile regressions with machine-learning variable selection, and summarize downside risk by Kelley skewness, the asymmetry between the upside and downside of the distribution. A more left-skewed conditional distribution forecasts 12-month excess returns roughly 16 percentage points higher, with an out-of-sample R 2 of 7.8%. Symmetric risk measures such as variance and dispersion have no comparable predictive power. In the cross section, consumption-skewness betas explain about 91% of return variation across size, book-to-market, and industry portfolios. The largest deteriorations in Kelley skewness follow financial uncertainty and bad investment-specific technology news, both operating through asymmetric movement in the lower tail rather than parallel shifts in the distribution. Monetary-policy surprises are not first-order unconditional drivers, but they exhibit clear state dependence: easing improves the lower tail of expected consumption growth precisely when downside risk is already elevated.

title: The Extraction Attenuation Framework

detail.title: The Extraction Attenuation Framework
detail.abstract: The Extraction Attenuation Framework (EAF) proposes γ = load/capacity as a portable normalization heuristic for quantifying extraction pressure across biological, economic, and institutional systems. We tested this heuristic across three structurally independent domains and found mixed but directionally consistent support. In the wage extraction domain (n = 11 sectors), a pre-specified composite γ_wage showed a strong, statistically significant rank correlation with voluntary quit rates from JOLTS data (Spearman ρ = 0.693, p = 0.018), robust to sensitivity analyses and replication in 2023 data. The sleep debt domain (n = 16 sectors from NHIS and BLS injury data) yielded a positive but non-significant correlation with workplace injury rates (ρ = 0.318, p = 0.230), with an exploratory saturation pattern near γ ≈ 0.68 (hypothesis-generating only). In the nursing home staffing domain (n ≈ 14,394 facilities), a single-ratio γ_staffing against a fixed normative benchmark produced only weak, gradual associations with health deficiencies and quality measures (R² ≈ 0.02); a linear model was preferred over logistic, and no sharp threshold was detected. A deliberate null test using aggregate household debt time series confirmed that low-resolution data cannot detect non-linear load-capacity dynamics. These results illustrate that EAF functions best as a flexible screening and comparison tool rather than a universal predictive law. Its value lies in making extraction pressure measurable and comparable across domains, while highlighting the critical role of data resolution and benchmark choice. We map 22 additional testable domains and provide open protocols for independent replication.

title: Demographics and Japanification: Who's Next?

detail.title: Demographics and Japanification: Who's Next?
detail.abstract: We test whether demographic structure predicts "Japanification"-the syndrome of simultaneously low growth, low inflation, and low interest rates-using Fair-Dominguez polynomial age-distribution variables in a panel of 194 countries from 1990 to 2024, with income-conditioned controls (log GDP per capita and Z₁ × log GDP/cap) replacing the prior KAOPEN-based specification. The answer is: weakly yes, but unstably so. On a cleaned two-component index (growth and inflation, with shock-year exclusions and five-year rolling averages), the first demographic polynomial is significant (Z₁ = 1.252, SE = 0.357, p < 0.001; N = 5,361, R² = 0.075), but the persistent channel is disinflation, not growth: on five-year rolling averages, all three Z terms significantly predict lower inflation (Z₁ =-3.07, p < 0.001) while no Z term predicts growth (Z₁ p = 0.26). In raw annual data, demographics sometimes correlate with growth, but that relationship is transitory and does not survive rolling-average smoothing. Old-age dependency ratio spline regressions identify a growth-drag threshold at approximately 20%, above which the association strengthens (p = 0.014). The demographic-Japanification link exhibits a structural break around the Global Financial Crisis: Z₁ is strongly positive pre-GFC (+2.93, p < 0.001) but turns negative and insignificant post-GFC (-0.27, p = 0.52), a pattern that survives balanced-panel, OECD/non-OECD, income-quartile, and global-factor controls. On a restricted sample using only 10-year government bond yields (eliminating rate measurement heterogeneity), demographics do predict interest rates (Z₁ = 53.1, p = 0.011), but this rate channel disappears post-GFC. The effect is concentrated in middle-income countries (~$8,000 GDP per capita) and is absorbed by working-age share controls. Conditional projections diverge across estimation periods: under pre-GFC coefficients, 8 of 24 focus economies cross the Japanification threshold by 2050; under full-sample coefficients, 1 does (Japan); under post-GFC coefficients, 3 do (Asian economies with high projected aging).

title: Aggregate Collateral Demand
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Department of Finance, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Aggregate Collateral Demand
detail.abstract: We study aggregate collateral demand and document its effect on the Treasury convenience yield. Prices of safe assets reflect a variety of non-pecuniary benefits—safety, liquidity, and collateral services—whose relative importance is hard to pin down. We establish the causal pass-through from aggregate collateral demand shocks to the Treasury convenience yield by measuring collateral sinks, different ways in which safe assets are removed from circulation, even if temporarily. We show that the rapidly growing over $1 trillion collateral-swap market exacerbates these effects in times of stress.

title: Explainable AI-Based Spam Email Classification System

detail.title: Explainable AI-Based Spam Email Classification System
detail.abstract: This research paper presents the analysis and design of an Explainable AI-based Spam Email Classification System that aims to enhance transparency and trust in automated email filtering. Email spam has become a critical issue in digital communication, often leading to security threats such as phishing, fraud, and malware attacks. While traditional machine learning techniques effectively classify spam emails, they lack interpretability and operate as black-box systems. To overcome this limitation, the proposed system integrates Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques with machine learning classification. The system uses TF-IDF vectorization and Logistic Regression for spam detection and incorporates SHAP-based explainability to provide word-level justification for classification decisions. UML diagrams including use case, class, activity, sequence, component, and deployment diagrams are used to model the system structure and behavior. The proposed model demonstrates how UML-based system design combined with Explainable AI improves transparency, reliability, and user confidence in spam detection systems. This research contributes to the development of interpretable and intelligent email security solutions suitable for academic and real-world applications.

title: AI-Driven Interview Preparation System with Automated Evaluation

detail.title: AI-Driven Interview Preparation System with Automated Evaluation
detail.abstract: In the highly competitive landscape of modern recruitment, effective interview preparation plays a crucial role in achieving career success. Traditional preparation methods, such as static question banks or peer-conducted mock interviews, often suffer from several limitations including inconsistency, lack of realism, and the absence of immediate and constructive feedback. To address these challenges, the AI Interview Simulator is proposed as an advanced webbased application designed to provide job seekers with a realistic, automated, and personalized interview preparation experience. The system aims to simulate real interview conditions so that candidates can practice effectively and improve their confidence before attending actual interviews. The proposed system utilizes Google Gemini AI as an intelligent virtual interviewer capable of generating dynamic questions based on specific job roles, job descriptions, and candidate experience levels. Unlike traditional static interview preparation platforms, this simulator adapts to the user's profile, ensuring that the questions are relevant, practical, and appropriately challenging. The application is developed using a modern technology stack that includes ReactJS with TypeScript to build a responsive and interactive frontend, while Shadcn UI is used to create a clean and professional user interface. Clerk Authentication is integrated to provide secure user access and maintain data privacy. Additionally, Firebase is used as the backend solution to manage real-time data storage, including user profiles and interview history, enabling users to track their progress and performance over time.

reference: 24 Nw. J. Tech. & Intell. Prop. (forthcoming 2026)
title: Two Cheers for Cox v. Sony
affiliations: and University of Richmond School of Law

detail.title: Two Cheers for Cox v. Sony
detail.abstract:
There’s a lot to dislike about the Supreme Court’s opinion in Cox Communications, Inc. v. Sony Music Entertainment.  It mischaracterizes, oversimplifies, and ignores precedent. It fails to engage with important arguments. It mangles the meaning of “intent.” And it introduces uncertainty into the workings of secondary liability in other intellectual property regimes.

For these reasons, the decision doesn’t deserve three cheers. But it deserves two. Because in two important ways, the Supreme Court has succeeded. First, the opinion fixes some misguided appellate court holdings by articulating a relatively workable standard for important future copyright cases. Second, despite its arguably disruptive effect, that standard draws the right lines between those that should be liable and those that should not.

title: Decomposed Specification Tests for Asymmetric Network Panels
affiliations: Depart of Economics, University of Sao Paulo

detail.title: Decomposed Specification Tests for Asymmetric Network Panels
detail.abstract: This paper develops specification tests for irregular network panels with time-varying and asymmetric interaction matrices. We decompose each matrix into symmetric and antisymmetric components and show that standard residual quadratic diagnostics, including Moran's I and the LM-error statistic, are exactly invariant to the antisymmetric component. In contrast, lag-type bilinear diagnostics retain directional information. Building on this dichotomy, we derive a joint score limit for the decomposed lag alternative and propose conditional score tests for directional and contextual relevance. The directional statistic LM a|s tests whether the antisymmetric component contributes information beyond symmetric exposure, while LM s|a provides the corresponding contextual test. The tests have standard chi-square limits under primitive conditions for irregular panels. Monte Carlo evidence shows that the decomposed tests control size and correctly attribute network propagation across contextual and directional channels, whereas conventional quadratic diagnostics are exactly direction-blind and conventional lag diagnostics conflate the two channels.

title: Relational Semantic Structure: A Framework for Meaning Beyond Vector Similarity

detail.title: Relational Semantic Structure: A Framework for Meaning Beyond Vector Similarity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Current AI systems treat meaning as a fixed representation encoded in vector space and retrieved through similarity-based mechanisms. This approach captures surfacelevel patterns, but structurally excludes the relational, contextual, and temporal dimensions through which meaning is actually formed. This paper proposes Relational Semantic Structure (RSS) as a framework for understanding how meaning is organized beyond static representation. We argue that meaning does not reside in nodes, but emerges from relational configurationsstructured through selection, constrained by context, and reinforced through collective interaction over time. We define nodes not as fixed units of meaning, but as points of relational divergence. Relations are understood as selection mechanisms that possess direction, strength, and emergent patterns. Within this framework, meaning exists not as a discrete entity but as an uneven distribution of relational possibilities, continuously reconfigured by contextual variables and observable through temporal change. We further demonstrate that the limitations of current AI systems arise not from insufficient scale or performance, but from the structural absence of relational tracking, reinforcement mechanisms, and contextual weighting. Similarity-based retrieval cannot substitute for relational selection, and therefore cannot sustain the structural continuity through which meaning persists. This paper extends the Fluid Relational Semiotic (FRS) framework introduced in previous work, shifting from the declaration that meaning is a process to a structural account of what that process produces. Meaning is not a representation. It is a constrained configuration of relational states.

title: Fluid Relational Semiotic: A Model of Meaning Construction Beyond Static Vector Representation

detail.title: Fluid Relational Semiotic: A Model of Meaning Construction Beyond Static Vector Representation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the structural limitations of how current AI systems handle meaning, and proposes a new framework to address them. While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate capabilities in natural language processing, they remain structurally limited in capturing the habitual patterns and fluid dynamics through which meaning emerges in collective interaction. This paper redefines meaning as a semiotic process, and proposes the Fluid Relational Semiotic (FRS) model on the basis that this process is constituted through relational structures and temporal change. Meaning is not defined-it is formed. Because it evolves, it cannot be fixed; because it cannot be fixed, it cannot be monopolized.

detail.abstract: Between November 2025 and April 2026, the five largest enterprise governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform vendors repositioned their product lines around artificial intelligence governance. Using documentary analysis of publicly available vendor materials across a twelve month window, this paper examines the pattern of capabilities these vendors now market as AI governance. It finds that the repositioning was substantive in marketing terms and minimal in architectural terms: every vendor's AI governance product is an extension of the observation and workflow automation infrastructure the vendor already sold.

title: Intrinsic Reliability and Robustness for Hyper-Complex Agentic AI Systems - Solution Outline: Architecture and Strategy

detail.title: Intrinsic Reliability and Robustness for Hyper-Complex Agentic AI Systems - Solution Outline: Architecture and Strategy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or non-financial interests. This work was conducted independently and reflects the authors’ research perspectives.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. No ethical approval was required.

detail.abstract: Agentic AI systems act at machine speed, yet the governance mechanisms meant to oversee them remain manual, reactive, and architecturally entangled with the systems they govern. The frontier problem is not capability; it is governability at runtime. This paper presents the complete architectural specification for the Governance Twin: a structurally independent, real-time governance system that shadows agentic AI operations without sharing code, memory, or direct communication channels. We introduce a three-plane architecture (Operational, Governance, Integrity) connected by strictly unidirectional data flows that enforce a fundamental separation: observation flows upward and is immutable, while guidance flows downward and influences agent context without controlling agent execution. Within this architecture, we specify four novel components and their interactions. Sentinels perform external-only behavioral observation, comparing agent actions against a governance baseline and packaging deviations into Evidence Bundles, the atomic unit of governance memory. A multi-agent Council aggregates evidence across the agent population, detects emergent patterns through statistical and correlation analysis, and reaches governance decisions via structured voting with delegated authority boundaries. The Historian maintains governance memory across three specialized stores (graph, vector, and append-only) to support provenance traversal, semantic precedent search, and sequential audit. An Ethics-Morals-Values (EMV) state hierarchy governs behavioral expectations at three levels of stability, from hard boundaries that change over months to adaptive thresholds that tune continuously. Integrity is achieved through hash chains, Merkle trees, and distributed ledger anchoring that make tampering detectable rather than claiming to make it impossible. The architecture is platform-independent, specifying capability requirements rather than vendor products, and is designed for incremental adoption from single-agent deployments to federated multi-organization governance. All design decisions are grounded in the principle that governance must operate at the same speed as the systems it governs, while remaining structurally incapable of becoming an operational bottleneck.

title: Joint Forest Management.

detail.title: Joint Forest Management.
detail.abstract: After the failure of the colonial 'command and control' approach of forest governance in the 1970s, a group of dedicated forest bureaucrats of West Bengal realised that the state forests could not be protected without local people's participation. At the behest of a handful of forest officials, villagers agreed to form protection committees to protect the forest, assisted by the Forest Department staff. The villagers' participation in forest protection soon enhanced the forest physiognomy, biodiversity, and economic benefits from non-timber forest produce to the forest villagers. The success of this early Joint Forest Management (JFM) led to the governmental endorsement of JFM as the forest management approach, to be emulated in all states. However, within a decade, bureaucratic high-handedness and corruption in collusion with the rural elite undermined the system.

keywords: Asset pricing model Paper type Research paper

publicationDetails.detailsText: International Journal of Emerging Markets, volume 18, issue 10, 2021[10.1108/IJOEM-09-2020-1124]

detail.abstract:
Purpose-This study is about the determinants of cash holding and impact of cash holding on mutual funds' performance. In addition, the study analyzes the impact of performance-related determinants of cash holding on funds' performance. 

Design/methodology/approach-Panel data of ten years of 190 open-end mutual funds are analyzed through fixed effect regression technique. The risk-adjusted funds' performance of cash based portfolios is computed through capital asset pricing model (CAPM) (1964), Fama and French (1993) and Carhart (1997) models. 

Findings-The results indicate that small size funds, high charging front-end load funds, high turnover ratio funds, high 12-month fund returns run up, high dividend paying funds and high redemption level funds hold more cash for precautionary purpose to avoid costs of cash shortfalls. Further, monthly average raw returns and risk-adjusted performance of funds with the lowest raw and residual cash holding are found higher than the funds with the highest cash holding. An increase in cash is found to dilute performance. 

Originality/value-This is a pioneer study in a corporate environment with shallow capital market, reliance of businesses on bank credit, firms exposed to agency issues, wealth expropriations and existence of business groups with political linkages but with opportunities of investments due to expected favorable geo-sociopolitical situation. The study generates outcomes relevant for other similar economies.

title: New evidence on business investment and capital reallocation
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy,  and Bank of Italy

detail.title: New evidence on business investment and capital reallocation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 996
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper provides new facts about business investment and capital reallocation by exploiting a novel and comprehensive dataset of firms’ vehicle transactions, covering the universe of purchases of new and used vehicles, as well as the leases recorded by the Italian vehicle register between 2015 and 2023. We show that leasing is very common, as it represents about 50 per cent of vehicle acquisitions. Financially constrained firms have a higher propensity to lease rather than purchase, while young firms rely heavily on the market for used vehicles. Reallocation of used vehicles occurs for about 50 per cent of the transactions within the same industry. Transactions involving used vehicles mostly occur among firms with similar productivity, or between very low productivity firms that sell vehicles to firms with higher productivity, as the former are likely to exit the market. When dealers are involved, vehicles are reallocated much more broadly across industries, geographical areas and firm productivity classes, which is consistent with dealers helping to improve capital reallocation.

detail.abstract: High-field infrastructures fail not at the operational level but at the structural threshold where continuity becomes unsustainable. UNC sYstEm L introduces a structural mechanism that activates continuity as a field, stabilizes pre-rupture dynamics, and transforms infrastructures into continuity entities capable of sustaining zero-disruption states. This paper presents the foundational architecture of UNC sYstEm L, its axial continuity codex, the Φ∞ operator, the Yield Engine (YE-Δ), and the structural interfaces that enable stability under high-field compression. The Germany-Belgium filière is examined as a continental case of alignment, demonstrating how structural authority replaces operational power in environments defined by systemic tension.

title: Restorative Justice and Sexual Harm: A Pathway to Gender Equality and Justice Transformation
affiliations: University of Windsor Faculty of Law and Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University

detail.title: Restorative Justice and Sexual Harm: A Pathway to Gender Equality and Justice Transformation
detail.abstract: Following in the wake of the "Hockey Canada trial" in 2025, this article begins from the recognition that sexual harm is a complex social problem of gender inequality in Canada that requires a transformative approach to remediate effectively. Restorative justice is one such transformative approach. In Ontario, however, where the Hockey Canada trial took place, Crown prosecution policy states that individuals charged with sexual offences are categorically ineligible to be diverted to restorative programs at pre-trial stage. In other provinces, there are similar policies and other moratoriums in place that limit the use of restorative justice to varying degrees. Building on insights from the criminal law, feminist legal theory, and penal abolition fields, this article argues that these policies should be revised and moratoriums should be lifted to enable restorative justice to be more widely available in sexual harm cases.

title: REBOUND: REsilience-Based OUtput Allocation for Nonlinear Drawdowns

detail.title: REBOUND: REsilience-Based OUtput Allocation for Nonlinear Drawdowns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper

detail.abstract: Drawdowns are asymmetric, path-dependent processes that dominate capital destruction and investor experience. Traditional allocation frameworks treat drawdowns as retrospective artifacts of return dispersion, providing limited mechanisms to regulate exposure dynamically during drawdown evolution or recovery formation. We introduce REBOUND, a resilience-centred allocation framework that governs capital deployment based on drawdown geometry and recovery stability rather than directional prediction. The framework comprises three components: REBOUND-M, a metric suite formalising resilience momentum (RM), recovery speed (RSI-R), and drawdown-recovery asymmetry (DRAR); REBOUND-S, a regime segmentation model identifying drawdown onset, maximum-stress, and recovery regimes using resilience-aware emissions; and REBOUND-E, a deterministic elastic exposure function that suppresses risk during structural decay and restores capital during statistically stable recoveries. Tested across 31 years of equity, bond, commodity, and cryptocurrency markets, REBOUND-E delivers a Sharpe ratio of 1.54 with a maximum drawdown of 9.11%, compared to Sharpe 0.52 and drawdown 55.19% for buy-and-hold. Out-of-sample validation across three independent train-test splits indicates limited performance degradation. Ablation studies highlight resilience momentum as a primary performance driver, while parameter stability across calibration splits suggests economic interpretability. REBOUND positions resilience as an allocation primitive for drawdown-aware risk control while preserving recovery participation.

detail.abstract: Green finance and sustainable investment have emerged as defining features of the twenty-firstcentury financial landscape, driven by the urgent imperative of addressing climate change and achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. This dissertation presents a comprehensive secondary research analysis of global green finance and sustainable investment trends, drawing on a systematic review of academic literature, regulatory frameworks, policy documents, and industry data. The study examines the principal drivers of green finance market growth-including regulatory innovation, investor demand, and the growing recognition of climate-related financial risks-and evaluates the effectiveness of key instruments including green bonds, ESG equity funds, sustainability-linked financing, and carbon markets. The analysis addresses the principal challenges constraining the green finance ecosystem, including greenwashing, ESG data quality deficiencies, geographic concentration of capital flows, and regulatory fragmentation. The findings confirm the extraordinary growth of the green finance market-with global GSSS bond and loan issuance reaching USD 1.6 trillion in 2021 and ESG fund assets under management exceeding USD 2.74 trillion-while highlighting persistent structural challenges. The analysis reveals that emerging market and developing economies continue to receive a disproportionately small share of global green finance flows, that greenwashing remains widespread despite intensifying regulatory responses, and that the global regulatory architecture for sustainable finance remains fragmented and incomplete. The study concludes with a set of policy and market recommendations for policymakers, financial regulators, institutional investors, and development finance institutions, focused on strengthening the quality, integrity, and geographic reach of green finance flows. The findings contribute to a growing body of evidence that green finance, while a necessary component of the sustainability transition, requires substantial institutional, regulatory, and market reforms to fulfil its transformative potential.

title: Intelligence Inertia: Physical Principles and Applications

detail.title: Intelligence Inertia: Physical Principles and Applications
detail.abstract: While Landauer's principle establishes the fundamental thermodynamic floor for information erasure and Fisher Information provides a metric for local curvature in parameter space, these classical frameworks function effectively only as approximations within regimes of sparse ruleconstraints. They fail to explain the super-linear, and often explosive, computational and energy costs incurred when maintaining symbolic interpretability during the reconfiguration of advanced intelligent systems. This paper introduces the property of intelligence inertia and its underlying physical principles as foundational characteristics for quantifying the computational weight of intelligence. We demonstrate that this phenomenon is not merely an empirical observation but originates from the fundamental non-commutativity between rules and states, a root cause we have formally organized into a rigorous mathematical framework. By analyzing the growing discrepancy between actual adaptation costs and static information-theoretic estimates, we derive a non-linear cost formula that mirrors the Lorentz factor, characterizing a relativistic J-shaped inflation curve-a "computational wall" that static models are blind to. The validity of these physical principles is examined through a trilogy of decisive experiments: (1) a comparative adjudication of this J-curve inflation against classical Fisher Information models, (2) a geometric analysis of the "Zig-Zag" trajectory of neural architecture evolution, and (3) the implementation of an inertia-aware scheduler wrapper that optimizes the training of deep networks by respecting the agent's physical resistance to change. Our results suggest a unified physical description for the cost of structural adaptation, offering a first-principle explanation for the computational and interpretabilitymaintenance overhead in intelligent agents.

title: The Ethical Spillovers of Customer Green Innovation: Evidence from Suppliers’ Carbon Emissions
affiliations: University of International Business and Economics, University of International Business and Economics (UIBE) - School of Banking and Finance, City University of Hong Kong and University of International Business and Economics

detail.title: The Ethical Spillovers of Customer Green Innovation: Evidence from Suppliers’ Carbon Emissions
detail.abstract: This study examines how firms’ climate-related innovation affects carbon emissions throughout supply chains in China. We provide novel evidence that customers’ green innovation generates significant ethical spillovers, leading to substantial reductions in suppliers’ carbon emissions. We further analyze the mechanisms through which green customers help suppliers lower their carbon footprint. Customers with more green innovations incentivize suppliers to increase their own climate-related innovation. In addition, greener customers expand suppliers’ access to trade credit and engage in direct vertical acquisitions, easing suppliers’ financial constraints and supporting their decarbonization activities. These mechanisms are amplified for firms with greater market power, highlighting the key role of powerful green customers in suppliers’ decarbonization decisions. Using the comprehensive quasi-natural experiments of supply chain disruptions and formations, we confirm the robustness and causality of the main findings.

title: Enhancing National Innovation Frameworks Through Open Innovation: a Theoretical Approach to Integrating Open Innovation Principles into the European Innovation Scoreboard

detail.title: Enhancing National Innovation Frameworks Through Open Innovation: a Theoretical Approach to Integrating Open Innovation Principles into the European Innovation Scoreboard

publicationDetails.detailsText: ENVIRONMENT. TECHNOLOGY. RESOURCES. Proceedings of the International Scientific and Practical Conference, volume 1, 2025[10.17770/etr2025vol1.8625]

detail.abstract: Despite the growing prominence of Open Innovation (OI) in business and policy, National Innovation Metrics (NIM) remain largely rooted in traditional, firmcentric models, failing to capture ecosystem-wide collaboration and knowledge exchange This study critically examines how OI is integrated-or overlooked-within major Innovation Measurement Frameworks (IMF), particularly the European Innovation Scoreboard (EIS), Global Innovation Index (GII), and Bloomberg Innovation Index (BII). Findings reveal that existing innovation scoreboards prioritize input-output indicators (e.g., R&D expenditure, patenting) while neglecting systemic, network-driven innovation dynamics. The continued absence of OI-specific metrics reinforces a "black box" effect, where national innovation success is assessed without visibility into knowledge flows and collaborative innovation mechanisms. This study contributes to rethinking NIM by advocating for a shift from closed-system assessments to dynamic, networkbased measurement models. By bridging innovation policy, measurement theory, and OI research, it provides a foundation for future empirical studies on integrating OI indicators into national benchmarking frameworks, ensuring more accurate assessments of Innovation Ecosystem (IE) performance.

title: 1 State or nation, sector or system? How granularity shapes U.S. energy modeling results
affiliations: Joint Global Change Research Institute, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: 1 State or nation, sector or system? How granularity shapes U.S. energy modeling results
detail.abstract: This study analyzes how spatial resolution and cross-sectoral interactions shape future modeled outcomes for the United States energy system, using the Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM). The analysis of spatial resolution considers two configurations: one representing the United States as a single region and another distinguishing each state as a separate region, using harmonized assumptions for all shared technologies. We find consistent high-level results, but demonstrate how the national resolution can be more accommodating to deployment of selected technologies where the use of nationally aggregated supply curves can mask geographic mismatches between low-cost production and demand. This is illustrated with hydrogen produced by renewable electrolysis, where low-cost production sites (e.g., the Northern Great Plains) are often quite far from major population and industrial centers. Cross-sectoral impacts from accelerated technological advances are weakest for buildings, greater for transportation, and strongest for electricity generation. In buildings, advanced technologies tend to increase electricity demand while also improving its efficiency. In contrast, improvements in the electricity generation sector drive nearly 400~TWh per year of additional electricity demand, primarily in industry and transportation, highlighting comparatively strong sectoral responses here. The study provides commentary on the implications of these results for the roles of single-sector as opposed to energy-system-wide modeling and analysis.

title: Does Digital Trade Boost Firms’ Green Innovation? A Quasi-Natural Experiment Of China’s Cross-Border E-Commerce Comprehensive Pilot Zones

detail.title: Does Digital Trade Boost Firms’ Green Innovation? A Quasi-Natural Experiment Of China’s Cross-Border E-Commerce Comprehensive Pilot Zones
detail.abstract: Trade-environmental nexus is a long-term and challenging research topic. The literature generally supports that international trade leads to technology effect, which is an important driver for improving environmental quality. However, the previous literature focuses on traditional trade. Amid diminishing traditional comparative advantages and developing digital technology, digital trade has been a new model for trade development. Is digital trade environmentally friendly? To answer this question, we regard the establishment of China’s Cross-Border E-Commerce Comprehensive Pilot Zones (CBECCPZ) as a quasi-natural experiment. We employ difference-in-difference model and Chinese listed firms from 2011 to 2022 for empirical analysis. The results demonstrate that CBECCPZ significantly increases firms’ green patents. Mechanisms show that firms’ green innovation is primarily driven by the increases in firms’ revenue, R&D investment and human capitals as well as the alleviation in financing constraint. These positive effects are more pronounced for central regions, the regions with fewer local fiscal expenditures and firms without CEO duality. Earlier batches of pilot policy generate greater innovation incentives relative to later batches. Spatial analysis reveals a negative spillover effect, which reduces green innovation of neighboring non-pilot regions within 50km radius. In general, we enrich the literature on the trade-environment nexus from the perspective of digital trade, and provide implications for new trade model and sustainable development (especially for developing countries).

title: Energy Markets at War The Effect of the Russian Invasion of Ukraine on Refinery Margins
affiliations: and German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf - Department of Economics

detail.title: Energy Markets at War The Effect of the Russian Invasion of Ukraine on Refinery Margins
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the effect of the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 on refinery margins, i.e. the difference between wholesale prices for road fuels (gasoline and diesel) and oil prices in Europe and Germany in particular. Following the Russian invasion of Ukraine, wholesale road fuel prices net of taxes rose by more than 50 cents per liter, whereas crude oil prices increased by only about 30 cents per liter. Using a difference-in-differences framework, we compare refinery margins in Germany with those on the Amsterdam–Rotterdam–Antwerp (ARA) spot market, which serves as a European benchmark price. The results indicate that refinery margins in Germany increased by approximately 5–6 cents per liter relative to the ARA region after the invasion. We attribute this differential primarily to Germany’s strong dependence on Russian Ural crude oil imports and to the presence of regional market power among German refineries. We further document substantial heterogeneity in treatment effects across both time and regions. In addition, the invasion was associated with a significant decline in fuel demand, with gasoline consumption falling by about 13% and diesel consumption by approximately 9%.

title: Identity Politics

detail.title: Identity Politics
detail.abstract:
This essay examines the origins, evolution, and internal contradictions of identity politics, arguing that in its modern form it has become, for the most part, a misdirected preoccupation. Identity politics has deep historical roots — in religious conflict, labor struggles, and the emancipatory movements of the Enlightenment — but its contemporary incarnation, grounded in immutable personal traits such as race, gender, and sexuality, has generated a characteristic dialectic: the demand for recognition based on difference sits uneasily alongside the liberal ideal of universal equality. 

That tension is explored through the civil rights tradition, the work of Martin Duberman, and the controversy surrounding Herrnstein and Murray's {\em The Bell Curve}, whose claims linking intelligence, race, and social stratification are shown to rest on methodological confusion, normative overreach, and a poorly concealed eugenic agenda. The essay then turns to the appropriation of identity politics by both the political Right and the political Left, arguing that, despite their opposed intentions, both deploy it in ways that are ultimately anti-democratic. Most critically, the shared embrace of diversity across the political spectrum serves to displace attention from economic inequality — the more fundamental and more tractable of the two problems. 

The essay concludes that neither a politics of recognition nor a politics of non-discrimination is sufficient: what is needed is a structural reorientation that takes seriously the systemic economic conditions that reproduce segregation, poverty, and exclusion.

detail.abstract: Whether a fully vegan world would actually be better for the planet, for people, and for animals is one of the most heated debates in food systems right now. This paper breaks down the evidence across five areas: environmental impact, affordability, nutrition, food shelf life, and the ethics of animal death in both plant and animal agriculture. After reviewing over 20 peer-reviewed studies and systematic reviews published between 2018 and 2025, the picture that emerges is more complicated than either side usually presents. Plantheavy diets offer real, well-documented environmental advantages, including 46 to 75% reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and land use. But a fully vegan global food system runs into serious problems with nutritional completeness (especially vitamin B12, iron, and omega-3s), affordability in developing nations, food system resilience, and cultural feasibility. The evidence points to a dramatic reduction in animal product consumption as the best path forward, not a complete elimination. The EAT-Lancet Commission's reference diet, which is mostly plant-based with small amounts of sustainably produced animal products, captures roughly 80 to 90% of the environmental and health benefits of full veganism while avoiding the biggest risks.

title: Second Chances, Unequal Gains: Gender Differences under High-Stakes Exam Reform
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS), Department of Economics, National University of Singapore (NUS) and National University of Singapore (NUS) - Department of Political Science

detail.title: Second Chances, Unequal Gains: Gender Differences under High-Stakes Exam Reform
detail.abstract: This paper studies how institutional design shapes gender differences in high-stakes examinations. We exploit a college entrance exam reform that introduced withinyear retake opportunities and greater flexibility in subject choice, and combine it with student-level data linking multiple exam attempts. We show that reducing the oneshot nature of high-stakes exams improves female performance relative to males, with effects concentrated in affected subjects. The gains arise from two mechanisms: lower exam pressure and endogenous subject sorting, as female students reallocate toward comparative-advantage subjects. These results suggest that high-stakes exams do not simply measure ability but actively shape how ability is expressed and how inequality emerges.

While property ownership is broadly consistent, discrepancies emerge in the distribution due to secondary dwellings being omitted in surveys and to missing properties in administrative data, mainly due to the failure to register ownership transfers of inherited properties. To address this issue, we propose two integration approaches which lead to a more complete representation of the housing wealth distribution.

detail.abstract: In the grand tapestry of cosmic time, the emergence of intelligence stands as a rare and precious phenomenon. Our journey, from the primordial soup to the cusp of interstellar civilization, is a testament to the power of adaptation, innovation, and the relentless pursuit of knowledge. But this journey is far from over. As we stand on the precipice of unprecedented technological advancements, we must confront the fundamental question of survival: How do we ensure the continuity of intelligence in a universe governed by entropy and punctuated by existential risks? This book is an exploration of that question. It is not a prophecy, but a rigorous examination of the scientific principles, technological possibilities, and ethical imperatives that will shape the future of our civilization. It is an attempt to bridge the gap between scientific reality and speculative horizons, to ground our aspirations in the firm foundation of physics and probability. Drawing upon the insights of cosmology, thermodynamics, artificial intelligence, and systems theory, I present a framework for understanding the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. I call this framework AURORAa civilizational survival architecture for post-planetary humanity. This is not a journey for the faint of heart. It requires us to confront uncomfortable truths about our place in the cosmos, the fragility of our existence, and the ethical responsibilities that come with the power to shape our own destiny. But it is a journey worth undertaking, for the stakes are nothing less than the survival of intelligence itself. I invite you to join me on this exploration, to challenge my assumptions, to question my conclusions, and to contribute your own insights to the ongoing conversation about the future of our civilization. Let us embark on this journey together, with open minds, critical thinking, and a deep sense of responsibility for the legacy we leave behind.

title: Iterative Adversarial Inquiry (IAI): "The Whetstone Method:- A Framework for Generating Theoretical Contributions Through Structured Adversarial Debate

detail.title: Iterative Adversarial Inquiry (IAI): "The Whetstone Method:- A Framework for Generating Theoretical Contributions Through Structured Adversarial Debate

keywords: epistemology Journal of Economic Literature (JEL) Classification: B40

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Iterative Adversarial Inquiry (IAI) colloquially, the Whetstone Method, a framework for generating original theoretical contributions through structured adversarial debate. The dominant model of social science research, the hypothetico-deductive method, begins with a hypothesis and tests it against data. IAI begins differently: with a provocation derived from a researcher's existing, post-experiential bias, which is then subjected to adversarial pressure in two sequential debate stages: a logical debate that tests internal coherence, and a literature debate that tests novelty and positioning. The framework is cyclical rather than linear. The output of each iteration becomes the starting point of the next, producing a progressively refined body of knowledge in which each element carries a documented record of the challenges it has survived. We argue that this method is epistemologically superior to hypothesis-first research for one specific class of problem: generating the theoretical category that does not yet exist. We demonstrate this claim using a detailed case study: the development of the Aspiration Horizon framework, which emerged through precisely this process. We trace the method's philosophical antecedents in Peirce's abductive inquiry and self-correcting epistemology, distinguish it from Grounded Theory and the Delphi method, and specify its quality criteria, sparring partner requirements, and documentation standards. We further examine the method's applicability across disciplines including management, policy, psychology, economics, and artificial intelligence research, and argue that the emergence of AI as a thinking interlocutor makes IAI available at scale for the first time in the history of academic research.

detail.abstract: Nigerian police misconduct, from extortion and illegal detention to extrajudicial violence and torture, is routinely dismissed by authorities as the work of isolated “bad apples.” This paper rejects that framing. Predatory behavior on this scale is not aberrant; it is symptomatic of institutional decay, dysfunctional internal discipline, and the commercialization of state coercion. Traditional reform strategies have consistently failed. In their place, this paper proposes concrete, technology-driven alternatives: the digitization of all police-civilian financial transactions, OSINT-integrated civilian oversight, the gazetting of checkpoints, and statutory protections for sousveillance.

title: Crisis Without a Hurricane: Accountability, Disability, and Crisis-Driven Education Reform in Virginia

detail.title: Crisis Without a Hurricane: Accountability, Disability, and Crisis-Driven Education Reform in Virginia
detail.abstract: Hurricane Katrina marked a pivotal moment in U.S. public education reform, enabling largescale restructuring through state takeover, charter expansion, and accountability-driven intervention. While framed as emergency recovery, these reforms became a national policy template, shaping education governance far beyond New Orleans. This article examines how post-Katrina reform logics have been normalized within Virginia public education policy absent a natural disaster. Using critical policy analysis informed by disaster capitalism theory and disability studies in education, the study analyzes Virginia's accountability, accreditation, and intervention frameworks, with particular attention to implications for students with disabilities. Findings indicate that crisis-oriented accountability systems privilege efficiency, comparability, and performance metrics over stability, continuity, and wellness-conditions essential for inclusive education. The replication of post-Katrina reform strategies without disaster conditions functions to institutionalize emergency governance as routine state practice, disproportionately affecting students with disabilities and marginalized communities. This study contributes to education policy scholarship by conceptualizing crisis as a governing logic embedded within accountability systems and highlighting its implications for disability equity and the long-term stability of inclusive education systems.

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the dynamics of household disposable income during and after the 2022– 2023 inflationary shock. Using a microsimulation approach based on Banca d’Italia’s BIMic model, we decompose changes in disposable income into four components: (i) nominal income adjustments to inflation; (ii) real income growth; (iii) fiscal drag and benefit erosion; and (iv) policy interventions. Our results indicate that, on average, household purchasing power eventually returned to pre-crisis levels in 2025. Over 2022-2025, disposable income growth was slightly higher than inflation for households in the three middle income quintile groups. It was broadly in line with inflation for the bottom quintile and fell slightly short of it for the top quintile.

title: AI-Powered Portfolio Optimization Platform with Multi-Asset Allocation and Adaptive Advisory

detail.title: AI-Powered Portfolio Optimization Platform with Multi-Asset Allocation and Adaptive Advisory
detail.abstract: The conventional approaches towards portfolio optimization such as Mean Variance Optimization (MVO) and Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), have strong dependencies on historical static performance and the assumption of linear behaviour in asset returns and their correlations, proving them inefficient under volatile market conditions where these assumptions fail to hold true. Moreover, traditional approaches lack the capability of handling unstructured data, such as sentiments from markets based on news articles and social media platforms or macroeconomic factors. In this paper, we present FinanceWiz, which is an intelligent platform developed for portfolio optimization through return forecasting using LSTM, analysis of market sentiments based on news and social media, rebalancing by reinforcement learning, and AI investment coach. This study was conducted using 10 years dataset of assets such as stocks, forex, commodities, and cryptocurrency. Our experiments have demonstrated that the AI advisory module of our proposed system is flexible under changing market dynamics. The findings of our analysis indicate that the proposed AI model is superior to MVO under volatile regimes.

title: The Black Hole Index: A Structural Lock-In Measurement Framework for Digital Platforms

detail.title: The Black Hole Index: A Structural Lock-In Measurement Framework for Digital Platforms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the creator and maintainer of the Black Hole Index platform (blackholeindex.com). All scores represent the author's expert assessment using published anchored rubrics. No external funding was received.

detail.abstract: We introduce the Black Hole Index (BHI), a domain-agnostic measurement instrument for quantifying structural lock-in and switching costs in digital and physical platforms. The model decomposes lock-in into 11 scored parameters grouped into three categories — Capture (six variables measuring dependency depth), Escape (three variables measuring exit feasibility), and Extended (two variables capturing organizational embedding and momentum). Parameters are aggregated using a modified Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) function with a Milgrom-Roberts complementarity correction and combined into a dimensionless ratio B = Capture / (ε + EscapeCore × feedback), where feedback implements endogenous escape suppression via behavioral inertia. We apply BHI to a cross-section of 96 platforms across 12 sectors — AI, cryptocurrency, social media, Big Tech, SaaS, banking, fintech, e-commerce, gaming, pharma, and critical infrastructure — generating the first systematic structural lock-in ranking of the global platform economy. Results reveal that infrastructure platforms (EDA duopoly: B ≈ 13.0; ASML: B ≈ 9.6; TSMC: B ≈ 10.9) exhibit lock-in an order of magnitude higher than attention-based platforms (Netflix: B ≈ 1.0; Dogecoin: B ≈ 0.2), despite the latter commanding larger user bases or market caps. A sensitivity analysis demonstrates ranking robustness to coefficient variation within ±30%. We further specify a dynamic extension modeling the co-evolution of structural lock-in and human skill decay. BHI is positioned as a proposed measurement instrument at a pre-empirical stage: formula specification and arithmetic verification are complete; inter-rater reliability testing and predictive validation against observable switching behavior remain pending. We discuss limitations, validation requirements, and paths toward empirical calibration.

detail.abstract:
Perkembangan pesat teknologi digital dalam era Revolusi Perindustrian Keempat telah membawa kepada kemunculan Taylorisme Digital dan pengurusan algoritma sebagai bentuk baharu kawalan kerja. Artikel ini menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif untuk mensintesis literatur berkaitan fenomena tersebut, dengan memberi tumpuan kepada implikasi terhadap struktur organisasi, autonomi, dan maruah pekerja. Analisis tematik mengenal pasti empat tema utama: dominasi pengurusan algoritma dalam organisasi moden, kemunculan panoptikon elektronik melalui pengawasan berterusan, erosi autonomi dan maruah pekerja akibat metricisation, serta kelemahan kerangka dasar dan perlindungan buruh. Dalam konteks Malaysia, khususnya Sabah, cabaran infrastruktur digital dan literasi teknologi yang tidak sekata memperdalam ketidakseimbangan kuasa antara majikan dan pekerja, sekali gus meningkatkan risiko eksploitasi. Kajian ini menekankan keperluan institusi seperti kementerian, jabatan tenaga kerja, dan kesatuan sekerja untuk membangunkan kerangka perundangan serta etika digital yang lebih komprehensif. Implikasi dasar termasuk keperluan ketelusan algoritma, perlindungan privasi data, program peningkatan kemahiran, serta penglibatan aktif kesatuan sekerja. Secara keseluruhannya, kajian ini menyumbang kepada literatur sosiologi kerja dengan menghubungkan konsep klasik Taylorisme kepada bentuk kawalan digital kontemporari, serta membuka ruang perdebatan tentang masa depan kerja dan keadilan organisasi dalam era digital.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Nepal Rastra Bank Samachar, Anniversary Issue, 2026

detail.abstract: This article explores the reason behind the weak private sector credit growth in Nepal despite ample liquidity and sustained monetary easing. Using quarterly data from 2015Q1-2025Q4 and dynamic regression framework, result shows, the rising uncertainty is the key constraint to suppress credit expansion by weakening the transmission channel of monetary policy. The findings reveal the importance of robust macroeconomic environment to boost confidence and strengthen policy transmission.

title: Improving Disaster Recovery Using the Agile Government Framework
affiliations: , University of Oregon, University of Oregon, University of Oregon and University of Oregon

detail.title: Improving Disaster Recovery Using the Agile Government Framework

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was approved by the University of Oregon Institutional Review Board
declarations.funderStatement: Funded by the Joint Fire Science Program, US Department of the Interior

detail.abstract: Wildfires are increasing in frequency and severity across the Western United States, yet longterm recovery efforts remain hampered by bureaucratic rigidity, unclear organizational roles, and resource inequities among jurisdictions. This article investigates how an agile government approach-adaptive leadership, iterative learning, cross-sector partnership, and procurement flexibility-could improve disaster recovery. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 15 state and local officials involved in recovery from Oregon's 2020 Labor Day Fires, we find that organizations able to quickly redeploy staff, form flexible partnerships, and work around rigid funding structures outperformed those constrained by bureaucratic inertia. However, these capacities were unevenly distributed, favoring better-resourced jurisdictions. Structural barriers, including federal and state reimbursement timelines, poor inter-agency coordination, and the absence of pre-disaster planning, repeatedly forced recovery actors to work around systems rather than through them.

title: Smart Agriculture Assistant Using Images

detail.title: Smart Agriculture Assistant Using Images
detail.abstract: Agriculture plays an important role in the economy, and access to proper information about modern crops and cultivation practices is essential for farmers and agricultural enthusiasts. Many people are interested in learning about foreign cultivated vegetables, but they often lack a simple platform where they can easily view information, fertilizer details, and purchasing options.

title: Knowledge Hiding Hindering Project Success: The Impact of Shared Leadership with The Mediating Role of Team Building and Relationship Quality

detail.title: Knowledge Hiding Hindering Project Success: The Impact of Shared Leadership with The Mediating Role of Team Building and Relationship Quality
detail.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of shared leadership (SL) on project success (PS) in knowledge-intensive environments, particularly within the Pakistani construction industry. It further investigates the mediating roles of team building (TB), relationship quality (RQ), and knowledge hiding (KH), grounded in Conservation of Resources (COR) theory. Design/Methodology/Approach: A quantitative research design was employed, with data collected from 381 construction professionals in Pakistan. The study utilized SPSS for preliminary analysis and SmartPLS (PLS-SEM) for hypothesis testing and structural model evaluation. Findings: The results reveal that shared leadership has a significant positive effect on project success and a significant negative effect on knowledge hiding. Additionally, team building and relationship quality partially mediate the relationship between shared leadership and project success by reducing knowledge hiding behaviors. Originality: This study contributes to the existing literature by integrating leadership, knowledge behavior, and team dynamics into a comprehensive framework. It extends the application of COR theory in project management and offers practical insights for enhancing project success in developing economies, particularly in the construction sector.
