title: The Effect of Employer Branding on Employees Retention, the Mediating role of Psychological Contract (An Empirical Study on the Employees of International Organizations in Syria)

detail.title: The Effect of Employer Branding on Employees Retention, the Mediating role of Psychological Contract (An Empirical Study on the Employees of International Organizations in Syria)
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of employer branding values and practices on the employees" retention. Data were collected from both primary and secondary sources. A total number of 371 valid questionnaires were collected from international organizations located in Syria. The main results are: (1) Economic, interest, and developmental values have significant and positive effect on employees" retention; (2) social value is significant and negative for employees" retention; (3) and application value is insignificant. (4) Economic, interest, and developmental values are significant and positive for psychological contract; (5) social and application values are insignificant. (6) Psychological contract is positive and significant for retention. (7) Psychological contract fully mediates the relationship between employer branding (economic, interest, and developmental values) and employees" retention, while it doesn"t play such role for social and application values. Recommendations and practical implications are mentioned at the end of the study.

title: Measuring Macroeconomic Uncertainty: A Cross-Country Analysis

detail.title: Measuring Macroeconomic Uncertainty: A Cross-Country Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper constructs internationally consistent measures of macroeconomic uncertainty. Our econometric framework extracts uncertainty from revisions in data obtained from standardized national accounts. Applying our model to post-WWII real-time data, we estimate macroeconomic uncertainty for 39 countries. The crosscountry dimension of our uncertainty data allows us to study the impact of uncertainty shocks under different employment protection legislation. Our empirical findings suggest that the effects of uncertainty shocks are stronger and more persistent in countries with low employment protection compared to countries with high employment protection. These empirical findings are in line with a theoretical model under varying firing cost.

title: Overconsumption Drives the Global Ecological Deficit
affiliations: Shandong University, Shandong University, The University of Hong Kong, University of Maryland, College Park - Department of Geographical Sciences, Shandong University, University of Maryland and Shandong University

detail.title: Overconsumption Drives the Global Ecological Deficit
detail.abstract: Global consumption increasingly exceeds the Earth's regenerative capacity, resulting in a persistent ecological deficit. However, the distribution of this deficit across global expenditure deciles and its underlying drivers remain insufficiently quantified. Here, we combine household expenditure data for 168 countries with a multiregional input-output approach to estimate the distribution of the global ecological footprints (EFs) and the associated drivers of ecological deficit. We find that the global ecological deficit is overwhelmingly concentrated among affluent consumers: the top 10% account for 57% of the total deficit, whereas the bottom 50% contribute negligibly and stay within biocapacity limits. This concentration is particularly pronounced in forest land (100%) and grazing land (76%). Decomposition analysis further shows that expansion in consumption scale is the dominant driver of the ecological deficit, outweighing the offsetting roles of consumption structure and footprint intensity. These findings identify consumption scale as the primary mechanism linking economic inequality to ecological deficit and provide a quantitative basis for evaluating demand-side strategies aimed at operating within planetary boundaries.

title: The Effectiveness of Quantitative Easing: A Comparative Analysis of the United States, Japan, and the Eurozone

detail.title: The Effectiveness of Quantitative Easing: A Comparative Analysis of the United States, Japan, and the Eurozone

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that they have no known personal or financial relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The paper will discuss the effectiveness of Quantitative Easing (QE) as an unusual tool of monetary policy in the three most significant economic zones: the United States, Japan and the Eurozone. Using a comparative theoretical and graphical approach, the transmission mechanisms and real economic outcomes of QE policies undertaken by the Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan, and European Central Bank since 2008 are analyzed through the application of five macroeconomic models: the money market model, the IS-LM model, the AD-AS model, the AA-DD model, and the Phillips Curve. Results affirm that QE attained its key financial market goals in all the three economies because it decreased the interest rates in the long term, narrowed the yield spreads on sovereign bonds and avoided deflationary spirals. Nonetheless, actual economic impacts on output, employment and inflation differed significantly in the three cases. Transmission of QE was most pronounced in the United States, where market-based financial system, credible central bank communications and supplementary fiscal stimulus added strength to the monetary expansion. Japan is an excellent example of the constraints of QE in a structural stagnation and deep-rooted deflationary psychology, validating the applicability of the liquidity trap and balance sheet recession models. The Eurozone offers a middle-ground solution, which is limited by the institutional heterogeneity, financial constraints, and ineffective transmission in the banking sector by the peripheral member states. They are three major determinants of QE effectiveness, and they are structure of the financial system, credibility of inflation expectations, and the existence of complementary fiscal and structural policies. The implications of these findings include significant implications to the design of monetary policy in low-growth and low-inflation settings.

title: Automation and High-Skill Labor Markets: Evidence from Robo-Advisors

detail.title: Automation and High-Skill Labor Markets: Evidence from Robo-Advisors
detail.abstract: Does artificial intelligence substitute or complement high-skill labor? We study financial robo-advisors and their impact on the labor market for human advisors. Using novel data on robo-advisors and advisor employment, we find that robo-advisors increase, rather than reduce, human advisor employment. To address endogenous adoption, we exploit cross-state regulatory entry costs interacted with a national financing shock affecting technology firms. States experiencing greater robo-advisor entry exhibit meaningful growth in advisor employment, particularly among firms serving retail investors. Investor-level evidence shows robo-advisor exposure increases subsequent engagement with human advisors, consistent with market expansion and complementarity between automation and professional financial services.

title: Automasi, Deskilling dan Polarisasi Pekerjaan: Ancaman dan Peluang Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif terhadap Struktur Pasaran Buruh

detail.title: Automasi, Deskilling dan Polarisasi Pekerjaan: Ancaman dan Peluang Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif terhadap Struktur Pasaran Buruh
detail.abstract:
Perkembangan pesat kecerdasan buatan generatif (KBG) telah mencetuskan transformasi mendalam dalam struktur pasaran buruh global dengan memperluaskan keupayaan automasi daripada tugas fizikal rutin kepada tugas kognitif yang kompleks. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis secara kritis impak KBG terhadap tenaga kerja, khususnya dalam konteks sama ada teknologi ini berfungsi sebagai mekanisme augmentasi yang meningkatkan keupayaan pekerja atau sebaliknya menyumbang kepada fenomena deskilling dan polarisasi pekerjaan. Pendekatan ulasan naratif digunakan dengan merujuk kepada literatur akademik terkini daripada pangkalan data seperti Scopus dan Google Scholar. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa KBG berpotensi meningkatkan produktiviti dan memperkaya peranan pekerja melalui kolaborasi manusia-mesin, namun pada masa yang sama mempercepatkan penggantian tugas rutin dan mengurangkan keperluan kemahiran tertentu. Fenomena ini seterusnya menyumbang kepada polarisasi pasaran buruh, di mana pekerjaan berkemahiran tinggi berkembang manakala pekerjaan pertengahan semakin terhakis. Dalam konteks Sabah, cabaran struktur seperti jurang digital dan ketidakseimbangan ekonomi memperhebat kesan tersebut. Artikel ini mencadangkan intervensi dasar yang menekankan pembangunan kemahiran adaptif, perlindungan sosial dan transformasi institusi bagi memastikan manfaat teknologi dapat diagihkan secara lebih inklusif.

 

Kata kunci: Automasi, Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif, Deskilling, Polarisasi Pekerjaan, Pasaran Buruh

title: The Humanization of Teaching: Addressing a Structural Gap in Teacher Preparation

detail.title: The Humanization of Teaching: Addressing a Structural Gap in Teacher Preparation
detail.abstract: Teacher preparation programs have historically emphasized instructional competence, assessment literacy, and classroom management, often at the expense of preparing candidates for the human, emotional, and ethical labor inherent in the profession (Hochschild, 1983; Hargreaves, 1998). Drawing on practitioner insight, teacher education scholarship, and contemporary challenges in workforce retention, this paper argues that the absence of a required, standalone course centered on the humanization of teaching represents a structural gap in teacher preparation. Using the author's positionality as a veteran educator navigating licensure preparation, this manuscript examines how fragmented approaches to identity, trauma, disability, emotional labor, and professional sustainability undermine teacher effectiveness and longevity (Ingersoll et al., 2018; Santoro, 2018). The paper proposes The Humanization of Teaching as a foundational course model and positions human-centered preparation as an institutional responsibility essential to equity, teacher retention, and student learning.

title: When Numb Becomes Normal: Emotional Numbness as a Systemic Condition in Secondary Schooling

detail.title: When Numb Becomes Normal: Emotional Numbness as a Systemic Condition in Secondary Schooling

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved secondary analysis of de-identified survey data voluntarily provided by students with appropriate consent procedures. No personally identifiable information was collected or retained, and all findings are reported in aggregate. The study adhered to applicable institutional and district research guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Emotional numbness—characterized by flattened affect, detachment, and restricted access to feeling—has become increasingly normalized in secondary schooling, particularly within systems serving communities exposed to chronic instability. This article advances a central claim: emotional numbness is not merely an individual coping response imported into schools, but a systemically produced and institutionally rewarded condition of contemporary schooling.

Drawing on trauma theory, critical pedagogy, affect scholarship, and engagement research, the article conceptualizes emotional numbness as both an adaptive response and an institutional outcome shaped by accountability systems, surveillance practices, and normative interpretations of compliance. To substantiate this claim, the study presents mixed-methods evidence from an urban public-school context, including survey data from over 600 secondary students examining emotional numbness and its relationships to attendance, engagement, disciplinary experiences, and academic performance.

Findings indicate that emotional numbness is a coherent and measurable construct, moderately prevalent across secondary schooling, significantly associated with reduced engagement and academic performance, and weakly related to disciplinary outcomes. This pattern suggests that emotional withdrawal can quietly erode learning while remaining institutionally undetected within systems designed to identify disruption.

The article concludes by critiquing individualistic approaches to social-emotional learning and trauma-informed reform and advancing emotional rehumanization as an analytic horizon for redesigning schools. Rather than focusing solely on student regulation, this framework calls for structural changes that make emotional presence safer and more sustainable within educational environments.

title: Kleptocracy

detail.title: Kleptocracy
detail.abstract: We build the first crosscountry database of kleptocratic regimes-governments organized around the personal enrichment of the ruler and the movement of stolen wealth offshore. Using financial evidence from offshore leaks, asset freezes, and forfeiture proceedings, we identify 47 episodes across 44 countries since 1948. We validate the database against the ICIJ Offshore Leaks records and then estimate the economic cost using synthetic control methods. The results reveal a large, persistent, and compositionally distinctive pattern of damage that direct theft alone cannot explain.

title: Banking Access and Crypto Participation: Evidence from India's Crypto Ban
affiliations: Texas State University,  and Prairie View A&M University - Department of Accounting, Finance & Information Systems

detail.title: Banking Access and Crypto Participation: Evidence from India's Crypto Ban
detail.abstract: Can governments curb retail cryptocurrency participation by restricting access to regulated banking rails, and what spillovers follow in the formal financial system? We study India's 2018 "banking ban" on virtual currencies and its 2020 reversal by the Supreme Court. Using a difference-indifferences design complemented by event-study evidence, we combine country-time measures of retail crypto participation with indicators of formal financial participation and payment activity. We document three findings. First, restricting banking access produces a large, immediate contraction in retail crypto activity. Second, the reversal does not generate an equal-and-opposite rebound; recovery is gradual rather than immediate. Third, the restriction is associated with spillovers into the formal financial system, including higher bankaccount ownership, household deposit accounts, and some payment-system measures. These results identify banking access as a key transmission channel for retail crypto participation and show that debanking policies can have persistent effects and broader financial spillovers even when later reversed.

title: Hazy Dreams: The Impact of Air Pollution on Sleep

detail.title: Hazy Dreams: The Impact of Air Pollution on Sleep

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required as this research relies exclusively on publicly available anonymous data.

keywords: environmental risk factors JEL Codes: I12

detail.abstract: Surprisingly little is known about the causal impact of air pollution on human sleep. We provide quasi experimental evidence that short-run exposure to particulate matter reduces objectively measured sleep. Using daily district-level data on sleep duration from 0.5 million consumer wearable users in Germany from 2020 to 2022, we show that even relatively low levels of particulate matter air pollution adversely affect sleep. We use a high-dimensional fixed effects approach and document that a 10 µg/m 3 increase in average daily PM10 concentration reduces sleep duration by about one minute. To strengthen the causal interpretation of our findings, we confirm these findings with an instrumental variables approach, using local wind direction as a predictor for local air pollution. Our findings offer a potential mechanism linking air pollution to a wide range of human outcomes. Although the estimated effects are modest in magnitude, the central role of sleep in human well-being highlights the potential social burden of pollution-induced sleep loss.

title: Banking Crises and Macroeconomic Forces: Global Perspectives

detail.title: Banking Crises and Macroeconomic Forces: Global Perspectives
detail.abstract: This study examines the likelihood of banking crises employing the logistic regression approach. The data is sourced from the Global Macro Database, a comprehensive macroeconomic time series repository covering 243 countries and territories. The findings suggest that GDP growth reduces the probability of banking crises, and conversely, tight monetary policy increases the likelihood. Likewise, appreciation in housing prices in the current period lowers the risk; however, the housing price in the past increases the probability of crises. The other control variables are money supply, sustainable public finance, and favorable current account balance, which significantly lower the probability of a crisis. Policymakers should strive to balance fiscal and monetary measures for sustainable growth and implement macro-prudential regulations to prevent excessive speculation in the asset market. Timely consideration of short-term and long-term risk factors strengthens financial stability and minimizes the probability of banking crises in the future.

title: Evaluation Framework for Agentic AI Learning Systems Date

detail.title: Evaluation Framework for Agentic AI Learning Systems Date
detail.abstract: Recent research has introduced agentic artificial intelligence architectures for educational systems in which specialized AI agents coordinate conversational tutoring, curriculum generation, speech interaction, and safety governance. While such architectures promise improved personalization, instructional reliability, and scalable learning delivery, systematic evaluation frameworks for assessing the performance and governance characteristics of agentic learning systems remain limited. This research contributes an evaluation methodology for next-generation agentic AI learning environments, providing a foundation for measuring reliability, safety governance, and adaptive learning effectiveness in multi-agent educational systems.

title: From Tools to Transformation: Building an Open-Access Resilience Toolkit Ecosystem for Asian Cities

detail.title: From Tools to Transformation: Building an Open-Access Resilience Toolkit Ecosystem for Asian Cities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not contain any studies with human or animal subjects performed by any of the authors.
declarations.funderStatement: The research is not funded.

detail.abstract:
Asian cities sit at the frontline of escalating climate and disaster risks, yet efforts to mainstream disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate adaptation into urban development remain fragmented and projectized. This policy-oriented paper asks: How can a functional, open-access resilience toolkit ecosystem enable officials and practitioners to systematically integrate standardized DRR and climate adaptation frameworks into city-level planning and implementation in Asia? Drawing on recent toolkits for integrating DRR and climate adaptation into local planning, open-data and e-resilience initiatives, ASEAN urban resilience programmes, and knowledge hubs, the paper develops a conceptual model for a "resilience toolkit ecosystem" that connects open standards, modular tools, and practice-based learning across cities.
It situates the GXS Resilience Hub and the book From Reaction to Resilience: Asia's Strategic Transformation in Disaster Risk Reduction as catalytic platforms that can translate this ecosystem into policy traction and political narratives. Methodologically, the paper synthesizes secondary literature and regional initiatives with practice-informed scenarios, and it deliberately includes contrarian perspectives-critiquing over-standardization, technocratic capture, and digital divides. 
The paper concludes with actionable recommendations for ASEAN, national governments, city leaders, and development partners to co-govern such an ecosystem, fund it sustainably, and embed it in planning mandates, thereby moving Asian cities from isolated pilots to systemic resilience.

title: The Huawei Pedigree: Honor, xFusion, Yinwang, and Huawei's Legacy

detail.title: The Huawei Pedigree: Honor, xFusion, Yinwang, and Huawei's Legacy
detail.abstract: One of the hottest names in Chinese tech is Honor, which built the “Lightning” autonomous robot that broke the world record set by a human for a half-marathon by seven minutes at the 2026 Beijing E-Town Half-Marathon. What is worth highlighting is the fact that Honor is not a robotics company at all. Honor is a smartphone company spun off from Huawei in 2020 that only started designing robots in 2025. In other words, Honor was able to beat out all of its competitors in China to create arguably the world's fastest running robot without any significant experience in robotics. As this article will show, a significant factor behind Honor's success and the success of  other Huawei spinoffs like xFusion and Shenzhen Yinwang is the "Huawei pedigree." With the benefit of the "Huawei gene," these short-lived spinoffs can adopt a long-term vision and boldly expand into new technological areas without running into then same short-term tunnel vision that afflicts most startups.

title: A tale of two cities: Bangalore's stagnation in the shadow of the California AI Boom

detail.title: A tale of two cities: Bangalore's stagnation in the shadow of the California AI Boom
detail.abstract: For decades, the Indian IT sector has been viewed as a leveraged proxy for US technology growth. This paper re-evaluates this relationship in the wake of the Generative AI revolution. Using daily data from March 2021 to February 2026, I apply a timezone-adjusted (lagged) asymmetric beta model to account for the market transmission delay between New York and Mumbai. I find that the structural relationship between the Nasdaq 100 and Nifty IT remains statistically stable. The sector continues to exhibit a low but significant upside beta (≈0.29) and a slightly higher downside beta (≈0.36), with no statistically significant structural break post-ChatGPT. However, a divergence emerges in risk-adjusted performance. While the Nasdaq 100's Sharpe Ratio surged from a crisis-level-0.57 to a hyper-efficient 1.14, the Nifty IT sector's efficiency remained stagnant (0.16 → 0.17). These findings suggest that Indian IT functions as a stable "utility-like" stakeholder in the tech ecosystem, insulated from the direct volatility of the AI boom but also excluded from its efficiency premium.

title: Melgo Sequence: A Price Structure Classification Framework Built on the Behavioral Properties of HL2, HLC3, and OHLC4 as Structural Market Levels

detail.title: Melgo Sequence: A Price Structure Classification Framework Built on the Behavioral Properties of HL2, HLC3, and OHLC4 as Structural Market Levels

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the sole developer of the Melgo Sequence indicator system, which is commercially available as an invite-only subscription product on TradingView. This research was conducted independently to validate the conceptual framework underlying that system. No external funding was received. No third party has a financial interest in the findings of this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involves no human participants, no patient data, and no personally identifiable information. All data analyzed consists of publicly available market price data from TradingView. No ethics approval is required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded by the author. No institutional, corporate, or grant funding was received or sought.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents the Melgo Sequence, an original price structure classification framework derived from the relative ordering of three standard derived price levels within any completed higher-timeframe candle: HL2 designated the Neutral Anchor, HLC3 designated the Structural Core, and OHLC4 designated the FakeOut Threshold. These levels were identified independently through direct market observation as behaviorally distinct structural zones — HL2 as a price equilibrium and stabilization zone, HLC3 as the most actively defended price within any candle, and OHLC4 as the zone where fakeout activity concentrates due to its sensitivity to candle origin. Their relative ordering produces six classification states with defined market character.

The framework was validated through eight phases of empirical backtesting across four instruments — BTCUSDT spot, SPY, EURUSD, and NASDAQ — covering 18,904 higher-timeframe candles. All findings are reported with binomial significance tests and Bonferroni-corrected confidence intervals. Single-timeframe classification produces no actionable directional edge after multiple comparison correction across any instrument or state. Multi-timeframe confluence produces statistically confirmed edge on two states: Accumulation on BTCUSDT at 62.3% bull directional accuracy (p=0.0021, n=162, 95% CI 54.4% to 69.8%) and Bear Trend on SPY at 60.0% bull (p=0.0041, n=215, 95% CI 53.1% to 66.6%), both surviving Bonferroni correction. Zone break at the primary structural level is the most statistically robust finding in the research: SPY Bull Rejection zone breaks produce 83.7% bearish outcomes (p<0.001, n=153, 95% CI 76.8% to 89.1%) and SPY Bear Trend zone breaks produce 90.5% bullish outcomes (p<0.001, n=63, 95% CI 80.4% to 96.4%). A structural crossover exit system warns before the hard stop fires in 82 to 89 percent of trades across all four instruments, all confirmed at p<0.001. An original touch-only wick finding reported in an earlier version is retracted following peer review — corrected measurement produces results statistically indistinguishable from a coin flip. The dominant variable in level pierce behavior is the timeframe that produced the level, not the specific level type, with 4H levels producing 74 to 85 percent fakeout rates on 15-minute bars compared to 61 to 65 percent for 1H levels. A statistically confirmed asset-class dependency is documented — the same structural state carries materially different directional implications on risk assets versus the EURUSD forex pair, confirmed by two-proportion z-test at z=3.044, p=0.0023. The conceptual framework was developed by Jeff Rey Melgo. Research architecture, statistical analysis, and manuscript preparation were conducted with substantial assistance from Claude, an AI language model developed by Anthropic. Full AI disclosure is included in the paper.

title: Taylorisme Digital dan Pengawasan Tempat Kerja: Penggunaan Teknologi Pemantauan Masa Nyata dan Pengurusan Algoritma di Tempat Kerja (Peranti Pengimbas di Gudang dan Perisian Penjejak)

detail.title: Taylorisme Digital dan Pengawasan Tempat Kerja: Penggunaan Teknologi Pemantauan Masa Nyata dan Pengurusan Algoritma di Tempat Kerja (Peranti Pengimbas di Gudang dan Perisian Penjejak)

declarations.ethicsApproval: Artikel ini merupakan ulasan naratif literatur dan tidak melibatkan sebarang pengumpulan data langsung daripada peserta manusia, haiwan, atau ujian klinikal. Justeru, kelulusan etika daripada jawatankuasa etika institusi tidak diperlukan.

detail.abstract: Revolusi Perindustrian Keempat telah melahirkan satu bentuk transformasi radikal dalam pengurusan buruh melalui pengintegrasian teknologi pemantauan masa nyata dan pengurusan algoritma di tempat kerja. Fenomena yang sering dirujuk sebagai Taylorisme Digital ini memperluaskan logik kawalan saintifik Frederick Taylor ke tahap yang lebih invasif, di mana peranti pengimbas di gudang, perisian penjejak produktiviti, dan sistem algoritma menggantikan pengawasan manusia tradisional. Artikel ulasan naratif ini bertujuan untuk menyintesis literatur sedia ada mengenai impak teknologi pemantauan digital terhadap autonomi pekerja, kesejahteraan psikologi, dan hubungan industri, dengan memberikan tumpuan khusus kepada konteks pasaran buruh di Sabah, Malaysia. Menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif, artikel ini menganalisis sumber daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar. Analisis tematik menghasilkan empat tema utama: landskap konseptual Taylorisme digital dan evolusi pengurusan algoritma, realiti perlaksanaan teknologi pemantauan di tempat kerja Malaysia dan Sabah, kapasiti institusi dalam melindungi hak privasi pekerja, serta kerangka perundangan dan dasar sedia ada. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa teknologi pemantauan masa nyata telah meningkatkan intensifikasi kerja dan tekanan psikososial pekerja, manakala di Sabah, ketiadaan peruntukan undang-undang khusus mengenai privasi data pekerja dan keterbatasan kesedaran digital dalam kalangan kesatuan sekerja memburukkan lagi keadaan. Artikel ini mengemukakan cadangan dasar termasuk pindaan Akta Kerja 1955 untuk memasukkan klausa perlindungan data peribadi pekerja, penubuhan garis panduan etika algoritma, dan program literasi digital untuk perwakilan kesatuan sekerja di Sabah.

title: The Predictive Power of Twitter Sentiment for Bitcoin and Ethereum Volatility: Evidence from HAR-RV and GARCH Models

detail.title: The Predictive Power of Twitter Sentiment for Bitcoin and Ethereum Volatility: Evidence from HAR-RV and GARCH Models

declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of the Master's Seminar "Money, Finance and Cryptocurrencies" at the University of Basel. No external funding was received.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether social media sentiment derived from Twitter and Reddit improves the explanatory power and predictive performance of cryptocurrency volatility models. Using Bitcoin and Ethereum as benchmark assets, we combine sentiment indicators with econometric volatility models, including GARCH-type specifications (GARCH, EGARCH, GJR-GARCH) and the Heterogeneous Autoregressive Realized Volatility (HAR-RV) framework. Twitter sentiment is quantified through polarity-based labels, while Reddit sentiment is extracted using VADER to ensure comparability across platforms. The empirical results show that Twitter sentiment exhibits statistically significant correlations with realized volatility and modestly enhances short-horizon forecasts in the HAR-RV setting, particularly during periods of heightened market stress such as the 2022 crash. Overall, the findings suggest that cryptocurrency volatility is primarily driven by internal market mechanisms rather than daily fluctuations in social media sentiment, offering implications for risk management and volatility forecasting in digital asset markets.

detail.abstract: Do markets erode morality, or do standard market-versus-non-market comparisons overstate their role? We study this question in a laboratory experiment with three repeated treatments: unilateral non-market choice, bilateral market trading, and a bilateral non-market environment in which the harmful outcome requires mutual consent. In all treatments, subjects decide whether to preserve a donation that finances one week of lunches for a rural school student in China or instead appropriate money privately. Reexamining the standard unilateral-versus-market comparison in a related but distinct setting, we find that market interaction is more permissive than unilateral non-market choice. But once we introduce a more comparable bilateral non-market benchmark, much of this contrast is already present without market exchange. Overall, the evidence suggests that standard market-versusunilateral comparisons capture more than market interaction alone, while the market retains a smaller and threshold-dependent permissive effect.

detail.abstract: This research explores the crucial role of bridge makers in fostering the success of open innovations within innovation ecosystems. Emphasizing governance structures, this study highlights the importance of creating synergies among participants through effective intermediaries. Bridge makers act as connectors, facilitators, and integrators, crucial for fostering collaboration among diverse stakeholders, aligning interests, and overcoming barriers to innovation. By integrating the bridge maker role into ecosystem strategies, stakeholders can ensure that the connections formed are not only numerous but also robust, inclusive, and capable of driving long-term innovation and collaboration. Given the fragmented nature of recent literature on the role of bridge makers, and the various terminologies used to describe similar roles, this research aims to provide a clear definition and comprehensive understanding of the bridge maker's role. The objective is to analyze different aspects and names attributed to this role within the context of innovation ecosystems. This paper concludes by discussing future research avenues that can build on the developed role typology, shedding further light on the process of open innovation ecosystem genesis. By incorporating the bridge maker role into the various ecosystem models, this research suggests that enhanced connectivity and synergy can be achieved, benefiting the entire ecosystem.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the emergence of managed-authoritarian tendencies within the United States as an outcome of self-reinforcing structural dynamics. Using systems thinking, institutional theory, and elements of behavioural and game theory, it argues that the political and cultural turbulence of the present reflects not merely leadership style but systemic drift—feedback loops that prioritize spectacle, competition, and short-term advantage over adaptation and balance.

By integrating insights from Donella Meadows, Hannah Arendt, Francis Fukuyama, Guy Debord, Niklas Luhmann, and others, the analysis traces how reinforcing loops of distrust, inequality, and information distortion weaken democratic resilience. It concludes by identifying alternate paths to address the shortcomings and breakdowns identified, grounded in feedback awareness, structural recalibration, and the renewal of civic learning.

The 21st-century crisis of democracy is not ideological but informational.

title: Methods for Measuring Open Innovation's Impact on Innovation Ecosystems in the Context of the European Innovation Scoreboard

detail.title: Methods for Measuring Open Innovation's Impact on Innovation Ecosystems in the Context of the European Innovation Scoreboard
detail.abstract: In today's globalized and rapidly evolving technological landscape, innovation serves as a critical driver of economic growth and competitive advantage. The concept of an innovation ecosystem has emerged to elucidate the complex interactions among various stakeholders-including public sectors, startups, academia, businesses, NGOs, and venture capitalists-who collaborate and compete to foster technological advancements and economic growth. Open innovation emphasizes leveraging external ideas alongside internal efforts to enhance innovation capabilities, fostering more dynamic and resilient systems. Additionally, learning from innovation failures plays a crucial role in shaping effective strategies for growth, as startups often translate these learnings into robust innovation frameworks. Given the increasing complexity and interconnectedness of innovation ecosystems, traditional metrics often fail to capture their dynamic and collaborative nature. The European Innovation Scoreboard (EIS) provides a comprehensive framework for assessing the innovation performance of EU countries, offering insights into the overall health and performance of innovation ecosystems. This review article addresses the need to identify metrics and methods for measuring open innovation's impact on innovation ecosystems. Building upon foundational theories and empirical findings, this study proposes a framework for evaluating the impact of open innovation on innovation ecosystems. It integrates insights from the academic literature with EIS metrics to develop robust methods for assessing open innovation's multifaceted influence. This review article is particularly relevant as firms and policymakers strive to understand which metrics are most affected by open innovation and how these can be leveraged to enhance the performance and sustainability of innovation ecosystems.

detail.abstract: Greenwashing, that is, the deceptive self-portrayal of companies as sustainable and environmentally friendly, is an increasingly relevant issue in finance. Identifying greenwashers is not a trivial task, given the difficulty of assessing firms’ true environmental profiles, especially when relying on traditional data sources that generally overlook communication strategies and mass perceptions. Using granular credit data from the euro area banking system, we show that during the period 2019-2023, greenwashers, initially identified by combining information on firms’ carbon emissions with an assessment of the reliability of their reporting, were able to borrow at lower interest rates than other companies. We then assess companies’ environmental profiles by extracting textual information from newspapers and the internet. We find that sentiment scores based on firms’ own websites are generally higher than those derived from newspapers, suggesting that companies use their communication channels to place greater emphasis on their sustainable image than is reflected in external sources. By integrating this textual metric with our initial proxy, we construct an alternative definition of greenwashing. Based on a sample of Italian firms, results obtained from this combined proxy are consistent with those derived from structured data alone. Finally, by introducing an unexpected contractionary monetary policy shock into our framework, we confirm the operation of the credit risk channel of monetary policy and find evidence of a reduction in the pricing benefits previously enjoyed by greenwashers.

detail.abstract: Product management is entering a period of real change. The forces driving this is artificial intelligence, the increasing amount of user data, and the way decision-making is spreading across organisations are not just small improvements. They are starting to reshape what product managers do, how they are evaluated, and the skills they need to stay effective. This article looks at where product management may be heading between 2026 and 2030. It draws on current research, emerging organisational trends, and the economic pressures shaping the technology sector. The main idea is straightforward: the product managers who will do well in this period are not just those who adopt AI tools. They are the ones who develop the judgment to use them carefully, knowing when to rely on them, when to question them, and how to keep decisions focused on real user needs rather than just efficiency metrics.

title: Small Modular Reactors and the Urban Just Transition: Behavioral and Institutional Insights for Climate Action
affiliations: Stetson University, College of Law, Students

detail.title: Small Modular Reactors and the Urban Just Transition: Behavioral and Institutional Insights for Climate Action
detail.abstract: From the domestication of fire to the combustion of coal and the electrification of modern grids, each leap in energy history has embodied both promise and peril. Nuclear energy is no exception. Despite being among the cleanest and most reliable sources of electricity, outperforming wind and solar in terms of lifecycle emissions, capacity factor, and land use efficiency, nuclear power remains marginalized in many sustainability taxonomies. This exclusion is not grounded in scientific evidence but in political inertia, financial orthodoxy, and regulatory asymmetry. This article presents a sustainability-centered critique of global clean energy governance, examining how the persistent policy rejection of nuclear energy, particularly Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), undermines emissions targets, violates principles of climate equity, and hinders scalable solutions for energy-insecure nations. Drawing on the UNECE Life Cycle Assessment, international taxonomy debates, and emerging U.S. energy policy shifts, the article argues that SMRs represent a test case for whether policy frameworks can evolve to meet the dual imperatives of Sustainable Development Goal 7 (affordable and clean energy) and Sustainable Development Goal 13 (climate action). When governance fails to recognize proven, dispatchable, zero-carbon energy sources, the barrier to decarbonization is not technical-it is institutional. Whether SMRs succeed or stagnate may serve as a litmus test for the adaptability and credibility of global climate governance.

detail.abstract: Mongolia's education sector has received more than USD 2 billion in international reform investment since 1990. Formal compliance with donor mandates has reached 91 per cent. Yet substantive learning outcomes have not improved commensurately, and the Ministry of Education's own 2025 Statistical Report documents 4,981 students enrolled in remedial programmes-an implicit acknowledgment that the system has not reached them the first time. This article proposes that the underlying cause is not a failure of intent, competence, or resources. It is a Systemic Ontological Mismatch: international reform programmes are architecturally premised on a linear, deadline-driven model of time, while Mongolia's educational organizations operate within a seasonally-structured temporal habitus formed through generations of nomadic pastoral life. When these two temporal frameworks occupy the same organizational field, the result is Involuntary Compliance Theater-actors throughout the system, including donors, state agencies, and school administrators, are structurally compelled to generate the appearance of reform while the conditions for genuine internalization remain absent. This article names the mechanism, maps its three operational forms, documents its most concentrated empirical manifestation-the Institutional Paradox in which rigid legal mandates conflict with locally effective pedagogical innovation-and proposes Temporal Due Diligence as a practical pre-implementation solution.

detail.abstract: High-stakes exams can be used to rank and select candidates for job openings, and the ability of successful candidates hinges on the design of the exam. I propose a method for modelling candidates’ performance in order to assess how effective the exam is at selecting high-ability candidates - defined as those more likely to provide correct answers after considering the observable characteristics of the candidates, their propensity to answer and the difficulty of the questions asked. I apply this method to the competitive exam used by the Bank of Italy in its hiring practices. This also offers an interesting case study on discrimination in hiring, as the selection rate for women is lower than that for men. The results suggest that the exam tends to select those candidates possessing a higher level of ability. Finally, some simulations show how certain modifications to the exam structure could potentially increase the average ability of the selected candidates.

title: Behavioral Finance in Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures and Swaps: A Systematic Literature Review
affiliations: EIM European Institute of Management, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Behavioral Finance in Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures and Swaps: A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: This review synthesizes the emerging literature on behavioral finance in cryptocurrency perpetual futures and perpetual swaps. It uses a constrained systematic review of accessible repositories, publisher pages, and citation trails for studies published or posted from January 2021 to April 2026. The synthesis separates 13 direct perpetual-futures studies from 6 adjacent behavioral studies that inform interpretation. The central question is how behavioral mechanisms shape trading, pricing, and market quality in perpetual futures markets. The strongest direct evidence concerns speculative demand and basis risk, leverage choice and liquidation risk, funding-rate carry and arbitrage behavior, informed trading and market quality, and exchange-design effects across centralized and decentralized venues. Direct evidence on classic behavioral constructs such as fear of missing out, overconfidence, disposition effects, and learning remains sparse in perpetual-specific settings. Three conclusions stand out. First, perpetuals are behaviorally distinctive because funding fees, leverage, mark-to-market margining, and auto-liquidation create a high-frequency feedback system between prices and trader positions. Second, the strongest causal evidence indicates that perpetual contracts increase spot-market trading volume but worsen adverse-selection conditions when informed trading rises around funding windows. Third, exchange design matters because inverse, linear, quanto, oracle-priced, and VAMM-based contracts expose traders to different incentives and liquidation dynamics. The most important research gaps concern trader-level identification, CEX-DEX comparisons using comparable data, contract-type heterogeneity, and causal tests of leverage-rule changes.

title: HERALDs & OOOKs: Solving Hard Problems in AI with a Herald and a Librarian

detail.title: HERALDs & OOOKs: Solving Hard Problems in AI with a Herald and a Librarian
detail.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as long-term collaborators rather than transient tools, failure modes emerge that are not adequately addressed by existing memory-centred approaches. In sustained human-AI interaction-spanning months, projects, or iterative revisions-errors previously corrected may reappear, exploratory variants may silently replace ratified definitions, and core concepts may drift without acknowledgment. Over time, this produces long-horizon epistemic degradation, in which frequency, recency, and user fatigue implicitly substitute for epistemic authority. We argue that these failures do not primarily result from insufficient context length, retrieval accuracy, or summarisation fidelity. Rather, they arise from epistemic role conflation: contemporary systems lack explicit separation between (1) maintaining what has been committed to as current understanding and (2) tracking how concepts emerge, evolve, diverge, and acquire aliases over time. In the absence of such separation, users are implicitly required to act as the system's primary epistemic memory and governance layer-repeatedly restating corrections, re-uploading profiles, and compensating for silent regressions. This expectation is neither cognitively realistic nor scalable and introduces a self-reinforcing error cycle driven by asymmetric correction cost under prolonged interaction. To address this gap, we propose a minimal, role-separated architectural pattern consisting of two cooperating agents. HERALD (Hierarchical Epistemic Registry of Authorially Locked Determinations) explicitly records ratified canon, corrections, and current epistemic state without adjudicating objective truth; authority is encoded through explicit commitment rather than inferred from repetition or recency. OOOK (an intentionally polysemous acronym denoting an omni-ontological knowledge layer) tracks the lifecycle of concepts, including emergence, revision, deprecation, divergence, and alias drift, while preserving provenance and contextual usage. Canonisation within this framework is explicit: silence is not treated as assent, and frequency is not treated as authority. We show how this separation arrests self-reinforcing error cycles, supports revisionheavy workflows (e.g., evolving theories and narrative worlds), and enables provisional concept retention without premature commitment. We further demonstrate how terminological variation and alias drift can be detected, contextualised, and interactively resolved, rather than silently accumulating ambiguity. Finally, we discuss how this architecture enables automatic, authoritative "resumption snapshots" that allow both humans and LLMs to reliably pick up where they left off across sessions and systems. Importantly, these roles operate asynchronously and event-driven rather than per-token, minimising overhead. Rather than treating memory as a larger storage problem, this work reframes sustained human-AI collaboration as a problem of epistemic governance. By externalising canon maintenance and concept lifecycle tracking as first-class infrastructural roles-rather than displacing these responsibilities onto users-HERALDs and OOOKs offer a path toward durable, humane, and cognitively aligned collaboration over extended time horizons.

detail.abstract: OPEC announcements reveal unanticipated information about future oil supply but may also lead imperfectly informed markets to revise their beliefs about demand conditions. As a result, surprises in oil futures prices around these announcements capture both a supply and a demand shock. Imposing an additional restriction on the sign of the comovement between oil futures surprises and stock price surprises results in clean instruments that separately identify these two components. A negative oil supply news shock has deep and long-lasting stagflationary effects, stronger than previously reported. This poses a challenge for monetary authorities and underscores the importance of accounting for information effects when identifying news shocks.

title: Implementable Randomization and Cross-Sectional Stability

detail.title: Implementable Randomization and Cross-Sectional Stability
detail.abstract: This paper studies equilibrium robustness when mixed strategies are not freely implementable. Players' feasible lotteries are affine cross-sections of mixed-strategy simplices, and restricted games keep payoffs fixed while reducing feasible strategy sets. A Nash equilibrium is cross-sectionally stable (CSSE) if restricted-game equilibria recur arbitrarily close to it along every vanishing family of restrictions. CSSE is a zero-radius implementability test: strict equilibria pass, while mixed equilibria sustained by payoff-distinguishable within-support indifference can fail. In generic two-player games with at least three actions per player, CSSE coincides with strict pure Nash equilibria; hence generic games without pure Nash equilibria have empty CSSE. A three-player benchmark extends the mechanism beyond two-player games. Weak CSSE (WCSSE) is a minimax selection over Nash equilibria; it always exists and agrees with CSSE when CSSE is nonempty. Examples show that WCSSE can select a Chebyshev center and that exposure constraints can overturn a proper equilibrium.

title: Building the Analytical Infrastructure for Governing Frontier AI Development

detail.title: Building the Analytical Infrastructure for Governing Frontier AI Development
detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence presents genuinely novel governance challenges. Its combination of rapid capability growth, omni-use applications, and nearly free proliferation is inconsistent with templates designed for other technologies that may have dangerous applications. Recent attempts to govern AI development have had mixed results, with many proposals vetoed, revoked, weakened, or still searching for enforcement mechanisms. The deeper problem is not political will. It is that the analytical foundations for thinking rigorously about AI governance do not yet exist. We lack even a shared vocabulary. The phrase “AI safety” means at least four different things across different communities, and as a result, summits, reports, and legislative proposals talk past each other.

This paper proposes building the missing analytical infrastructure through a dedicated, independent research institution with a long time horizon. The RAND Corporation's role in nuclear strategy is a useful analogy, not because AI is comparable to nuclear weapons, but because AI, like nuclear technology in the late 1940s, presents strategic questions that existing intellectual frameworks cannot answer. Over roughly fifteen years, RAND and affiliated researchers produced the conceptual vocabulary (deterrence, crisis stability, second-strike capability) that made nuclear governance possible. AI governance has no comparable vocabulary and no institution dedicated to building one.

The proposed institution would be lean, comprising roughly fourteen resident scholars and an annual budget of approximately $12 million, closer in spirit to the Institute for Advanced Study, though much smaller, than to the “CERN for AI” proposals that envision billions in shared infrastructure. It would not need access to proprietary models or training data. Its questions are about actors, incentives, and institutions, not about what any particular frontier AI model can do. Its outputs would include assessments of whether safety frameworks actually constrain behavior, formal models of AI competition dynamics, structured scenario analyses for regulators, and post-incident analysis producing shared facts.

The paper examines why no existing institution fills this role. Government-housed bodies are politically fragile (the U.S. AI Safety Institute was dismantled and repurposed in less than 2 years). University centers are vulnerable to institutional politics (Oxford closed the Future of Humanity Institute in 2024). Industry-funded bodies gravitate toward consensus. Each reason for failure informs the proposed design, which involves freestanding governance, an irrevocable endowment severing funder from research, geographic separation from political capitals, and scholar-driven rather than program-directed organization.

The paper tries to stress-test the idea. A “Why This Might Be Wrong” section considers whether governance risks increasing concentration, whether the object of control is too entangled with general-purpose infrastructure, whether existing institutions could simply be scaled, whether a distributed regime complex is preferable, and whether AI might be the kind of problem that resists institutional solutions entirely. What the objections cannot answer is the cost of inaction. The longer the wait, the more governance builds on foundations no one has tested, and the harder those foundations become to replace.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews The AI Revolution in Medicine: GPT-4 and Beyond by Lee et al., which explores the transformative potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) acting as symbiotic partners in healthcare. While acknowledging AI's profound ability to alleviate administrative burdens and assist in complex diagnostics, this review argues that deploying such systems requires rigorous scrutiny regarding safety, equity, and the risks of automation bias. Drawing on empirical evidence and the author's own research, the review examines the dangers of cognitive offloading, where clinicians subconsciously defer to confident but potentially inaccurate AI outputs, and the potential for AI models to exacerbate global health disparities. Finally, the paper advocates for mandated "friction" in clinical user interfaces to enforce critical human validation, while projecting a future where multimodal AI seamlessly integrates imaging and clinical records to democratize diagnostics.

title: The Formality Space: A Network Approach to the Multidimensional Structure of Informality

detail.title: The Formality Space: A Network Approach to the Multidimensional Structure of Informality
detail.abstract: Informality in developing economies constitutes a multidimensional phenomenon in which distinct attributes such as absence of registration, lack of social security coverage, low capitalisation, and precarious contracting systematically and interdependently co-occur. However, existing policy approaches often address these dimensions in isolation, overlooking the structural architecture that connects them. This concept note introduces the Formality Space, a network of co-occurrences among informality attributes at the level of productive units and individual workers, constructed using methods from network science. In this framework, nodes represent binary or categorical attributes of informality, while edges denote the conditional probability that one attribute is present given another. Eigenvector centrality is used to identify which attributes are most structurally interconnected, serving as "levers" whose resolution is most likely to trigger cascading transitions toward formality across the network. The approach is directly inspired by the Poverty Space of Stojkoski, Lopez-Calva et al. (2024) and extends that framework from multidimensional poverty to multidimensional informality. When applied to Peruvian microdata, integrating establishment-level census data with household employment surveys, the Formality Space provides a novel diagnostic tool for formalisation policy that complements conventional cost-benefit analysis by incorporating the systemic architecture of informality. To the best of the author's knowledge, this represents the first application of network complexity methods to the multidimensional measurement of informality in Latin America.

title: General-Purpose Technology and Speculative Bubble Detection
affiliations: Xiamen University, WISE and School of Economics, Xiamen University, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science (AMSS), Renmin University of China and University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

detail.title: General-Purpose Technology and Speculative Bubble Detection
detail.abstract: We show that the leading bubble test suffers severe size distortion when fundamentals incorporate general-purpose technology adoption. Embedding a hump-shaped technology shock in the Campbell-Shiller present-value model, we prove that the fundamental price becomes locally explosive during adoption, contaminating the test's limit distribution with a non-centrality parameter proportional to the shock's peak. We propose a fundamental-versus-speculative decomposition that projects prices onto observable technology proxies and applies the test to the residual. Empirically, the decomposition eliminates evidence of speculation in the 2020-2025 AI rally while confirming a speculative peak confined to December 1999-March 2000 in the dot-com episode.

title: Automating Regulatory Compliance Review in Financial Institutions Using Natural Language Processing

detail.title: Automating Regulatory Compliance Review in Financial Institutions Using Natural Language Processing
detail.abstract: Financial institutions face a growing volume of regulatory documents, guidance notes, and policy updates that must be monitored and translated into internal actions. Manual review is labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. This study examines whether natural language processing can reduce the effort involved in document intake, obligation extraction, and change-impact analysis. The workflow combines named entity recognition, sentence-level obligation classification, and semantic similarity matching to connect new regulations with existing internal policies. On a corpus of 340 regulatory documents from U.S. and EU financial regulators, the approach achieves 87.4% precision and 82.1% recall in obligation extraction and correctly maps 79% of regulatory changes to affected policy sections. The results suggest that NLP can shorten the first stage of compliance review without removing the need for human legal and compliance judgment.

title: Extracting Risk Signals from Financial Filings with Applied Natural Language Processing

detail.title: Extracting Risk Signals from Financial Filings with Applied Natural Language Processing
detail.abstract: Risk disclosures in annual reports and quarterly filings contain early signals about operational stress, litigation exposure, concentration risk, cyber incidents, and liquidity concerns. The difficulty for analysts is not access to documents but the ability to compare long disclosures quickly and consistently. This paper studies an applied natural language processing workflow for extracting and ranking risk signals from public financial filings. The workflow combines section segmentation, sentence-level risk scoring, and disclosureshift analysis to track changes in risk language across reporting periods. On a labeled sample of 4,200 filing sentences, the approach achieves 86.9% precision and 83.5% recall in identifying material risk statements. A disclosure-shift index built on the extracted sentences highlights periods where banks expand discussion of fraud losses, cybersecurity, deposit pressure, or vendor dependence. The paper is framed as analyst support rather than automated investment advice.

title: Detecting Escalation Risk in AI-Assisted Banking Conversations Using Conversation-State Signals

detail.title: Detecting Escalation Risk in AI-Assisted Banking Conversations Using Conversation-State Signals
detail.abstract: AI-assisted service channels in banking must decide not only customer intent but also when to transfer a conversation to a human specialist. Late escalation can increase customer frustration, repeat contact, and operational risk, especially when problems unfold gradually across multiple turns. This paper presents an interpretable escalation-risk workflow that combines turn-level sentence embeddings, conversation-state features, and lightweight sequence modeling. The evaluation uses publicly accessible banking intent data, complaint narratives, support-query text, and synthetic multi-turn conversation templates derived from those sources. Across both a binary escalation task and a three-level urgency task, the proposed workflow improves macro-F1 from 78.4 to 86.7 and reduces missed high-risk conversations by 23% relative to a rules-first baseline. The findings show that conversationstate modeling can materially improve escalation decisions in practical banking support operations.

title: Costly firm supervision: the impact of statutory auditors on Italian firms
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Costly firm supervision: the impact of statutory auditors on Italian firms

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1517
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the costs and benefits of firm supervision on Italian private limited companies. Using a regression discontinuity design, we estimate that being just above the thresholds for the mandatory appointment of auditors increases the likelihood of appointing auditors by 13 percentage points. For firms just above these thresholds, auditors prompted a modest strengthening of firms’ balance sheets, with the share of assets held as reserves and paid-in capital increasing marginally by 1.3 percent. Given their legal responsibility in case of insolvency, they also accelerated debt restructuring by nearly one year and temporarily reduced bankruptcies by 0.5 percentage points during the same period. However, these improvements did not translate into better access to credit or lower borrowing costs. The annual average cost of auditors per firm was 21-27 thousand euros, corresponding to around 3 percent of the labor cost for a firm with 20 employees. A cost-benefit analysis suggests that the aggregate costs of supervision outweigh its measurable benefits, particularly for smaller firms.

reference: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1518
title: Risky firms and fragile banks: implications for macroprudential policy
affiliations: Banque de France, Research Centre, Deutsche Bundesbank - Research Centre and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Risky firms and fragile banks: implications for macroprudential policy

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1518
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Based on US data, increases in firm default risk raise the probability of bank default while decreasing output and prices. To rationalize the empirical evidence, we analyze firm risk shocks using a New Keynesian model in which entrepreneurs and banks enter into a loan contract and both are subject to default risk. Corporate defaults lead to losses on banks' balance sheets. A highly leveraged banking sector exacerbates the contractionary effects of firm defaults. We estimate the parameters of the model by matching the VAR impulse responses of firm and bank risk, output, prices and the policy rate to a range of shocks -- firm risk, demand, technology and monetary policy. Our model performs well at replicating the observed dynamics, making it suitable for policy analysis. We show that high minimum capital requirements jointly implemented with a countercyclical capital buffer are effective in dampening the adverse consequences of firm risk shocks.

reference: NBER Working Paper No. w35015
title: Market Power in Mortgage Pricing: the Role of Referral Lending
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison, Cornell University - Department of Economics, University of Wisconsin at Madison and University of Wisconsin-Madison - Department of Economics

detail.title: Market Power in Mortgage Pricing: the Role of Referral Lending
detail.abstract:
Despite intense competition among mortgage lenders, borrowers face substantial price dispersion. We argue that realtor–loan officer referral networks are a key source of lender market power: by steering homebuyers toward a small set of loan officers, these networks restrict effective borrower choice even in competitive markets. Using a novel dataset linking 81,306 realtors to 102,860 loan officers across 41 states, we document that such networks are pervasive and highly concentrated — 85% of realtors direct over 40% of their clients to fewer than four loan officers — and that this concentration persists and even increases in markets with more lenders. IV estimates indicate that borrowers using referred loan officers pay 18.6 basis points higher mortgage rates, equivalent to $2,609 in upfront costs on the average loan of $306K. Referral lending raises rate spreads by 36.5% and accounts for half of the residual cross-sectional variation in spreads. The premium is nearly three times as large for Hispanic borrowers as for White borrowers, and is systematically higher for Black borrowers and financially constrained households. We identify two channels: referrals reduce borrowers' search intensity across lenders, and referred loan officers exercise pricing power relative to colleagues within the same institution. Efficiency gains from faster processing and reduced denial risk do not offset the additional costs.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

detail.title: Resilient Justice: Ukraine's Judicial Reform Amid War on the Path to EU Accession

publicationDetails.detailsText: PILPG Journal of Frontline Scholarship, 0[10.66193/02.01]

detail.abstract: This article analyzes Ukraine’s ongoing judicial reform in the context of Russia’s War of aggression and Ukraine’s pursuit of European Union (EU) membership. Since the 2014 Revolution of Dignity, the judiciary has become a central pillar of Ukraine’s democratic transformation, facing entrenched corruption, post-Soviet legacies, and fluctuating political will. The 2022 Russian invasion accelerated reform efforts, reinforcing the judiciary’s dual role in maintaining domestic justice and prosecuting war crimes. This article highlights the resilience of legal institutions and professionals working under extreme conditions. It examines how EU accession requirements, particularly the Copenhagen Criteria, have shaped Ukraine’s legal agenda and how digital innovation, civil society engagement, and international partnerships have bolstered reform. Despite war-related disruptions, Ukraine’s judiciary has demonstrated remarkable adaptability and progress. The article concludes that sustainable judicial reform is not merely technical, it is a human-driven process essential to Ukraine’s democratic future and its integration into the European legal and political community.

reference: Accepted for publication in the Scandinavian Journal of Military Studies (SJMS) (https://sjms.nu/about)
title: Autonomous Systems and the Speed of Battle: Legal Risks and Strategic Adaptation in AI-Enabled Warfare
affiliations: , National Academy of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine named after Bohdan Khmelnytskyi and National Academy of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine named after Bohdan Khmelnytskyi

detail.title: Autonomous Systems and the Speed of Battle: Legal Risks and Strategic Adaptation in AI-Enabled Warfare

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted for publication in the Scandinavian Journal of Military Studies (SJMS) (https://sjms.nu/about)

detail.abstract: This article investigates the strategic implications of deploying autonomous unmanned systems (AI-UxS) powered by artificial intelligence in contemporary military operations. It focuses on the legal and operational challenges arising from delegating critical functions to algorithms capable of independently identifying, tracking, and engaging targets without direct human oversight. The analysis highlights concern about disrupted accountability chains, vulnerabilities to cyber interference, and the risk of escalatory dynamics arising from interactions among multiple autonomous platforms. Particular attention is paid to the phenomenon of "decision-time compression," in which AI-driven systems operate on timescales that outpace human decision-making. The study examines the operational impact of uncrewed water systems (UWS) on naval warfare, emphasizing how these technologies reshape traditional concepts of maritime engagement. Rather than proposing entirely new treaties, the article argues for a strengthened interpretation of existing International Humanitarian Law (IHL) focused on the challenge of "decision-time compression." It explicitly uses the case of Uncrewed Water Systems (UWS) to demonstrate that naval autonomy necessitates new standards for meaningful human control. In support of this, the paper outlines policy recommendations to incentivize technological innovation, establish national oversight mechanisms, and promote interagency coordination. It also stresses the importance of aligning international regulatory efforts through existing platforms, including the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW), the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (GGE-LAWS), NATO, the European Commission, and AUKUS. Ultimately, the article emphasizes the importance of ensuring that the development and deployment of AI-enabled military systems align with humanitarian law in future armed conflicts.

title: AcademIQ: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Methodological Auditing of Doctoral Theses in Economics and Social Sciences

detail.title: AcademIQ: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Methodological Auditing of Doctoral Theses in Economics and Social Sciences

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest. AcademIQ is an independent academic project developed at FSEGT, Université Tunis El Manar. No financial relationship with any organization influenced this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The project was self-funded by the authors as part of their doctoral and post-doctoral research activities at FSEGT, Université Tunis El Manar, Tunisia.

detail.abstract:
The evaluation of doctoral dissertations in economics and social sciences requires deep methodological expertise, typically demanding 4 to 8 hours of expert review per thesis. Existing AI-assisted tools — including Elicit, SciSpace, and Consensus — focus exclusively on literature retrieval and summarization, leaving the critical task of methodological auditing unaddressed. We present AcademIQ, a multi-agent system that deploys 12 specialized AI agents in parallel to perform automated scientific auditing of doctoral dissertations. The system produces a normalized AcademIQ Score (0–100) across seven dimensions — structural coherence, theoretical framework, methodology, empirical credibility, scientific contribution, academic integrity, and publication readiness — alongside a formal Q1-style referee report. An Econometric Judge module detects violations of established protocols (Hausman, Pesaran CD, AR(2), Sargan, Westerlund) and applies discipline-calibrated penalties. Validated on five doctoral theses across economics, finance, medicine, machine learning, and history in the MENA region, AcademIQ reduces analysis time from 4 hours to under 20 minutes. To our knowledge, this is the first system to perform critical methodological auditing — rather than mere summarization — of academic dissertations.

Note: This version is an abridged preprint intended to establish authorship priority and summarize empirical validation results. Detailed technical specifications of the Econometric Judge module, Self-Resilience layer, document processing pipeline, cache architecture, and real statistical computation modules have been redacted pending intellectual property review. A full technical description will be made available upon peer-reviewed publication.

reference: CEIS Working Paper No. 620
title: The Misallocation Costs of Inflation: A Sufficient Statistics Approach
affiliations: University of Mannheim, University of Rome Tor Vergata - Department of Economics and Finance and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: The Misallocation Costs of Inflation: A Sufficient Statistics Approach

publicationDetails.journalName: CEIS: Centre for Economic & International Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The misallocation costs associated with different aggregate inflation rates can be estimated from micro price data via a set of sufficient statistics. We show that this works for a broad class of price-setting models and in the presence of unobserved product-level heterogeneity in pricing frictions and flexible prices. Applying the sufficient statistics approach to the micro price data underlying the U.K. consumer price index, we find large misallocation costs: aggregate productivity falls by about 1% if aggregate inflation is 8 percentage points above or below its optimal rate of 1.8%. Our findings provide important lessons for the calibration of sticky-price models: standard calibration targets can be uninformative about the sufficient statistics characterizing misallocation costs. To correctly capture these costs, models should be directly calibrated to the sufficient statistics that we uncover. JEL Class. No.: E31, E58 * We thank Yvette Agape for valuable research assistance. Klaus Adam acknowledges support from the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft through CRC-TR 224 (Project C02). The opinions expressed in this paper are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Deutsche Bundesbank or the Eurosystem.
