detail.abstract: Despite progress in the adoption of sanitary pads, use of cloth as an absorbent remains in vogueparticularly in rural India. In this paper we argue that shared concern about reproductive health beyond price incentive is instrumental in the adoption of hygienic menstrual products. We posit that more open discussion between male and females in the household regarding household expenditure and problems of menstruation, will lead to better use of hygienic methods of menstrual practices. We conducted couple survey of about 500 households to see that to what extent the use of hygienic menstrual products is influenced by the demographic, cultural factors of the household and how inter-partner discourse, male participation in household chores, can influence the use of sanitary pad. We found that controlling for education, age and family income, use of sanitary pads is more likely for the families where women are openly discussing period issues with male. We also found that more male participation in sharing household chores leading to better menstrual management.

title: The Global Economic Impact of the 2026 Iran-US War: A Hybrid Time-Series and Comparative Cross-Country Analysis and Modelling
affiliations: Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, Akenten Appiah-Menka University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development. Akenten Appiah-Menka University of Skills Training den Entrepreneurial Development,, University of Bradford and Transilvania University of Brasov

detail.title: The Global Economic Impact of the 2026 Iran-US War: A Hybrid Time-Series and Comparative Cross-Country Analysis and Modelling

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Human Ethics, Consent to Participate, and Consent to Publish: Human Ethics, Consent to Participate, and Consent to Publish: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Background: The United States-Israel military operation against Iran, launched on 28 February 2026 and codenamed Operation Epic Fury, triggered the most significant global energy security disruption since the 1970s oil embargo. The near-total blockade of the Strait of Hormuz-through which approximately 20 million barrels per day of crude oil and one-fifth of global liquefied natural gas (LNG) trade transit-generated cascading macroeconomic shocks across commodity, financial, and food markets worldwide. Methods: This study employs a hybrid research design combining event-driven time-series analysis with comparative cross-sectional analysis covering 19 economies and the World aggregate. Five novel econometric models are proposed and calibrated to the observed data: (1) the Multi-Commodity Contagion Index (MCCI), a composite time-series shock index; (2) the Hormuz Chokepoint Vulnerability Index (HCVI), a crosscountry Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression framework; (3) the Geopolitical Stagflation Surface (GSS), a nonlinear bivariate response surface; (4) the Threshold Structural Break Model (TSBM), applying Bai-Perron structural break detection to the oil risk premium series; and (5) the Cascading Supply-Chain Amplification Model (CSCAM), an input-output network multiplier framework. Results: Brent crude oil prices surged 55.3% from $72.48 to $112.57 per barrel within one month. The MCCI peaked at 100 on 27 March 2026, revealing an escalation-to-abatement velocity ratio of 22:1. The HCVI OLS regression explains 84.7% of crosscountry gross domestic product (GDP) revision variance (R² = 0.847, N = 18 excluding structural outlier Iran). The TSBM identifies three structural breaks and a permanently elevated post-ceasefire risk premium of $24/bbl. The CSCAM estimates an aggregate global amplification multiplier of $3.20 GDP loss per $1 of chokepoint disruption. Conclusions: The 2026 Iran-US war constitutes a compound geopolitical-economic shock with asymmetric regional consequences and a multi-commodity contagion architecture unprecedented in modern economic history. The novel models developed here provide a replicable framework for realtime assessment of future Hormuz disruption scenarios and broader geopolitical supply chain crises.

title: LLMs Are Not Polymaths and Reconciliation at the Seams Still Needs Humans

detail.title: LLMs Are Not Polymaths and Reconciliation at the Seams Still Needs Humans

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None

detail.abstract: This paper studies two epistemic actors: the large language model 𝑀 and the Expert 𝐸. The question is not whether 𝑀 can produce plausible interdisciplinary language; it plainly can. The question is whether 𝑀 can replace 𝐸 as a terminal arbiter at the seams where one domain's verified claims are translated into another domain's admissible judgments. The answer developed here is no, except in the degenerate case in which the model's internal information partition is already fine enough to separate the expert's decisive target classes.

title: Brain drain on the fast train: high-speed connections and student mobility
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Università di Firenze and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Brain drain on the fast train: high-speed connections and student mobility

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1519
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines the effects of improved connectivity on internal student mobility, focusing on the staggered expansion of Italy’s high-speed trains (HST) network between 2010 and 2019. Using administrative data on university enrollments and a difference-in-differences design that accounts for variation in treatment timing, we find that the introduction of an HST stop leads to a significant increase in student outflows from treated provinces, with no corresponding rise in inflows. The effect is concentrated in Southern regions and driven by long-distance relocations, particularly toward larger urban centers. These findings suggest that extending high-speed train service may contribute to the spatial reallocation of human capital away from the newly connected, more peripheral areas, reinforcing existing regional disparities in talent distribution.

title: AI in asset Pricing and Investment Strategies.

detail.title: AI in asset Pricing and Investment Strategies.
detail.abstract: This research explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into traditional asset pricing models and investment strategies , focusing on whether Ai acts as a replacement or a complement to human financial analysis abilities. While traditional models like the Capital asset pricing Model (CAPM) rely on linear assumptions , AI and specifically machine learning , allows for the processing of non-linear data. This study examines the synergy between algorithmic precision and historical market wisdom , using a quantitative framework to measure performance enhancements in diversified portfolios. The result indicates that while AI excels at short-term pattern recognition and risk qualification , it requires the foundational stability of traditional assets and human oversight during systematic shocks (Market risk) .

title: Money Follows Power: Political Turnover and Private Investment in Infrastructure
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley - Accounting Group,  and

detail.title: Money Follows Power: Political Turnover and Private Investment in Infrastructure
detail.abstract: This paper studies how political turnover affects private investment in infrastructure in Chinese cities. We match the universe of Ministry of Finance infrastructure contracts with private participation to all mayoral appointments, exits, and inter-city transfers between 2018 and 2022. Through a mayor-firm network, we develop continuous measures of political connection and bias. Using multi-period difference-in-differences estimation, we show that mayoral replacement significantly increases contract failures. The effects are stronger when the outgoing mayor is not promoted and when the mayor's contracting portfolio is more concentrated, suggesting greater reliance on relationship-based contracting and hence larger disruption upon turnover. We further show that political turnover reduces renegotiation and increases formal disputes, consistent with a shift from informal, relationship-based enforcement to formal, rule-based conflict resolution. We also document a robust pattern of spatial portability in which private capital and firms follow officials' transfers, consistent with a "money follows power" pattern. Using project internal rates of return (IRR), we show that turnover-induced failures are selective: less biased incoming mayors disproportionately terminate high-IRR, low-efficiency projects, whereas biased mayors generate broader disruptions that also affect relatively efficient projects. We develop a dynamic structural model of contract continuation, renegotiation, litigation, and relational reallocation, and estimate it by indirect inference targeting the reduced-form moments. Counterfactual analysis shows that eliminating biased succession raises welfare by 3.2 percent, while eliminating turnover entirely reduces welfare by 1.8 percent, implying that turnover's disciplinary function outweighs its disruption costs. The welfare-maximizing rotation frequency corresponds to an average tenure of 3.7 years, longer than the observed 2.7 years.

title: Financial Market Opacity and Systemic Liquidity Risk
affiliations: Saint Louis University - Richard A. Chaifetz School of Business, Indian Institute of Management Udaipur and Universidad de las Islas Baleares

detail.title: Financial Market Opacity and Systemic Liquidity Risk
detail.abstract: We examine whether the growth of dark trading in U.S. equity markets alters liquidity commonality, a key dimension of systemic risk. Using FINRA dark pool transparency data from 2014-2020 and 172,229 firm-quarter observations, we relate commonality measures constructed from multiple liquidity proxies to dark pool activity. Pooled and fixed-effects regressions as well as instrumental variable regressions show that higher dark trading significantly reduces commonality, especially for larger (Tier 1) stocks. Our results suggest that despite greater opacity, dark pools may dampen the transmission of liquidity shocks across lit markets and thus have a potentially stabilizing systemic effect.

title: From Point Estimates to Probabilistic Valuation

detail.title: From Point Estimates to Probabilistic Valuation
detail.abstract: This working paper proposes a practical way to communicate valuation uncertainty in real estate by applying Monte Carlo simulation to discounted cash flow (DCF) models. Instead of treating market value as a single figure, it reports a distribution of plausible values at the valuation date, alongside decision-useful statistics (e.g., P50 and percentile intervals). The framework is designed for professional use: valuers evidence and parameterise uncertainty through bounded input distributions (including explicit dependency assumptions), while governance bodies can make any required point selection for reporting explicit and documented. The paper also provides a reporting template (outputs and minimum disclosures) and a limitations section that clarifies what the ranges do-and do not-mean in practice.

title: International Patent Protection under Climate Policy

detail.title: International Patent Protection under Climate Policy
detail.abstract: How will climate change affect intellectual property rights (IPR) enforcement and what does this imply for unilaterally optimal climate policy? I develop a North-South model with carbon taxation and endogenous innovation in a clean and a dirty sector, in which both countries enforce IPR endogenously. I find that (1) in the presence of climate damages, domestic IPR enforcement can be both a strategic substitute and a complement to foreign enforcement, (2) climate change may have a significant influence on the evolution of IPR protection, lowering the regions' willingness to enforce patents except if innovation in the clean sector is much more productive than in the dirty sector, (3) endogenous IPR protection may imply substantially higher optimal carbon taxation than under a fixed enforcement regime, especially when tax policy is unilateral and (4) environmental tax policy may increase the gains from international cooperation on IPR enforcement.

title: SkillSphere: A Local Skill Exchange Platform for Communities

detail.title: SkillSphere: A Local Skill Exchange Platform for Communities
detail.abstract: SkillSphere is a web-based system designed to advance local community development through tailored skill exchange and collaborative learning. This survey paper presents a comprehensive review of SkillSphere's conceptual foundations, technical architecture, and operational practices, emphasizing its potential to address gaps in decentralized education and lifelong learning. The platform enables users to develop detailed personal profiles conveying both skill offerings and learning interests. Location-aware intelligent matching algorithms connect users directly for skill-sharing interactions via built-in, secure messaging and scheduling features. In addition to facilitating one-on-one and group learning sessions, SkillSphere incorporates milestone tracking, robust user reputation management via verified credentials, and detailed review mechanisms to enhance reliability, transparency, and trust. This paper analyzes survey data and case studies from pilot deployments across diverse urban and peri-urban communities, highlighting how algorithmic matching and user-driven content curation support effective skill exchange and increase participation. Implementation experiences underscore critical challenges-such as technology adoption barriers, content moderation, and incentivization models-alongside opportunities for scaling through network effects and community partnerships. The survey discusses SkillSphere's contribution to the literature on peer-to-peer learning, reviews the impact of its design choices on user engagement, and synthesizes feedback from both early adopters and platform managers. Based on empirical evidence, actionable recommendations are provided regarding platform architecture, user onboarding, reputation systems, and future directions including mobile integration and AI-driven skill assessment. Ultimately, SkillSphere demonstrates that local skill-sharing platforms can significantly strengthen social capital, accelerate knowledge dissemination, and provide flexible, cost-effective alternatives to conventional educational models within community settings.

title: Dari Pengurusan ke Pelanggan: Platform Ulasan Digital sebagai Mekanisme Kawalan dan Pendisiplinan Pekerja dalam Industri Hospitaliti -Sintesis Global dan Analisis Kontekstual Sabah, Malaysia NUR ANISAH BINTI ABD MUTALIP @ TALIP

detail.title: Dari Pengurusan ke Pelanggan: Platform Ulasan Digital sebagai Mekanisme Kawalan dan Pendisiplinan Pekerja dalam Industri Hospitaliti -Sintesis Global dan Analisis Kontekstual Sabah, Malaysia NUR ANISAH BINTI ABD MUTALIP @ TALIP
detail.abstract:
Transformasi digital dalam industri hospitaliti telah mengubah secara fundamental hubungan kuasa antara majikan, pekerja, dan pelanggan. Platform ulasan seperti TripAdvisor, Agoda, dan Booking.com tidak lagi berfungsi semata-mata sebagai medium maklum balas pengguna, tetapi sebagai mekanisme kawalan buruh yang beroperasi secara tidak formal. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis literatur global dan serantau bagi memahami bagaimana sistem penarafan pelanggan bertindak sebagai alat pendisiplinan pekerja serta mendedahkan mereka kepada diskriminasi dan eksploitasi tanpa perlindungan institusi yang mencukupi.
Pendekatan ulasan naratif digunakan dengan analisis tematik berdasarkan Braun dan Clarke (2006), melibatkan kajian dari 2014 hingga 2025. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa platform digital telah memperkukuh fenomena “algorithmic management”, meningkatkan dominasi pelanggan sebagai agen kawalan, melemahkan peranan institusi buruh, dan menimbulkan kekosongan regulatori. Dalam konteks Sabah, kebergantungan tinggi kepada sektor pelancongan digital memperlihatkan pekerja garis hadapan menghadapi tekanan emosi, ketidakstabilan pekerjaan, dan risiko penilaian berat sebelah.
Kesimpulannya, tanpa reformasi dasar dan intervensi institusi, sistem ulasan digital akan terus memperluas ketidakseimbangan kuasa dalam industri hospitaliti. Artikel ini mencadangkan pembentukan kerangka perlindungan pekerja yang lebih inklusif, telus, dan berasaskan keadilan sosial.

declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This study analyzes the local economic effects of stagflation in Valledupar, Colombia, during the period 2020-2022. Stagflation, defined as the simultaneous occurrence of inflation, economic stagnation, and labor market deterioration, represents a significant challenge for regional economic stability and development. The research adopts a quantitative approach with a non-experimental, cross-sectional design. Data were collected through structured surveys applied to 100 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), allowing for the integration of both economic indicators and business perceptions. The findings reveal a significant decline in purchasing power, increased levels of indebtedness, reduced income, and limitations in productive capacity. Additionally, structural factors such as low economic diversification, dependence on traditional sectors, and labor market rigidity were identified as key elements that intensify the effects of stagflation. The study concludes that stagflation in Valledupar is not solely the result of external shocks but is also strongly linked to internal structural weaknesses, highlighting the need for adaptive economic policies and strategies aimed at strengthening local resilience.

title: The growth of digital payment in india

detail.title: The growth of digital payment in india
detail.abstract:
The rapid growth of digital payments in India represents one of the most significant 
transformations in the country’s financial ecosystem over the past decade. Driven by
technological advancements, supportive government policies, financial inclusion initiatives, and 
the widespread adoption of smartphones and internet connectivity, digital payments have
reshaped how individuals, businesses, and institutions conduct financial transactions. This 
abstract provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution, drivers, impact, challenges, and 
future prospects of digital payments in India.
India’s transition from a predominantly cash-based economy to a digitally empowered financial 
system gained momentum particularly after 2016, when the government introduced 
demonetization and accelerated initiatives under the Digital India mission. These efforts
encouraged citizens to adopt electronic payment methods and reduced dependency on cash 
transactions. Over time, the development of robust digital infrastructure, including Aadhaar-
enabled systems, Jan Dhan bank accounts, and mobile connectivity, created a strong foundation 
for the growth of digital payments.
A major breakthrough in India’s digital payment ecosystem was the introduction of the Unified 
Payments Interface (UPI) in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). UPI 
revolutionized the payment landscape by enabling real-time, seamless, and interoperable
transactions between bank accounts using mobile devices. Its simplicity, speed, and zero-cost 
structure significantly contributed to its widespread adoption. Over the years, UPI has emerged 
as the dominant digital payment method in India. By 2024–25, UPI accounted for more than 
80% of the total digital payment volume in the country, reflecting its massive penetration and 
popularity.
The growth trajectory of digital payments in India has been remarkable. The volume of digital 
transactions has in
creased exponentially, reaching over 200 billion transactions.

title: Government-Regulated Direct-to-Consumer Pharmaceutical Distribution and Pricing Portal: A Policy and Technical Framework for Affordable Medicine Access

detail.title: Government-Regulated Direct-to-Consumer Pharmaceutical Distribution and Pricing Portal: A Policy and Technical Framework for Affordable Medicine Access

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, clinical trials, or patient data, and therefore did not require ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted as part of an academic course requirement.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This study does not involve any clinical trials.

detail.abstract:
The pharmaceutical distribution system in many developing economies is characterized by multi-layered supply chains, price opacity, and high trade margins that significantly increase out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure for consumers. In India, despite the presence of price regulation mechanisms and generic medicine initiatives, retail drug prices often remain substantially higher than manufacturing costs due to intermediaries such as stockists, distributors, and retailers. This research explores the concept of a Government-Regulated Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) pharmaceutical distribution and pricing portal designed to reduce medicine costs through trade margin rationalization, price transparency, and centralized procurement. 
The study examines the transition from traditional retail pharmaceutical distribution systems to a government-backed digital distribution model where medicines are procured directly from manufacturers, quality-verified through regulatory bodies, and sold to citizens via an online government platform or authorized distribution centers. The research also evaluates the role of the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) and the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), which has expanded to over 18,000 centers by 2026, in improving affordability and access to medicines. 
Using comparative price analysis, supply chain modeling, and policy analysis, this research proposes a government-regulated D2C pricing portal as a policy framework that may reduce medicine prices by approximately 50–60% based on simulation assumptions, improve transparency, and ensure drug quality through blockchain tracking and QR-based authentication

title: Mathematics of Derivative Pricing: A Comprehensive Object-Oriented Framework for Valuation and Strategy

detail.title: Mathematics of Derivative Pricing: A Comprehensive Object-Oriented Framework for Valuation and Strategy
detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive mathematical treatment of derivative pricing, spanning the full arc from foundational interest rate theory and fixed-income mathematics through advanced stochastic calculus and practical trading strategy construction. Beginning with the mechanics of financial markets, compounding conventions, and term structure theory, the exposition progresses systematically through cash flow valuation, bond pricing, Macaulay and modified duration, and forward rate bootstrapping from the yield curve. Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) is examined in depth, including the Markowitz mean-variance framework, efficient frontier construction, and three distinct optimization objectives-Sharpe ratio maximization yielding annualised return of 52.59% with volatility 50.05% and Sharpe 1.0507, return maximization under risk constraints (55.25%/52.67%/1.0490), and minimum variance portfolio (18.08%/25.50%/0.5911)-applied to a seven-stock NASDAQ universe. The paper derives no-arbitrage forward and futures pricing under both continuous dividend yields and discrete dividends, examines cost-of-carry relationships, contango and backwardation, mark-tomarket mechanics, and constructs optimal futures hedges using the minimum variance hedge ratio. Option theory is developed rigorously: put-call parity, premium bounds with arbitrage proofs, and a complete step-by-step derivation of the Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) PDE via Itô's Lemma and delta-neutral hedging, followed by an independent derivation via the risk-neutral (martingale) pricing approach under Girsanov's measure change. The Cox-Ross-Rubinstein Binomial Model is derived and shown to converge to BSM as N → ∞. All five option Greeks-Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, and Rho-are presented in closed form. Discrete-time Greek approximations from the binomial lattice are also established. Numerical methods including Monte Carlo simulation (converging to ≈ 10.50), BSM closed form (10.45), and explicit finite difference PDE solution (≈ 10.45) are compared. Practical option strategies-Bull Call Spread, Bear Put Spread, Long Straddle, Long Strangle, Butterfly Spread, and Iron Condor-are analysed with full payoff functions, Greek profiles, and scenario tables at spot prices S ∈ {85, 100, 115}. All results are implemented in Python using Geometric Brownian Motion simulation, Monte Carlo methods, and finite difference solvers, with empirical validation using NSE and NASDAQ historical data.

title: Assessing the impact of digital finance on inequality, poverty and carbon emissions in developing Asian countries using structural equation model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and International Islamic University Chittagong

detail.title: Assessing the impact of digital finance on inequality, poverty and carbon emissions in developing Asian countries using structural equation model
detail.abstract: In this paper, considers the relationships between digital financial services in particular, account ownership, saving, and borrowing and three sustainable development goals: poverty (SDG 1), income inequality (SDG 10), and CO2 emissions (SDG 13). It analyzes the relationships between 25 developing Asian nations between 2011 and 2021 and uses structural equation modeling (SEM) and subsequent regression-based robustness checking to determine both direct and indirect relationships with account ownership, saving, and borrowing being the mediating channels of financial inclusion. The results suggest that high utilization of the digital payments correlates with reduced income inequality and increased consumption spending in households, especially in the environment with a wider access to financial services. Meanwhile, the use of digital payments has a positive correlation with CO2 emissions, which is in line with the rise in energy consumption associated with digital infrastructure. Nonetheless, the channels of financial inclusion account ownership, saving and borrowing are mediated by these environmental pressures to a certain degree and are related to more sustainable patterns of consumption and investment. To the best of our knowledge, this study is among the first to jointly examine these multidimensional direct and indirect associations between digital finance, inequality, poverty-related outcomes, and environmental sustainability in developing Asia. The results underscore the relevance of integrated financial inclusion and environmental responsibility policies and may inform the design of targeted interventions such as support for low-income digital users and incentives for green financial products aimed at aligning digital finance with equitable and sustainable development objectives.

title: Cost Pass-Through, Price Competition, and Market Power in Brick-and-Mortar Pharmacies: Evidence from Germany

detail.title: Cost Pass-Through, Price Competition, and Market Power in Brick-and-Mortar Pharmacies: Evidence from Germany

declarations.funderStatement: The Pharmacists Association Westfalen-Lippe (AVWL) and pharmacists’ co-operative NOWEDA are funding a research project at the Chair of Georg Götz. The study is a product of this project. The project itself was scientific in nature (i. e., no commercial research project).

detail.abstract: In the German pharmacy market, strictly regulated prescription (Rx) drug prices coexist with free pricing for over-the-counter (OTC) drugs. This paper investigates the extent of market power in the non-prescription segment (OTC drugs and non-pharmaceuticals) and explores the role of Rx drugs in facilitating this. Leveraging nearly a billion daily observations from over 6,300 pharmacies and 213,000 products (2018-2022), this study estimates wholesale-to-retail pass-through rates via an error correction model (ECM) and analyzes product-level markups (Lerner Indices). Results reveal asymmetric pass-through (rockets and feathers): retail prices adjust to cost increases faster than decreases, a dynamic driven by niche products while bestsellers exhibit pricing inertia. Long-run pass-through rates (1.3-1.7) indicate systematic cost overshifting. However, while OTC drugs sustain high long-run markups-corroborated by Lerner Indices that are 35 % higher than those of non-pharmaceuticals-non-pharmaceuticals face more competitive pricing dynamics, passing through cost decreases more aggressively than increases. Furthermore, a spatial analysis reveals that rural pharmacies exhibit higher long-run pass-through rates and appear to compensate for lower transaction volumes (-7.6 %) with markups 8.3 % higher than urban competitors, effectively nullifying aggregate gross profit differences. These spatial dynamics are characterized by rural pharmacies exhibiting greater short-run pricing inertia, followed by stronger long-run pass-through. The findings suggest that pharmacies leverage the regulated Rx segment to facilitate higher markups and systematic overshifting. Consequently, the financial viability of rural networks relies partially on this cross-subsidization from Rx drugs, a model facing risks from increasing digitization.

title: The Operational Trilemma of Production Generative AI: Quality, Latency, and Safety Cannot All Win

detail.title: The Operational Trilemma of Production Generative AI: Quality, Latency, and Safety Cannot All Win

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed at Snap Inc. The observations and framework presented in this paper are based on the author's professional experience and do not represent the views or proprietary information of Snap Inc.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding. This research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Production deployment of generative AI systems at consumer scale reveals a persistent structural conflict between three operational dimensions: output quality, response latency, and content safety. Unlike the academic literature's focus on model performance optimization, this paper documents the practitioner's problem: how to make capable models reliable, fast, and safe simultaneously in systems processing millions of real-time requests. Drawing on firsthand experience building and shipping generative video and augmented reality products, this paper argues that quality, latency, and safety form an optimization trilemma under fixed resource constraints-and that recognizing this trilemma as structural rather than solvable is the foundation of sound production AI architecture. We describe the practical mechanisms of this conflict, document evaluation failures that occur when teams optimize offline metrics, present a layered safety architecture that aims to reduce false positives while maintaining detection coverage, and derive six operational principles from production deployment. This is not a theoretical contribution but a structured practitioner account of problems and solutions that are poorly represented in published literature.

title: Value Creation Chain Tokenization as a Structural Response to the Challenges of Technological Civilization

detail.title: Value Creation Chain Tokenization as a Structural Response to the Challenges of Technological Civilization
detail.abstract:
Most discussions of real-world asset tokenization revolve around the question of how. How is the smart contract structured. How does the oracle work. How does the regulator classify a digital asset. How does one attract an investor.

These are important questions. But they are secondary to another — to the question of why. Why now, why in this particular form, why with such a persistent intuition that this is not merely another financial product but something structurally different?

Answering that question requires stepping outside the boundaries of financial engineering — into the domain where economics meets the philosophy of technology. The philosophy of technology is not a metaphor or an ornament. It is an attempt to understand what specific problem a given instrument is designed to solve, whether this problem is genuinely new or reproduces a deeper historical pattern, and what will change in the relations among people if the instrument achieves mass adoption. It is precisely this inquiry that forms the subject of the present paper.

title: The Dynamic Exchange of Entropy: A Unified Physical Foundation for Economics From Entropic Dashboard to Entropic Exchange Process

detail.title: The Dynamic Exchange of Entropy: A Unified Physical Foundation for Economics From Entropic Dashboard to Entropic Exchange Process
detail.abstract: Previous work defined the economy as the entropic dashboard of a society, treating the state of the economy as an indicator of whether entropy is balanced or accumulated. This paper corrects and extends that definition. The economy is not entropy itself. The economy is the dynamic exchange of entropy across agents, regions, and time. Production transforms disordered raw materials into ordered products, which is local entropy reduction. Consumption degrades ordered products into disordered waste, which is local entropy increase. Trade transfers entropy-reducing resources from surplus agents to deficit agents, which is entropy exchange. Migration moves labor as entropy-reducing capacity from low-productivity regions to high-productivity regions, which is also entropy exchange. Institutional reform breaks down barriers that block entropy exchange, which increases entropy exchange efficiency. This paper argues that all economic phenomena, including production, consumption, trade, migration, price formation, market competition, monopoly, regulation, and macroeconomic fluctuations, can be understood as particular forms of the dynamic exchange of entropy. Economic prosperity occurs when entropy exchange efficiency is high, entropy accumulation is low, and circulation is fast. Economic decline occurs when entropy exchange efficiency is low, entropy accumulation is high, and circulation is blocked. The paper reinterprets the entropic theorem of economic externalities, the four-stage cycle of national rise and fall, the structure of social classes, and the role of hidden resources within this corrected framework. It concludes that the dynamic exchange of entropy provides a unified physical foundation for economics, grounding the discipline in the second law of thermodynamics and connecting economic phenomena to the same physical laws that govern all other natural processes.

title: The Entropic Dynamics of National Rise and Fall A Macro-Historical Extension of the Entropic Theorem of Economic Externalities

detail.title: The Entropic Dynamics of National Rise and Fall A Macro-Historical Extension of the Entropic Theorem of Economic Externalities
detail.abstract: The Entropic Theorem of Economic Externalities, proposed in previous work, establishes that positive externalities are local entropy reduction, negative externalities are local entropy increase, and the fundamental function of economic circulation is entropy equalization through the cross-agent exchange of entropy-reducing resources. This paper extends that theorem from the micro-economic and meso-economic levels to the macro-historical level of national rise and fall. The core proposition is that the economy of a society, a nation, or a group is the primary indicator of its entropic state. When an economy functions well, entropy is balanced and stable. Local entropy reduction matches or exceeds local entropy increase, and the society experiences prosperity and peace. When an economy deteriorates, the entropic state becomes disorganized. Local entropy increase accumulates and eventually exceeds total entropy reduction, leading to social unrest, war, and national collapse. The paper argues that war and national destruction are not the disappearance of entropy but a forced reallocation of entropy-reducing resources. Using the case of historical floods in ancient China's Jiangnan region, the paper illustrates how a local natural disaster destroys entropy-reducing resources, halts entropy exchange efficiency, triggers local entropy increase (famine, disease, death), and then spreads entropy disorder through supply chains, population displacement, and fiscal collapse. When the entropic disorder reaches a critical threshold, the social system's spontaneous entropy-balancing mechanism fails. War or revolution becomes the only channel for forced entropy release. The paper further shows that the collapse of an old regime and the emergence of a new one follow a four-stage entropic cycle: local entropy increase triggered by natural or human-made disasters, spread of entropy disorder to the whole system, critical collapse and forced entropy reallocation through war, and the establishment of a new entropy-balancing system with a new economy. This cycle explains the dynastic cycle of imperial China and, more generally, the rise and fall of civilizations. The paper concludes that the entropic theorem of economic externalities, when extended to the macro-historical scale, provides a unified physical explanation for national prosperity, social stability, war, collapse, and the rebirth of economies.

title: An Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) framework for artist ranking: evidence from an art gallery in Italy
affiliations: Ca Foscari University of Venice - Department of Management, Ca Foscari University of Venice - Dipartimento di Economia and Ca’ Foscari University of Venice

detail.title: An Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) framework for artist ranking: evidence from an art gallery in Italy

publicationDetails.detailsText: Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics Research Paper Series No. 15/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: Department of Economics, Ca' Foscari University of Venice Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Art evaluation is a longstanding challenge mainly due to its multidimensional nature. In recent decades, the expansion of online art markets and the increasing interest in art as an asset class have intensified the demand for transparent, systematic tools for art assessment. Existing artist rankings are widely used, but often rely on opaque logics and embedded biases. This research introduces a structured framework for building artist rankings through Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA), specifically the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). To assess its feasibility, we conducted a case study using data from an art gallery in Trento, Italy. Our findings indicate that this approach improves transparency and interpretability, while balancing both quantitative indicators and expert judgements. Moreover, the framework is flexible and adaptable to specific objectives and various artistic contexts.

title: Empirical validation of Market Resonance Theory (MRT 5590670)

detail.title: Empirical validation of Market Resonance Theory (MRT 5590670)
detail.abstract:
This paper presents the empirical validation of Market Resonance Theory (MRT), a framework originally proposed by LJ Parsons in 2018 positing that financial markets operate as structured multiplicative recursive systems governed by harmonic frequency relationships analogous to the equal temperament tuning systems.

Building on the theoretical foundation established in the original thesis, this paper formalises the mathematical derivation of the MRT harmonic grid - a price level lattice anchored to the note C in the 432 Hz equal temperament tuning system - and presents systematic empirical evidence of its governing influence across multiple asset classes and timeframes.

Empirical analysis of gold spanning 1971 to 2026, Bitcoin across its entire price history, and the US Dollar Index across two decades demonstrates that pre-calculated harmonic levels and Resonant Frequency Zones consistently define the structural boundaries of market behaviour — including major turning points, consolidation ranges, breakout levels, and support and resistance transitions, with a precision and consistency that conventional analytical frameworks fail to replicate or explain.

Furthermore this paper demonstrates that the harmonic architecture exhibits fractal self-similarity across all observable timeframes, from multi-decade annual structure down to single minute intraday price action, providing direct empirical confirmation of the recursive multiplicatory behaviour proposed in the original theoretical framework.

The findings have significant implications for the understanding of price as a structural phenomenon and invite fundamental re-examination of the conventional price discovery model.

title:
The Entropic Nature of Hidden Resources

From Institutional Blockage to Entropy Exchange

detail.title:
The Entropic Nature of Hidden Resources

From Institutional Blockage to Entropy Exchange
detail.abstract: Previous work in this series has developed two distinct but related frameworks. The first is the economics of hidden resources, which argues that resources such as the sex industry and gambling are not inherently problematic but are blocked from formal circulation by legal, moral, and institutional barriers. The second is the entropic theorem of economic externalities, which argues that economic circulation is the dynamic exchange of entropy and that institutional blockage creates entropy accumulation. This paper integrates these two frameworks into a single unified theory. The core proposition is that hidden resources are entropy-regulating carriers that have been institutionally blocked. Their blockage creates two distinct problems. First, the entropic potential for entropy reduction is trapped in the hands of a few, creating entropy accumulation through hoarding. Second, the demand for entropy reduction continues to exist, and when it cannot find a legal channel, it creates uncontrolled local entropy increase, including individual psychological distress, social disorder, and underground violence. The paper argues that the activation of hidden resources through legalization, regulation, and taxation is not merely about capturing economic value. It is about unblocking entropy exchange. Using the examples of sexual desire and gambling, the paper shows that these are basic human needs that must be released. When they are suppressed, entropy accumulates in the individual, leading to psychological disorder, crime, and social harm. When they are released through regulated channels, entropy is reduced for the individual, and the economic transaction produces value for the system. The paper further argues that the release of hidden resources can produce longterm entropy reduction through reproduction. A satisfied individual may form a family and raise children, who are themselves low-entropy resources with future productive potential. This extends the entropic benefit from immediate entropy reduction to intergenerational entropy maintenance. The paper concludes that hidden resources are not a special category. They are entropy-reducing resources that have been artificially blocked. Their activation is entropy unblocking.

title: Social Stratification as Entropy Accumulation

detail.title: Social Stratification as Entropy Accumulation
detail.abstract: Traditional theories of social stratification classify individuals and groups by occupation, income, wealth, or status. These classifications describe surface characteristics but do not explain the underlying mechanism that generates and reproduces inequality. This paper proposes an alternative framework based on the entropic theory of economic exchange developed in previous work. The core proposition is that social class is determined by the weight of entropy accumulation. The lower class consists of individuals whose only entropy-reducing resource is their labor. They provide immediate entropy reduction through work but cannot accumulate entropy surplus. The middle class consists of individuals who have accumulated entropy through trade, commerce, or professional skills. Their wealth is stored entropy. The upper class consists of individuals who control not only accumulated entropy but also the power to redirect entropy flows through policy, regulation, and institutional design. Their power is potential entropy accumulation: the capacity to convert influence into wealth, to transfer entropy from one group to another, and to shape the rules of entropy exchange itself. The paper argues that the distinction between wealth and power is entropically superficial. Wealth is actualized entropy accumulation. Power is potential entropy accumulation. The upper class holds both. The paper further argues that policy is the mechanism through which entropy is forcibly transferred between classes. Taxation, regulation, legalization, and prohibition are all forms of entropy redistribution. They can transfer entropy from the rich to the poor or from the poor to the rich. The entropic framework provides a unified physical explanation for class formation, class reproduction, and class struggle.

title: Macroeconomic impact of the 2026 Iranian oil shock: A BGVAR model analysis
affiliations: TAC Economics, TAC Economics and TAC Economics

detail.title: Macroeconomic impact of the 2026 Iranian oil shock: A BGVAR model analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper quanties the global macroeconomic eects of the oil price shock triggered by the February 2026 Iran conict. Utilizing a Bayesian Global Vector Autoregressive (BGVAR) model covering 14 major economies (4 mature and 10 emerging markets), we simulate the transmission of oil prices to global ination, GDP growth and interest rates. In a departure from standard endogenous frameworks, this model treats Brent crude as an exogenous variable, ensuring that the energy shock remains independent of model-driven demand uctuations to accurately represent the Iran shock. We evaluate three distinct paths, normalization, persistence, and breakdown, to account for the conict's uncertain duration and provide a comprehensive sensitivity analysis of global economic resilience. The results indicate substantial but dierentiated eects: while commodity-importing advanced economies face persistent inationary pressure, commodity exporters experience distinct responses reecting their structural positions in energy markets.

title: War and Peace Are One An Entropic Theorem of Social Equilibrium

detail.title: War and Peace Are One An Entropic Theorem of Social Equilibrium
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a theorem that unifies war and peace under a single entropic framework. The core proposition is that war is peace and peace is war. War is the violent reconstruction of entropy equilibrium. Peace is the temporary state of entropy equilibrium that inevitably generates the conditions for its own destruction. Using concepts developed in previous work-entropy equilibrium, entropy accumulation, entropy fracture, and entropy radiation-the paper proves two theorems. First, war is peace. When peace persists, entropy-reducing resources become concentrated in the hands of a few. The majority falls into entropy increase. The system reaches an entropy fracture. War is the only remaining mechanism to break up hoarded resources and restore entropy equilibrium. War is therefore the path to peace. Second, peace is war. Peace is never permanent. In any stable society, entropy accumulation begins immediately. Elites hoard resources. The middle class is squeezed. The poor sink into disorder. Internal entropy grows silently. Natural disasters, external shocks, or the mere passage of time pushes the system toward another entropy fracture. Peace is the incubation period of war. The paper concludes that war and peace are not opposites. They are two phases of the same entropic cycle. War is dynamic entropy equilibrium. Peace is static entropy equilibrium. The static inevitably decays into the dynamic. The dynamic inevitably returns to the static. Therefore, war is peace, and peace is war.

title: Entropy Equilibrium and International Aid From Entropy Fracture to External Radiation

detail.title: Entropy Equilibrium and International Aid From Entropy Fracture to External Radiation
detail.abstract: International aid is conventionally understood as charity, humanitarian obligation, or strategic diplomacy. This paper argues that these interpretations miss the underlying physical logic. Drawing on the entropic theory of economic exchange developed in previous work, this paper proposes that a neighboring country's famine or collapse is not merely a humanitarian crisis but an entropy fracture. Within the collapsing country, entropy-reducing resources such as food, medicine, fuel, and organizational capacity become concentrated in the hands of a small elite: war profiteers, hoarders, warlords, and corrupt officials. This small group forms an extremely low-entropy enclave. The majority of the population falls into extreme entropy increase: disorder, hunger, violence, and the breakdown of social order. The entropy difference between the lowentropy elite and the high-entropy masses becomes unsustainable. At a critical threshold, the system has only three possible evolutionary paths. The first path is revolution: the high-entropy masses overthrow the low-entropy monopolists, forcibly redistributing entropy-reducing resources and resetting the system to a lower-entropy state. The second path is reform: internal redistribution of entropy resources, restoring order without violent collapse. The third path is external radiation: the high-entropy population spills across borders as refugees, carrying entropy increase into neighboring low-entropy countries. This paper argues that international aid is not charity. It is the strategic maintenance of entropy equilibrium across borders. Refusing aid does not prevent entropy increase. It merely shifts the timing and location of entropy overflow. By providing aid, the donor country stabilizes the neighboring system's entropy state, prevents the fracture from reaching the critical threshold, and blocks the radiation of entropy increase across its own borders. The paper concludes that aid is entropy defense.

title: Material Entropy Reduction Determines Mental Entropy Reduction

detail.title: Material Entropy Reduction Determines Mental Entropy Reduction
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a foundational axiom for the entropic theory of human behavior: material entropy reduction determines mental entropy reduction. An individual with abundant material resources, defined as entropy-reducing resources such as food, shelter, safety, and economic security, has a stable mental state. His psychological entropy is low. He is not preoccupied with survival. He can think clearly, plan for the future, and maintain emotional stability. An individual with scarce material resources is in a state of material entropy increase. He is hungry, anxious, and threatened. His mental state reflects this material condition. His psychological entropy is high. He is preoccupied with survival. His thinking is disorganized. His emotions are volatile. His attention is captured by immediate threats. The paper argues that this relationship is not merely correlational. It is causal and foundational. Material entropy reduction is the precondition for mental entropy reduction. A person cannot maintain low mental entropy when his material system is in entropy increase. The paper derives three corollaries. First, social class differences are differences in material entropy reduction, which produce differences in mental entropy reduction. The upper class has abundant material resources and therefore low mental entropy. The middle class has sufficient material resources but faces competitive pressure, producing moderate mental entropy. The lower class has scarce material resources and therefore high mental entropy. Second, mental instability, emotional dysregulation, and cognitive disorganization in lower-class populations are not character flaws. They are the necessary consequences of material entropy increase. Third, interventions that improve material conditions reduce mental entropy more effectively than interventions that target psychology directly. The paper concludes that material entropy reduction is the foundational layer of human well-being. All higher layers depend on it.

title: Industry-Academia Partnerships for Experiential Learning: Enhancing Workforce Readiness through Collaborative Education

detail.title: Industry-Academia Partnerships for Experiential Learning: Enhancing Workforce Readiness through Collaborative Education

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was conducted in accordance with established ethical standards for research involving human participants. The data collected for this research were obtained through voluntary participation, and informed consent was secured from all respondents prior to their involvement. Participants were assured of confidentiality and anonymity, and no personally identifiable information was collected or disclosed. The research posed minimal risk to participants, and their responses were used solely for academic and research purposes. As the study involved non-invasive survey-based data collection, formal institutional ethics committee approval was not required.

detail.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of Industry-Academia Partnerships (IAPs) in enhancing experiential learning and employability outcomes among students. While existing literature strongly advocates collaborative education models, empirical evidence capturing multistakeholder perspectives remains limited. To address this gap, the research integrates both primary and secondary data. Primary data were collected from 32 stakeholders, including industry professionals, faculty members, and students, to assess perceptions and measurable outcomes of IAP engagement. Statistical analysis reveals a strong positive correlation (r = 0.703) between Industry-Academia Partnerships and student skill development. Regression results indicate that IAP exposure significantly influences experiential learning and employability outcomes, explaining approximately 49.4% of the variation in student skill development (R² = 0.494, p < 0.05). The findings reject the null hypothesis regarding impact, confirming that IAPs play a substantial role in improving student outcomes. However, ANOVA results indicate no significant difference in stakeholder perceptions, suggesting a shared recognition of IAP effectiveness across groups. The study concludes that well-structured Industry-Academia Partnerships significantly enhance workforce readiness, but their impact depends on systematic implementation, alignment mechanisms, and quality assurance frameworks. The research contributes empirical validation to experiential learning theory within collaborative education models.

title: The Entropic Dynamics of Urban Rise and Fall From Siphoning to Collapse to Decentralized Reconstruction

detail.title: The Entropic Dynamics of Urban Rise and Fall From Siphoning to Collapse to Decentralized Reconstruction
detail.abstract: This paper applies the entropic framework developed in previous work to the dynamics of urban systems. The core proposition is that during periods of peace and stability, a dominant city acts as a local entropy-reduction sink. It siphons entropy-reducing resources-population, capital, talent, information, and organizational capacity-from surrounding smaller cities and rural areas. This siphoning effect produces extreme local entropy reduction in the dominant city, accompanied by entropy increase in the periphery. The periphery becomes hollowed out. The dominant city becomes hyper-concentrated, highly ordered, and increasingly fragile. When this high-density entropy-reduction structure is disrupted by war, economic collapse, plague, or famine, the system undergoes forced entropy increase. The high-density structure disintegrates. Entropy-reducing resources disperse outward. People, skills, capital, and organizational capacity flow from the collapsed core to secondary cities and rural areas. This dispersion is not merely flight from violence. It is the entropic redistribution of resources from an overloaded, failed entropy-reduction structure to lower-density, more sustainable locations. The paper distinguishes two collapse mechanisms. Violent collapse occurs through war, invasion, or rebellion, which destroys the entropy-reduction structure rapidly. Silent collapse occurs through economic depression, fiscal crisis, or institutional decay, which erodes the entropy-reduction structure gradually. Both produce the same entropic outcome: the siphoning intensity of the dominant city falls to zero or becomes negative, and the population disperses. The paper further argues that post-collapse reconstruction is not a return to the previous single-center structure. It is a phase of decentralized entropy reduction. Power, resources, and organizational capacity are distributed across multiple regional centers. This multi-center structure is more resilient and sustainable. The paper concludes that the entropic framework provides a unified explanation for urban siphoning, collapse, dispersion, and reconstruction, grounding urban dynamics in the second law of thermodynamics.

title: Rural Reverse Siphoning: The Ultimate Entropic Siphon in Human History When Cities Collapse and the Countryside Becomes the Last Entropy Sink

detail.title: Rural Reverse Siphoning: The Ultimate Entropic Siphon in Human History When Cities Collapse and the Countryside Becomes the Last Entropy Sink
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a new concept in the entropic analysis of human settlement: rural reverse siphoning, also called the ultimate rural siphon. In normal times, cities act as entropy-reduction sinks, siphoning people, capital, and talent from the countryside. However, when a systemic food or survival crisis occurs, the urban entropy-reduction system can collapse entirely. Cities produce no food of their own and depend completely on external supply chains. When those chains break, the city's entropy-reducing capacity falls to zero. Its dense population, lacking any means of subsistence, enters a state of explosive entropy increase. The countryside, by contrast, retains the most basic entropy-reducing capability: it can produce food directly from the land. Under these conditions, the entropic gradient reverses with overwhelming force. The city no longer siphons from the country. The country siphons the city. Millions of starving urban dwellers pour into rural areas, desperately seeking the last remaining entropy reduction. This paper argues that this rural reverse siphoning is the strongest, most extreme, and most brutal form of entropic siphoning in human history. It is not ordinary migration, not economic depression, not even war refugee movement. It is survival siphoning. Drawing on historical cases of systemic food collapse, the paper defines the conditions under which rural reverse siphoning occurs: total urban entropy-reduction failure, persistent rural survival entropy, and an entropic gradient so steep that it overrides all social, legal, and moral constraints. The paper concludes that rural reverse siphoning represents the ultimate test of any civilization's entropic structure. When it appears, the civilization has already failed.

title: The Entropic Structure of Leadership and Followership How High-Entropy Individuals Stabilize Low-Entropy Groups

detail.title: The Entropic Structure of Leadership and Followership How High-Entropy Individuals Stabilize Low-Entropy Groups
detail.abstract: This paper applies the entropic framework developed in previous work to the structure of leadership and followership. The core proposition is that a leader, revolutionary, or ideological pioneer is a high-entropy-accumulation individual. He has a highly ordered mental state: strong beliefs, clear direction, stable emotions, and a coherent sense of meaning. He possesses a large reserve of mental negative entropy. Followers, by contrast, are low-entropy-accumulation individuals. They are in a state of mental entropy increase. They are materially deprived, anxious, confused, and unable to see a way out. Their mental system is on the verge of collapse. They desperately need external input of meaning, hope, and certainty to achieve mental entropy reduction. The leader provides this input. He outputs beliefs, direction, mission, and a vision of the future. The followers receive this output. Their mental entropy decreases. They become stable, loyal, and willing to sacrifice. The relationship between leader and follower is therefore an entropic exchange: the leader's high entropy accumulation is transferred to the followers as mental negative entropy, achieving a dynamic entropy equilibrium at the group level. The paper applies this framework to communism, utopianism, and ideological movements. It argues that these movements succeed not because they are true or false, but because they provide mental negative entropy to populations in a state of mental entropy increase. The paper concludes that leadership is not merely a social role. It is an entropic function.

contentType.other: Center for Financial Studies Working Paper

detail.abstract: Since the Iran war, fuel prices in Germany have risen sharply. Our analysis shows that diesel prices at gas stations have increased much more than crude oil prices. On average, downstream margins for oil companies rose by 29 euro cents per liter of diesel during the period under review. To ensure that, in times of crisis, only actual changes in crude oil prices are passed on to end consumers, gas station prices could be linked to daily spot prices in Rotterdam or to short-term Brent futures contracts.

title: The Entropic Nature of Religion From Spiritual Entropy Reduction to Organizational Extremization

detail.title: The Entropic Nature of Religion From Spiritual Entropy Reduction to Organizational Extremization
detail.abstract: This paper applies the entropic framework developed in previous work to the origin and evolution of religion. The core proposition is that the founders of major world religions-Shakyamuni, Laozi, Confucius, Jesus Christ, and Muhammad-were individuals with extremely high mental entropy accumulation. They had highly ordered mental states: absolute internal order, stable emotions, a coherent understanding of the world, and a clear path for others to follow. They emerged during periods of extreme social entropy increase: war, chaos, suffering, and meaninglessness. The masses were in a state of mental entropy increase, desperate for meaning, order, and relief. The founders provided massive outputs of mental negative entropy. They explained suffering and gave a path to liberation. They revealed the natural order and taught how to follow it. They established social norms and reduced internal conflict. They offered love, redemption, and emotional stability. They created rules and community, ending chaos and predation. These outputs reduced the mental entropy of the masses, stabilizing individuals and societies. The paper argues that the founders were not gods. They were extreme entropyreduction agents. Their teachings were entropy-reduction systems. Religion emerged when these teachings were institutionalized, dogmatized, and mythologized by later followers. Organizational power, the need for certainty, and the demand for belonging turned entropyreduction systems into worship, dogma, and hierarchy. The paper concludes that religion is entropy-reduction teachings extremized. Understanding this entropic structure explains why religions emerge, why they endure for millennia, and why they produce both profound good and profound harm.

title: The Entropic Collapse of Regional Core Cities and the Diffusion of Regional Entropy Increase From Urban Hollowing to Cross-Regional Migration

detail.title: The Entropic Collapse of Regional Core Cities and the Diffusion of Regional Entropy Increase From Urban Hollowing to Cross-Regional Migration
detail.abstract: When a dominant city experiences prolonged economic depression and an influx of population beyond its carrying capacity, it transforms from an entropy-reduction machine into an entropy-increase quagmire. This paper extends the entropic analysis of urban dynamics from the level of a single city to that of an entire region. It argues that when all core cities within a region suffer the same collapse of entropy-reducing capacity, the region as a whole enters a state of regional entropy-reduction failure. Rural and small-town environments cannot provide enough entropy-reducing resources to compensate for the entropy increase of the population. The result is not merely reverse siphoning, but a regional entropic equilibrium at a high-entropy, low-welfare level. Under such conditions, the population does not simply disperse to nearby smaller cities; it engages in cross-regional entropy migration, moving to distant areas where entropy-reducing resources are still available. The paper examines the case of Northeast China, where the collapse of old industrial cores has led to widespread ghost cities and a sustained outflow of population to the warmer, more dynamic southern regions. It also notes that natural disasters such as floods or droughts in the south can trigger reverse flows. The paper concludes that the entropic framework provides a unified explanation for regional decline, ghost towns, and large-scale population movements across history, from the great migrations of late antiquity to modern rust-belt collapses.

title: From Closed-System Entropy Deficit to Open-System Entropy Recovery The Entropic Logic of China's Urban-Rural Migration (1955-1980)

detail.title: From Closed-System Entropy Deficit to Open-System Entropy Recovery The Entropic Logic of China's Urban-Rural Migration (1955-1980)
detail.abstract: Between the mid-1950s and the end of the 1970s, China experienced a massive, state-organized transfer of urban youth to the countryside. Standard historical narratives interpret this policy through political or social lenses. This paper offers an alternative, purely physical explanation based on the entropic framework developed in previous work. It treats the national economy as a nearly closed entropic system in which the most basic entropy-reducing resource is food (grain). During this period, agricultural technology was primitive, external trade was minimal, and grain output stagnated near subsistence levels. At the same time, the urban population, especially young adults, grew rapidly. Cities consumed grain but produced almost none, making them pure entropy-consuming units. The result was a chronic entropy deficit: total entropy demand (urban consumption plus rural subsistence) persistently exceeded the system's ability to produce entropy reduction (grain). Under a closed-system constraint, the only way to prevent systemic collapse (mass famine and social disintegration) was to reduce the entropy load of the cities by transferring surplus urban youth to the only subsystem that could still produce basic entropy reduction-the countryside. The paper argues that the "sent-down youth" (rustication) policy was not an ideological whim but a compulsory entropy-balancing emergency measure. It transformed urban entropy-increasing population into rural entropy-reducing labor, however inefficiently. The paper then analyses the reversal of this policy after 1979. Normalization of relations with the United States and the opening of foreign trade turned China from a closed system into an open system that could import external entropy reduction (chemical fertilisers, grain, machinery, capital). Urban industries revived, cities began to generate their own entropy reduction, and the entropic gradient reversed, allowing the youth to return to the cities. The paper concludes that the entropic framework provides a unified, value-free explanation for the rustication movement and its abrupt end, without recourse to political or moral judgment.

title: Model Monoculture Risk: Systemic AI Convergence in Banking and Financial Markets

detail.title: Model Monoculture Risk: Systemic AI Convergence in Banking and Financial Markets
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is significantly changing the landscape of banking and financial markets, improving predictive precision, operational productivity, and decision-making speed. However, underlying these improvements is an underexplored structural vulnerability: the risk of systemic AI convergence. As financial institutions become more dependent on similar foundational models, cloud infrastructure, data suppliers, and AI middleware platforms, diverse firms may begin to interpret and respond to market signals in similar ways. This paper presents the notion of model monoculture risk—a systemic fragility that arises when model similarities, market synchronisation, and infrastructure concentration align. Rather than focusing solely on traditional firm-level model risk management, this paper introduces the M³ Framework (Model–Market–Middleware) to clarify how shared AI architectures can transform localised optimisations into widespread amplification. The Model layer encapsulates the convergence of foundational architectures and training interdependencies; the Market layer reflects synchronised adjustments in portfolios, credit, and liquidity; and the Middleware layer emphasises the concentration of cloud services and vendors that quickens the spread. Collectively, these layers create multiplied exposure to correlated failures. To put this concept into practice, the paper proposes a qualitative Model Monoculture Risk Index (MMRI) to evaluate cross-layer alignment and the erosion of diversity within AI-driven financial systems. By redefining AI governance as a challenge of structural diversification rather than just a validation task, this contribution highlights cognitive diversity as an essential element of financial stability in the era of AI.

title: Enhancing Tax Compliance and Citizen Trust: The Case for a Single Tax Jurisdiction in the European Union

detail.abstract: This study aims to investigate the implications of establishing a Single Tax Jurisdiction (STJ) within the European Union, focusing on its potential to enhance tax compliance, efficiency, and citizen trust. Utilizing advanced AI analysis techniques, the research examines existing tax frameworks across member states, identifying inefficiencies and disparities that hinder effective tax administration. The methodology involves a comprehensive data analysis of tax compliance rates, administrative capacities, and stakeholder perceptions, supplemented by simulations of potential STJ implementation scenarios. Key findings reveal that a unified tax jurisdiction could significantly reduce compliance costs, streamline administrative processes, and improve revenue generation across diverse economic contexts. Furthermore, the study highlights the importance of transparency mechanisms, such as citizen panels and real-time data sharing, in fostering trust and engagement among taxpayers. Overall, the conclusions suggest that the establishment of an STJ presents a viable pathway for addressing the challenges of fragmented tax systems in the EU. By promoting a more equitable and efficient tax environment, the STJ has the potential to enhance fiscal legitimacy and support deeper economic integration within the Union. The findings underscore the necessity for collaborative efforts among member states to realize the benefits of a unified tax framework while ensuring that citizen concerns and expectations are adequately addressed. We submit a four-pronged approach will be necessary to move forward the EU as a Tax Polity: (1) An EU-MS Tax Partnership (2) A EU Common Tax base (3) The EU as a multilevel Tax administration (4) A Single EU Tax Jurisdiction. Finally, the EU doesn't generate enough income per capita in comparison to GDP ratio that stands at €7,1 trillion in revenues compared to €21 trillion in GDP. This has a negative impact on the EU's perceived and real abilities to accumulate wealth hence its potential to develop into a powerful polity.

detail.abstract: Institutional performance in complex environments is commonly evaluated through observable outputs, leadership actions, and short-term effectiveness metrics. While these indicators capture discrete outcomes, they provide limited explanatory power regarding the structural conditions that generate decision behavior across repeated cycles. This paper advances decision system reliability as a distinct analytical variable necessary for understanding institutional performance under sustained strategic load. Decision systems are defined as structured environments within which decisions are produced, including authority architectures, escalation pathways, coordination protocols, regulatory constraints, feedback mechanisms, and embedded behavioral norms. The analysis develops a structural model linking sustained strategic load to adaptive transformations in decision behavior. It demonstrates that under persistent cognitive, informational, and regulatory pressure, decision systems systematically reconfigure toward short-term stability, often at the expense of long-term functional alignment. To capture this dynamic, the paper introduces the concept of decision integrity, defined as the degree of sustained alignment between decision processes and the enduring functional requirements of the institution. A formal representation of decision system stress is proposed, conceptualizing reliability as a function of load relative to processing capacity. The framework contributes to institutional analysis by shifting the unit of observation from individual decisions to the structural conditions that produce them. It provides a basis for evaluating institutional performance in environments where stability is maintained operationally while strategic degradation accumulates over time.

title: Urban Reverse Siphoning and the Large-Scale "Ghost City" Phenomenon in China An Entropic Analysis of Systemic Collapse and Structural Entropy Increase

detail.title: Urban Reverse Siphoning and the Large-Scale "Ghost City" Phenomenon in China An Entropic Analysis of Systemic Collapse and Structural Entropy Increase
detail.abstract: This paper applies the entropic framework developed in previous work to the phenomenon of large-scale urban hollowing in China, known colloquially as "Hegang-ization" (after the city of Hegang, a typical shrinking industrial city). The core proposition is that when a city loses its capacity to provide entropy-reducing resources (jobs, income, public services, capital, and a stable order), the previous urban siphoning effect reverses. Instead of attracting population, the city becomes a source of population outflow. People disperse to smaller cities, towns, rural areas, or other provinces. If the collapse affects only a single city, the outflow is locally contained. If the entire regional or national urban system loses entropy-reducing capacity, the result is large-scale reverse siphoning across the whole society. The paper argues that the widespread appearance of ghost cities and collapsing housing prices in China is not a short-term adjustment but a symptom of systemic structural entropy increase. The previous model of urbanisation-based on continuous growth, investment, and population concentration-has reached a point where the maintenance cost of the urban system exceeds its benefits. The system is forced into a phase of disorder: capital devaluation, human capital dispersal, fiscal collapse, and the breakdown of hierarchical spatial order. The paper concludes that Hegang-ization is the physical manifestation of a societal entropy explosion, and that the only possible equilibria are either a new, lower-order stable state or continued entropic decay.

title: The Entropic Dynamics of Cities During Economic Depression Why Siphoning Fails and Reverse Siphoning Emerges

detail.title: The Entropic Dynamics of Cities During Economic Depression Why Siphoning Fails and Reverse Siphoning Emerges
detail.abstract: A common misconception in urban economics and regional studies is that during economic depression, large cities continue to exhibit a siphoning effect. They are believed to attract population from surrounding areas because they offer more jobs, better infrastructure, and greater resilience. This paper argues that this view is mistaken. Drawing on the entropic framework developed in previous work, it distinguishes between the flow of people and the structure of entropy-reducing resources. During a depression, the total entropy-reducing capacity of a dominant city declines. Employment shrinks. Investment disappears. Public services weaken. Fiscal capacity falls. However, because smaller cities and rural areas are even worse off, people continue to migrate to the large city. This inflow of population does not represent genuine siphoning, because the city's entropy-reducing resources are not expanding. They are contracting. The per-capita availability of entropy-reducing resources falls sharply. Jobs become scarce. Wages drop. Housing costs remain rigid. The cost of survival rises. The large city transforms from an entropy-reduction ⾼地 into a hell of internal competition. Under these conditions, those who cannot compete are forced out. They return to their places of origin, move to smaller cities, or go to rural areas. This is reverse siphoning: the outward flow of entropy-reducing capacity from the overloaded core to the periphery. The paper proposes the law of reverse siphoning during depression. It argues that economic depression does not strengthen urban siphoning. It makes siphoning in name only, and ultimately produces a net outflow of population. The paper concludes that the conventional wisdom is reversed. The direction of population flow during depression is not a sign of the city's strength. It is a sign of the city's overload.

title: Between Moral Judgment and Randomness: Existential Anxiety, Meaning-Making, and the Human Fear of Death

detail.title: Between Moral Judgment and Randomness: Existential Anxiety, Meaning-Making, and the Human Fear of Death
