detail.abstract: This paper examines a limited category of intangible goods: reproducible, non-rival knowledge and technology commodities produced through organized labor and usable by multiple agents without physical depletion. It asks whether Marx s labor theory of value can be applied to such commodities and how their labor value may be more fairly realized and distributed. The paper proposes a cost-sharing theory in which labor value is socially distributed among beneficiaries rather than captured through monopoly pricing or left uncompensated through free disclosure. It also critiques the patent system as technological monopoly and argues that free disclosure, while useful for diffusion, does not solve the problem of producer compensation. Finally, the paper offers a preliminary framework for quantifying effective labor and considers implications for access, innovation incentives, and social equity.

title: Price as Focal Point: Prediction Markets, Conditional Reflexivity, and the Politics of Common Knowledge

detail.title: Price as Focal Point: Prediction Markets, Conditional Reflexivity, and the Politics of Common Knowledge
detail.abstract: Prediction markets are widely treated as forecasting devices that reveal collective expectations about uncertain futures. This article argues that under specifiable conditions they also function as coordination mechanisms: public probabilities that organize the behavior of voters, donors, journalists, traders, and institutions in ways that can be self-fulfilling or self-defeating. Most existing work asks whether prediction markets forecast accurately; this paper asks whether accurate forecasting is even the right criterion for a market that has become a public coordination device. Drawing on transaction-level evidence from the 2024 U.S. presidential election, we show that the social force of a market signal depends less on its size than on its persistence, the breadth of responding trader types, and cross-platform consensus. We introduce a Signal Credibility Index (SCI) -- combining the variance ratio VR(6), a two-sidedness diagnostic, and a trader-concentration adjustment -- as a microstructure-grounded criterion for predicting when price moves acquire behavioral traction. Applied to three major 2024 political shocks, the framework reveals that superficially similar events generated qualitatively distinct signal types with different implications for elite coordination. A cross-platform comparison establishes a systematic decoupling of social authority from epistemic robustness: the most visible market produced the least accurate forecasts. The framework carries direct implications for regulating prediction markets as democratic information infrastructure.

title: Testing CCP Resolution Preparedness: A Crisis Simulation by the Spanish CCP Resolution Authority
affiliations: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV)

detail.title: Testing CCP Resolution Preparedness: A Crisis Simulation by the Spanish CCP Resolution Authority
detail.abstract: Central counterparties (CCPs) play a critical role in modern financial markets, making their resilience and resolvability essential for f inancial stability. While regulatory frameworks for CCP recovery and resolution have been significantly strengthened since the global financial crisis, their operational implementation remains largely untested. This paper presents a case study of the Spanish National Securities Market Commission (CNMV), acting as the CCP resolution authority, in developing an operational framework for CCP crisis management. In particular, it describes the development of a Crisis Management Handbook and the implementation of a full-scale crisis simulation exercise designed to test governance arrangements, decision-making processes and the operational deployment of recovery, early intervention and resolution tools. The case study contributes to the emerging literature on the operationalisation of financial crisis management frameworks. It illustrates how resolution authorities can translate complex regulatory frameworks into operational procedures, documents the use of crisis simulation exercises to test resolvability, and highlights the potential role of technological tools (ResTech) in supporting crisis management. The exercise generated a number of lessons learnt, leading to concrete action plans to strengthen crisis preparedness. The results underline the importance of operational readiness, crisis simulation exercises and technological capabilities, while also pointing to the growing need for stronger international coordination in managing crises in an increasingly interconnected financial system.

title: Keeping Circular 230 in the Middle

detail.title: Keeping Circular 230 in the Middle
detail.abstract: Ethics in tax practice rarely fail because a practitioner does not know the rules. It fails because of ordinary pressures-time, incomplete records, client urgency, and technology shortcuts-pull decision-making away from standards. Circular 230 is issued under the U.S. Department of the Treasury and governs practice before the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), administered and enforced through the Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR). It imposes enforceable duties on practitioners, including diligence, competence, and written advice standards (including electronic communications). For Enrolled Agents, the most defensible posture is evidence-based: positions are anchored to verified facts, supported by authority, explained clearly, and documented in a file that can survive later scrutiny. This feature article focuses on four recurring pressure points in federal tax work: due diligence; written advice; client pressure and independent judgment; and technology and AI risk.

title: Biological economics: the evolutionary biology of (state) institutions in modern humans

detail.title: Biological economics: the evolutionary biology of (state) institutions in modern humans

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None to declare
declarations.ethicsApproval: none needed
declarations.funderStatement: No specific funder associated to this paper

detail.abstract: The evolutionary history of modern humans (Homo sapiens) spans a brief ~315,000 years over which a series of unprecedented cultural and technological innovations-such as complex language, agriculture, money, and industrialisation-led our species to consolidate into the most successful and influential organism that ever lived. The transformative magnitude of these innovations is such, that they have triggered global-scale alterations of planetary systems, including climate change and the rapid loss of biodiversity. What made modern humans such an exceptional species? To address this question, I introduce the 'biological economics' framework-the conceptualisation of ('state') institutions as a modern human-exclusive adaptive key innovation driven and shaped by natural selection. The biological economics framework proposes that (1) institutions drove modern humans into a distinctive evolutionary pathway by shifting social dynamics from an 'unfettered' competition-based distribution of resources across individuals in a population (the system that prevails across nature), to a unique (and still imperfect) collective norms-based allocation of resources. Therefore, institutions have led humans to progressively supress natural selection on inherited functional variation (a process I term 'natural rejection'); (2) institutions evolutionarily originated with the emergence of modern human self-domestication-the collective punishment of aggressive antisocial disruptors by coordinated alliances of individuals-following the split from the Neanderthal-Denisovan lineage; (3) institutions have diversified through time and across regions of the world from local-scale sets of norms to regulate common-pool resources, to larger-scale complex social dynamics sustained by the rule of law, property rights, and economic and political norms, which enable the emergence of successive transformative technological and cultural innovations, economic growth and, ultimately, to generalised shared prosperity at varying degrees. I discuss the wider implications of the biological economics framework for the emergence of inequality, in the context of differences in prosperity across groups, and the role of 'natural rejection' as the cultural approach for the pursuit of prosperity by humanity.

title: Dynamic Adjustment of Capital Structure in Distressed Sector of an Emerging Economy: Evidence from Pakistan's Textile Sector

detail.title: Dynamic Adjustment of Capital Structure in Distressed Sector of an Emerging Economy: Evidence from Pakistan's Textile Sector
detail.abstract: Capital structure theories are rarely tested in industries facing long-term financial distress within emerging economies. This study investigates how firms in Pakistan's distressed textile sector adjust their capital structure under persistent financial pressure. Using a panel data of 114 firms from 1999 to 2023 and system GMM estimation, we examine whether firms converge toward a target capital structure, testing the validity of trade-off and pecking order theories in a distressed environment. To address distortions in conventional leverage ratios caused by continuous losses, we introduce an adjusted measure that excludes retained earnings. Results show that textile firms close 42 percent of the gap toward target leverage annually, indicating partial adjustment consistent with trade-off theory. Unlike healthier industries, profitability exerts no influence, while asset tangibility is inversely related to leverage, reflecting liquidity constraints rather than collateral strength. These findings demonstrate that distress reshapes conventional capital structure behavior and contribute new insights to financing dynamics in emerging markets.

This paper examines the role of administrative process standardisation as a key driver of interoperability and policy coherence in contemporary public administration. The study adopts a qualitative case study approach, supported by descriptive analysis of administrative data, focusing on the Greek National Registry of Administrative Procedures (MITOS).

detail.abstract: Why do well-intentioned reformers consistently fail to transform dysfunctional public systems? This paper synthesizes institutional theory with non-equilibrium thermodynamics to introduce the theory of Institutional Parasitism. While existing literature identifies institutional parasites as illegitimate actors who exploit the systems they inhabit (AMR, 2024), and others apply entropy as a metaphor for decay (Aksom, 2023), a mechanical link between parasitic behavior and systemic energy dissipation remains absent. We propose a formal model of Managed Failure Equilibrium (MFE), defining it as a mathematically stable Nash Equilibrium where the system actively dissipates reform energy to maintain parasitic extraction networks. Drawing on Prigogine's dissipative structures, we demonstrate that as Institutional Temperature (Tinst)defined by meritocratic stability and trust-decreases, the entropy production of any reform effort increases, rendering the marginal productivity of reform agents structurally negligible. We validate the model against 34 years and 20 ministerial transitions in Mongolia's education sector, calculating a reform efficiency coefficient of η < 0.15, implying that over 85% of cumulative reform energy has been dissipated without improving learning outcomes. Our findings reframe the policy prescription: effective governance requires raising the system's thermodynamic threshold through Institutional Cooling and a Negentropy Flux architecture, not merely increasing reform input energy.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Fontaise Institute of Computational Social Science FICSS Working Paper Series WP-2026-003

detail.abstract: The Arab Spring of 2010-2012 challenged conventional understanding of political stability in authoritarian regimes, as protests rapidly toppled long-standing governments in Tunisia and Egypt while leaving others, such as Saudi Arabia, largely unaffected. Existing explanations emphasizing social media, youth demographics, or economic grievances have struggled to account for this differential pattern. The Computational Macrohistory (CMH) framework, grounded in structural-demographic theory, offers a quantitative approach to analyzing conditions that predispose societies toward political instability. We apply the CMH operational framework to analyze three Arab Spring cases: Tunisia (revolution), Egypt (revolution), and Saudi Arabia (stability). Using data from 2000-2012, we construct a Systemic Stress Index (SSI) comprising five structural variables: youth bulge (D₂), income inequality (E₂), youth unemployment (E₄), regime type (P₁), and internet penetration (S₃). We employ comparative case study methodology, threshold analysis, and counterfactual reasoning to assess the framework's ability to discriminate between revolutionary and stable outcomes. The SSI correctly ranks all three countries by outcome severity: Tunisia (0.52) > Egypt (0.10) > Saudi Arabia (-0.09). A threshold of SSI > 0 achieves perfect discrimination in this sample. Component decomposition reveals regime type as the primary discriminating variable: Saudi Arabia's full autocracy (Polity =-10) generates a strongly negative anocracy stress contribution (-0.42), while Tunisia and Egypt's anocratic regimes (Polity =-3 to -4) contribute positively. Counterfactual analysis indicates that if Saudi Arabia had been an anocracy, its SSI would have increased by +0.58, placing it in the revolutionary zone. Economic stress factors (youth unemployment, inequality) prove necessary but not sufficient for revolution. Important caveat: This proof-of-concept analysis with N=3 demonstrates framework applicability but does not constitute statistical validation. The sample size precludes formal inference, and perfect discrimination could occur by chance with probability ≈12.5%. These findings provide preliminary, exploratory support for the CMH framework and highlight the critical moderating role of regime type in translating structural stress into political mobilization. The results suggest that revolution requires the conjunction of structural grievances and regime vulnerability—an interaction effect consistent with both structural-demographic theory and the anocracy hypothesis. While limited by small sample size (N=3), this proof-of-concept analysis demonstrates the framework's analytical potential and motivates expanded validation across additional cases.

detail.abstract: The organisational framework Holacracy aims at a decentralisation of leadership, «management without managers», and is gaining traction among Swiss companies. As Swiss legal scholarship has so far not engaged substantively with the topic, this contribution examines how directors' and officers' liability under Art. 754 CO operates in holacratically structured stock corporations. The central question is whether management functions can be validly delegated under Art. 716b CO to roles within the Holacracy framework, despite its decentralised design. The analysis shows that the Lead Link of the General Company Circle qualifies as a legitimate delegate, whereas the status of Lead Links at subordinate circle levels requires case-by-case assessment. The contribution further addresses the risk of de facto organ status arising from structural power concentrations. The unconventional architecture of the model entails heightened duties of care and elevated compliance risks, including with respect to corporate criminal liability under Art. 102 SCC, and calls for an adequate internal control and monitoring system.

title: Overrated Judgment, Underrated Power: Gen AI at Work

detail.title: Overrated Judgment, Underrated Power: Gen AI at Work
detail.abstract: Generative AI is reshaping cognitive work by compressing productivity gaps between top and low performers and improving the relative position of senior workers over junior entrants, because it still cannot adequately exercise human judgment in nuanced contexts. This paper argues that human judgment is less robust than the rhetoric of human oversight assumes-it is biased, noisy, weakly introspectable, and reliably narratable rather than reliably explainable-and that the only human function not replaceable by machines is, hopefully, goalsetting. Unfortunately, that function is exercised primarily by the firms that build and own the most capable models, not by users. The resulting axis of inequality runs between a small number of producing firms and user populations worldwide. Inclusion and accountability therefore require participation in defining the objectives these systems optimise for. The paper points out the necessity of reclassifying AI producers under the editorial obligations of transparency and pluralism that other communicative powers carry, and argues for close collaboration among academia, engineers, and policymakers to determine how shared participation in goal-setting can be secured. It acknowledges that no institutional response presently on offer is adequate to the asymmetry it confronts, and that mere regulation or sovereign AI alone does not resolve the problem.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the **IFTU-Based Cognitive Economics** framework, which redefines economic decision-making as a non-linear, factorial cognitive process rather than a static, linear model. By integrating the Infinite Factorial Thought Universe (IFTU) with Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), the framework proposes autonomous decision systems capable of operating across dynamic commercial and financial environments. Drawing upon the author's earlier work on ICLM (IFTU-Based Agile Cognitive Learning Model), AGI-Finance, and AGI-Commerce, the model shifts traditional economics from human-limited, Newtonian-style structures to adaptive, self-evolving intelligence systems. The framework is illustrated through real classroom applications in commerce education and Mintzberg's emergent strategy concepts, establishing a practical pathway toward post-agile, post-human economic intelligence. "The study further integrates behavioral and mathematical validation to support the transition from human-centered to intelligence-centered economic systems.

title: Reviewing The Role Of AI In Fraud Detection

detail.title: Reviewing The Role Of AI In Fraud Detection
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital financial services has significantly increased the scale and sophistication of fraudulent activities, creating critical challenges for financial institutions and payment platforms. Traditional fraud detection methods, which rely on static rules and manual monitoring, are increasingly inadequate in identifying complex and evolving fraud patterns. In this context, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative solution. This paper reviews the role of AI in fraud detection, focusing on its applications, effectiveness, and associated challenges within modern financial systems. AI-based fraud detection systems utilize advanced techniques such as machine learning, data mining, and anomaly detection to process large volumes of transactional data in real time. These systems can identify hidden patterns and detect suspicious behaviour more accurately than traditional approaches. Organizations such as PayPal and Mastercard have successfully integrated AI technologies to enhance fraud prevention and reduce financial losses. The adaptive nature of AI allows it to continuously learn from new data, making it effective against emerging fraud strategies. However, the implementation of AI in fraud detection also presents several challenges. Issues such as false positives, data privacy concerns, high implementation costs, and algorithmic bias can limit its effectiveness. Furthermore, the reliability of AI systems depends on the quality and diversity of the data used for training. This paper concludes that while AI significantly improves fraud detection capabilities, a balanced approach combining technological innovation with human oversight is essential for achieving optimal results in financial security.

detail.abstract: Fenomena fissured workplace oleh David Weil merujuk kepada perubahan organisasi moden daripada pekerjaan berpusat kepada sistem berpecah melalui penyumberan luar, subkontrak, agensi pekerja, dan francais. Perubahan ini didorong oleh kecekapan kos, persaingan global, serta pendigitalan pasaran buruh. Kajian ini menganalisis bagaimana pengaturan kerja segitiga (pekerja–agensi–syarikat induk) mempengaruhi struktur kuasa dalam hubungan pekerjaan, khususnya terhadap keupayaan pekerja menyertai kesatuan, menuntut hak kolektif, dan mengenal pasti majikan sebenar. Didapati wujud kekaburan antara “majikan formal” dan “majikan sebenar”, yang mewujudkan jurang akauntabiliti. Walaupun model ini meningkatkan kecekapan dan fleksibiliti organisasi, ia melemahkan perlindungan pekerja. Pekerja sering berada dalam pekerjaan tidak standard, menghadapi ketidakjaminan kerja, serta sukar mengakses hak asas seperti gaji adil dan perlindungan undang-undang. Fragmentasi ini juga menyukarkan kesatuan sekerja berfungsi secara berkesan. Kesimpulannya, fenomena ini memerlukan reformasi dasar seperti pengiktirafan “majikan bersama”, pengukuhan perlindungan pekerja kontrak, dan strategi baharu kesatuan sekerja bagi memastikan keadilan dalam hubungan pekerjaan moden.

detail.abstract:
For many investors, short-term interest rates are often treated as something the market "discovers." In reality, the Federal Reserve has enormous control over how the front end of the yield curve evolves. While textbooks often portray the Fed's policy rate as a flexible tool that reacts quickly to economic data, the actual behavior of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) looks very different. In practice, monetary policy tends to move in long, persistent cycles. The Fed spends years hiking rates, or years cutting them, and only rarely reverses direction quickly. For anyone trading rates, bonds, or rate-sensitive assets, this persistence matters. It means that the path of short-term interest rates over the next one to two years is often largely shaped by the Fed's policy trajectory rather than by constantly shifting market expectations. 
This observation has an important implication: the short end of the Treasury curve often behaves less like a forecasting market and more like a gradual reflection of the Fed's policy cycle. When the Fed enters a tightening or easing phase, that trend tends to propagate through Treasury yields from one month out to roughly two years. In this article, we show that these policy-driven trends can be measured and used. By identifying whether the Fed is in a tightening, easing, or neutral phase, investors can improve their expectations about the near-term evolution of the yield curve. For fixed-income portfolio managers and macro traders, recognizing these policy regimes can help sharpen rate forecasts, improve duration positioning, and better manage risks tied to interest-rate movements.

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Stock Market Volatility and Risk Management

detail.title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Stock Market Volatility and Risk Management
detail.abstract: Precise forecasting of financial market volatility is fundamental to derivative pricing, portfolio optimization, and risk management practices such as calculating Value-at-Risk (VaR). While traditional linear and parametric models like GARCH have served the financial sector for decades, they struggle to adapt to sudden market shocks driven by complex macroeconomic and geopolitical factors. This study investigates the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning techniques in predicting stock market volatility, focusing on their ability to map non-linear patterns across large financial datasets. Adopting a quantitative research design utilizing historical data from the S&P 500 Index and the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), the study compares a traditional GARCH model against a Support Vector Machine (SVM) and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) deep learning network, as well as a hybrid GARCH-LSTM model. The empirical findings demonstrate that the hybrid GARCH-LSTM model outperforms standalone models, achieving the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Furthermore, while the traditional GARCH model tended to underestimate tail risk (breaching the targeted 5% VaR at 7.2%), the hybrid framework provided the most accurate safety buffers for financial institutions. However, the study notes that AI prediction accuracy decreases as volatility increases during extreme market events. Ultimately, the paper highlights the superiority of hybrid deep learning architectures in boosting financial system resilience and providing actionable dynamic hedging insights for portfolio managers.

detail.abstract: Entrepreneurial passion is widely recognized as a critical driver of startup initiation and persistence. However, existing literature often treats passion as a static trait rather than a dynamic construct that evolves across the startup lifecycle. This study proposes a Dynamic Passion Model, conceptualizing entrepreneurial passion as a shifting alignment between founder energy, organizational demands, and lifecycle stage requirements. Drawing on lifecycle theory, leadership adaptability research, and qualitative insights from founder experiences, the study identifies four distinct phases of passion evolution and examines their impact on decision-making, team alignment, and venture outcomes. The findings suggest that misalignment between passion expression and lifecycle demands contributes to strategic drift, founder burnout, and organizational inefficiency. The study contributes a novel framework integrating psychological and operational perspectives on entrepreneurial motivation, offering practical implications for founders, coaches, and entrepreneurship educators, and advancing the theoretical literature on dynamic entrepreneurial passion. "Note: Select figures and conceptual Note’models in this paper were developed with the assistance of generative AI tools. detail.abstract: Why do well-informed decisions so often fail to translate into sustained action? This research note introduces decision sovereignty as a missing transmission variable between decision quality and implementation in complex institutional and behavioural systems. While advances in data, analytics and artificial intelligence have dramatically reduced the cost of prediction, realised outcomes have not increased proportionately. The paper argues that this disconnect arises from an endogenous execution constraint: governance structures designed for lower decision intensity impose convex costs as decision volume, scope and contestation increase. Decision sovereignty specifies the institutional capacity to select a course of action and carry it through to completion despite internal fragmentation and external pressure. Introduced as a boundary-condition variable rather than a substitute theory, decision sovereignty clarifies when improvements in predictive capacity translate into outcomes and when they do not. The paper develops a reduced-form representation, proposes a conceptual Decision Sovereignty Index, and outlines falsifiable implications for future empirical research.

detail.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) is rapidly transforming the modern workplace, yet its specific impact on Human Resources functions remains underexplored. This study applies a skills-based analytical framework to assess the Gen AI task exposure of 8 HR occupations using task-level data from the O*NET 30.2 Database, comprising 180 HR-specific task statements across occupations ranging from HR Assistants to HR Managers. Each task was scored on a 1 to 5 AI exposure scale using a keyword-based rubric grounded in established automation research. Results indicate that HR Assistants show the highest task exposure score (3.95/5.0), with 58% of their O*NET documented task statements classified as high-exposure. Education Administrators demonstrate the lowest exposure score (3.00/5.0). Skills analysis reveals a bifurcation among top HR competencies: Active Listening and Social Perceptiveness are classified as AI-resistant, while Critical Thinking and Writing show higher AI exposure. These findings carry significant implications for HR workforce planning, reskilling strategies, and the future design of HR roles.

detail.abstract: In early-stage ventures, where resource constraints amplify individual performance variability, the capacity to diagnose and manage team capability and motivation is a core founder competency. Yet skill and will are rarely integrated into a unified diagnostic tool. This study introduces the Skill-Will Alignment Framework-a four-quadrant model classifying team members by capability and motivational alignment-developed through mixed-method research combining founder interviews and startup survey data. Findings show that skill and will operate as interactive rather than additive determinants: high-skill/high-will individuals substantially outperform all other configurations, while high skill paired with low will generates disproportionate cultural and performance costs. detail.abstract: This study investigates the antibacterial activities and phytochemical composition of three native medicinal plants from Saudi Arabia: Ziziphus spina-christi (Sidr), Rhanterium epapposum (Arfaj), and Peganum harmala (Harmal). Ethanol extracts were obtained from the plant leaves using Soxhlet extraction and subsequently analyzed via Gas-Liquid Chromatography (GLC), which identified bioactive molecules with established antimicrobial properties. P. harmala extracts were found to be rich in β-carboline alkaloids, including harmine, harmaline, and vasicinone, which are known to interfere with microbial DNA and protein synthesis. R. epapposum yielded fatty acids (hexadecanoic, linoleic, and oleic acids), β-sitosterol, and squalene. GLC analysis of Z. spina-christi confirmed the presence of triterpenoids (lupeol), phytosterols, and linoleic acids, collectively contributing to cell wall disintegration and metabolic inhibition. A novel aspect of this research involved evaluating the synergistic potential of binary and ternary combinations of the three plant extracts. Our findings revealed that specific mixtures significantly enhanced antimicrobial efficacy compared to individual extracts. Notably, the ternary combination demonstrated a superior broad-spectrum inhibitory effect against both bacterial and fungal pathogens. The antimicrobial efficacy was evaluated against Streptococcus and Staphylococcus species, as well as three phytopathogenic fungi: Botrytis cinerea, Fusarium oxysporum, and Phytophthora infestans. All extracts exhibited dose-dependent bactericidal properties; Z. spinachristi and P. harmala achieved complete growth inhibition at a concentration of 0.20 g/mL. Particularly against B. cinerea, the synergistic interaction between P. harmala and R. epapposum was most pronounced. These results validate the traditional medicinal use of these species and highlight their potential as advanced natural antimicrobial agents for therapeutic and agricultural applications.

title:
First-Order Manufacturing Failure in Small-Firm International Sourcing:
A Practice-Derived Cascade Model from 412 Cases (DS-PR412, 2011–2024)

detail.title:
First-Order Manufacturing Failure in Small-Firm International Sourcing:
A Practice-Derived Cascade Model from 412 Cases (DS-PR412, 2011–2024)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial conflicts of interest related to this paper. The author is an independent researcher and practitioner in manufacturing operations. detail.abstract:
This paper presents a diagnostic model of first-order manufacturing failure in small-firm international sourcing. The model is derived from DS-PR412 — a hand-coded dataset of 412 first manufacturing orders placed by small founder-led firms with overseas factories across six countries (Bangladesh, Vietnam, China, India, South Korea, Thailand) in five product categories between 2011 and 2024.

Four variables determine whether a first order fails: specification, verification, incentive alignment, and timing. They operate as a strict dependency sequence. Each unresolved variable structurally disables the next — a weak specification cannot be verified; an unverified order cannot be governed; a misaligned incentive cannot be corrected in time. The dependency direction is invariant in the dataset. This is a Tier 1 structural claim.

Three directional findings are reported as Tier 2 — correlation observed, confounds not controlled, causal interpretation is the author's inference:

(1) Among the n=94 subset of orders where the factory asked zero clarifying questions before quoting, 87% deviated from specification at bulk production (Claim 2.3).

(2) In the n=88 inspection-timing subset (n=43 inline, n=45 pre-shipment-only), 75.9% of orders with inline inspection at approximately unit 120 produced a documented mid-run correction, versus 31% of orders relying on pre-shipment inspection alone (Claim 2.9). Among orders that triggered correction at the inline window, the median correction cost was 4.2% of order value (Claim 2.10, n=16, small sample).

(3) Among second orders placed with the same factory but with materially changed cascade structure, 73.6% improved on the primary failure metric (n=87). Among second orders with the same factory and unchanged structure, 29% improved (n=31). The structure is the variable, not the supplier (Claim 2.11).

Named cases (Marcus, Sophie, Maren, Nadia, Daniel, Victor, Amara) are Tier 3 illustrative composites built from clusters of documented orders. Quantitative case-level details illustrate mechanism, not population estimates. The dataset is practice-derived and author-coded; inter-rater reliability review (Workstream C, Cohen's kappa) is in progress and will be reported separately. The full claims register, sample sizes, tier labels, and methodological caveats are reproduced in Appendix B of the underlying manuscript.

detail.title: Causonomy: A Formal Science of Failure and Causation in Normative Systems
detail.abstract: Problem solving is universally practised yet lacks a formal scientific foundation. Existing approaches rely on heuristic search, domain expertise, or probabilistic inference because failure has not been defined as a closed and enumerable object. This paper introduces Causonomy, a science in which failure is defined as a measurable deviation between a required state 𝑅(𝑓)and an observed state 𝑂(𝑓)at an activity boundary.

detail.abstract: Startups face a persistent tension between operational efficiency and continuous innovation. While standardization enables scalability, excessive rigidity can hinder adaptability in dynamic markets. This study proposes an 80/20 operational framework, where 80% of organizational activities are standardized for efficiency and predictability, and 20% are deliberately reserved for innovation and experimentation. Using a qualitative multiple-case approach supported by founder interviews and operational analysis, the study examines how startups implement and benefit from this balance. Findings indicate that startups applying structured standardization alongside controlled innovation buffers achieve improved operational efficiency, reduced waste, and faster adaptation to market changes. The study contributes a practical framework for founders seeking scalable yet flexible operating systems.

title: Final Draft: Semiconductor Value Chain

detail.title: Final Draft: Semiconductor Value Chain
detail.abstract: The capital pouring into the semiconductor industry is driven by AI-driven growth prospects and geopolitically driven demand. However, this influx of capital has overlooked the industry's structural complexity. The semiconductor industry's heterogeneity lies in its segmentation across Design, Fabrication, OSAT, Equipment and Chemicals. Each segment has unique value propositions, constraints, unit economics (e.g., wafer cost, yield), and competitive dynamics. To unlock defensible positions in early-stage investments, this paper adopts a multi-faceted approach, combining market sizing (TAM-SAM-SOM) with Porter's Five Forces and financial viability assessment (capital intensity vs margin matrix). By integrating these frameworks, we can identify areas where an investment can not only generate returns but also establish a lasting presence in the market. The framework culminates in Roger Martin's Cascade, which enables us to translate analytical insights into actionable strategic outcomes. Our analysis yields a decisive outcome: three categories are eliminated due to insurmountable barriers to entry, while one remains as a conviction. Fabrication is first to go, not because of profitability concerns, but because the required capital outlay is inaccessible without a sovereign balance sheet. This highlights a critical distinction between potential investments: those that require significant upfront costs and those that do not. The Design segment emerges as the most promising option, boasting an impressive 61.2% gross margin and lowest capital intensity at 1.9%. Its massive TAM of $209.9B further solidifies its appeal. More importantly, our analysis reveals that Fierce Competition and Buyer Power, the primary constraints on profitability in this space, can be strategically mitigated by targeting sub-segments. This playbook is not novel; NVIDIA's success with AI accelerators, Qualcomm's dominance in mobile baseband, and AMD's current foray into adaptive SOCs demonstrate the efficacy of "going narrow" to overcome these challenges. Industry Architecture & Segmentation Semiconductors sit at the core of the AI economy, but treating the semiconductor value chain as a monolithic investment would be a critical error. It is not one industry. It is a stack of structurally different businesses. Each with distinct economics, bottlenecks, and sources of advantage.

title: A Constraint-Driven Product Development Cycle: Evidence from Iterative Startup Environments

detail.title: A Constraint-Driven Product Development Cycle: Evidence from Iterative Startup Environments

detail.abstract: This study proposes the Constraint-Driven Product Development Cycle (CDPDC), a framework that repositions resource limitations-time, capital, team size, and technical debt-as active structural inputs to iterative product development rather than background conditions to be minimized. Drawing on qualitative multi-case analysis of early-stage startups, the study finds that constraint-driven teams achieved iteration cycles approximately 30-40% shorter than lower-constraint counterparts, with measurably lower feature waste and higher rates of productmarket alignment. Three mechanisms explain these outcomes: constraints force ruthless scoping in the Create stage, limit hypothesis-testing to high-priority experiments, and necessitate efficient feedback collection. Founders who reframed constraints as design variables reported stronger team alignment and fewer postlaunch prioritization regrets. The CDPDC extends and complements Lean Startup and Agile frameworks by making constraint-awareness an explicit structural element of the iteration loop, and offers targeted practical guidance for founders on designing and managing constraint frameworks across startup lifecycle stages. Note: Select figures and conceptual models in this paper were developed with the assistance of generative AI tools. The author maintains full responsibility for the content and accuracy.

detail.abstract: In startup ecosystems, profit is often treated as a primary objective or delayed outcome, frequently subordinated to growth strategies. This study challenges that perspective by conceptualizing profit as an emergent outcome of interconnected organizational systems rather than a directly pursued goal. Building on a systemsbased framework integrating leadership alignment (passion), human capital (people), product-market fit (product), and operational efficiency (process), this research examines how the interaction of these dimensions produces sustainable profitability. Using a qualitative multi-case approach supported by founder interviews and operational analysis, the study finds that startups achieving internal alignment across these dimensions generate consistent profitability without prioritizing profit as an isolated target. The findings contribute to entrepreneurship literature by reframing profit as a systemic consequence and offer practical implications for founders seeking sustainable growth. Note: Select figures and conceptual models in this paper were developed with the assistance of generative AI tools. title: Russia and System Disruption: A Signal-Pattern Analysis of Transformational Strategic Behaviour

detail.title: Russia and System Disruption: A Signal-Pattern Analysis of Transformational Strategic Behaviour

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This article applies the Signal-Pattern Analysis (SPA) framework (Tymoshenko, 2026) to analyse Russia’s strategic behaviour as a distinct configuration of disruptive signalling patterns within the contemporary international system. Rather than interpreting Russia’s actions solely through conventional categories of competition or conflict, the analysis focuses on the functional structure of observable signals and their aggregation into patterns that indicate a qualitatively different strategic logic. Using SPA, the study identifies and classifies military-coercive, institutional, and informational signals and interprets them within a dual-layer analytical structure that distinguishes between their functional role and broader strategic meaning.

The findings demonstrate that Russia’s behaviour does not primarily aim at managing or expanding the existing system as such, but at transforming its structural conditions. Instead, it produces a pattern of strategic destabilisation directed at altering the structural and normative conditions of international interaction. The article introduces the concept of a disruptive strategic pattern, in which influence is generated through the selective destabilisation of institutional arrangements, the erosion of normative consensus, and the creation of systemic uncertainty.

This pattern reflects a strategy of transformation rather than adaptation, operating through the reconfiguration of the environment in which other actors must operate. The analysis further shows that contemporary global dynamics are shaped by the coexistence of structurally distinct signal-pattern configurations. While some actors pursue control-oriented or expansion-based strategies, Russia’s behaviour represents a third type of strategic logic centred on disruption and systemic transformation. SPA thus provides a framework for identifying and differentiating these configurations within a unified analytical approach.

detail.abstract: This paper is the result of real practice, not just theory. Over the course of a year, a range of training programmes were designed and delivered across an organisation, and what unfolded was genuinely surprising, even for someone who already believed in the power of training. People changed. Relationships changed. The organisation itself changed. What had been a culture of silence, hidden frustrations, and quiet dysfunction began to open up. Employees who were previously reluctant to speak found their voice. Conflicts that were once buried started to come to the surface, and because they came to the surface, they could actually be addressed. This paper attempts to document and explore why that happened. It looks at Training Needs Analysis (TNA) and its role in the employee life cycle, why leaders must be part of the training journey, how training addresses conflict and builds alignment, and what makes training so uniquely valuable for NGO workers who carry emotional burdens most people never see. The paper draws on a year of lived experience, and the intention is that it reads that way.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Employment and Workforce in Business Organizations

detail.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Employment and Workforce in Business Organizations
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the growing impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on employment and organizational dynamics from a business management perspective. While AI adoption is increasing rapidly across firms, its effects are more evolutionary than revolutionary, with improvements in individual productivity but limited evidence of large-scale organizational transformation.

The study highlights a “productivity paradox,” where performance gains are visible, yet structural changes in work processes remain gradual. AI is reshaping workforce composition by reducing routine and clerical roles while increasing demand for skilled, technical, and AI-augmented positions. This shift reflects labor reallocation rather than simple job displacement.

A key finding is the divergence in expectations between executives and employees, with leaders anticipating workforce reductions and employees expecting job growth. Additionally, concerns regarding job security and workforce readiness underline the importance of reskilling and upskilling initiatives.

Evidence from European firms suggests that AI adoption can enhance productivity and wages without significantly affecting short-term employment levels. The paper concludes that organizations must treat AI as a core strategic tool, focusing on inclusive growth, continuous skill development, and effective communication to successfully navigate the evolving future of work.

title: GENDERED STRUCTURAL INTELLIGENCE: WOMEN'S SYSTEMCRAFT AND THE ADAPTIVE ETHICS OF CONSTRAINT IN PATRIARCHAL ORGANIZATIONAL ENVIRONMENTS

detail.title: GENDERED STRUCTURAL INTELLIGENCE: WOMEN'S SYSTEMCRAFT AND THE ADAPTIVE ETHICS OF CONSTRAINT IN PATRIARCHAL ORGANIZATIONAL ENVIRONMENTS

The research does not involve clinical intervention, patient data, or formal experimental procedures. Participant confidentiality is maintained throughout.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Gendered Structural Intelligence (GSI) as a new theoretical construct in cross-cultural organizational behavior and women’s leadership development. Drawing on sustained practitioner observation across private healthcare systems in Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and humanitarian operations in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, the paper argues that existing frameworks — including Acker’s gendered organizations theory (1990), Hochschild’s emotional labor thesis (1983), and Kandiyoti’s patriarchal bargain (1988) — are necessary but insufficient. Each names what patriarchal structures do to women. None theorizes what women construct in response. GSI proposes that women leaders in high-constraint patriarchal environments do not merely survive within patriarchal systems — they redirect them, making the system an unwitting instrument of change while rewarding it with the credit it requires to remain satisfied. The system becomes complicit in its own transformation without knowing it is being transformed. GSI is proposed as a second-order expression of Structural Navigation Competency (Marsh 2026), comprising three dimensions: Legitimacy Weaving — the relational construction of credible authority through alliance and selective visibility; Constraint Translation — the cognitive reframing of structural limitation into organizational design parameters; and Ethical Systemcraft — the moral intelligence to transform unjust systems while preserving the dignity of all actors within them. Implications for feminist organizational theory, women’s leadership development, and cross-cultural HR strategy are discussed.

title: Beyond the Score: A Hybrid Framework Combining Ridge Regression with Large Language Models for Actionable Net Promoter Score Analysis

detail.title: Beyond the Score: A Hybrid Framework Combining Ridge Regression with Large Language Models for Actionable Net Promoter Score Analysis
detail.abstract: The Net Promoter Score (NPS) remains one of the most widely adopted customer experience metrics, yet organizations consistently struggle to translate NPS data into actionable operational improvements. This paper presents a hybrid analytical framework that combines ridge regression with large language model (LLM) interpretation to bridge the gap between customer satisfaction measurement and operational decision-making. The framework operates on two complementary axes-quantitative and qualitative, external (survey) and internal (business context)-to produce segment-level insights that identify both which customer segments and operational levers drive NPS variation and why, using customers' own verbatim responses as evidence. Ridge regression is selected over tree-based alternatives for its ability to produce signed, interpretable coefficients for each feature, which then serve as directional hypotheses for LLM-guided qualitative analysis. A multi-stage feature selection process employing recursive cross-validated elimination, statistical significance filtering, and hyperparameter optimization ensures coefficient reliability. The framework was deployed on a B2B customer satisfaction survey (n = 775, 88 features), reducing analysis time from approximately one week of manual effort to under 40 minutes while producing a comprehensive 20-page analytical report. The ridge regression model achieved an R² of 0.49, explaining approximately half of NPS variance through segment-level drivers. Operational experience during development indicates that statistically directed LLM analysis produces markedly more specific and actionable insights than either method in isolation. The framework generalizes to any domain combining quantitative outcomes with unstructured text, including CSAT, Customer Effort Score, employee engagement, and churn prediction.

title: Decentralised Currency Hedging: Transatlantic Remittances and the Spanish Peseta, 1870-1936

detail.title: Decentralised Currency Hedging: Transatlantic Remittances and the Spanish Peseta, 1870-1936

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no relevant or material financial interests that relate to the research described in this paper.

detail.abstract: Between 1870 and 1936, the Spanish transatlantic diaspora remitted substantial capital to their home country. However, how these decentralised networks navigated severe macroeconomic instability without formal state intervention remains a puzzle. This paper compares Constant and Dynamic Conditional Correlation specifications to evaluate transatlantic financial integration. The empirical results reveal significant volatility clustering and a positive, statistically significant conditional correlation between remittance growth and real exchange rate shocks. While the annual data frequency favours the more parsimonious constant model, the stability of this correlation across specifications is consistent with structural currency-hedging behaviour. Conversely, results reveal no conditional correlation with isolated domestic inflation or nominal exchange rate fluctuations. Additionally, a rolling volatility analysis demonstrates a structural shift in the network's resilience after 1900, in line with the idea that technological maturity enabled migrants to process and dissipate shocks more efficiently than in the nineteenth century. Findings align with the view that migrants did not act as simple currency speculators, but rather successfully synthesised qualitative domestic price reports with international financial data to target the real exchange rate. In the absence of formal state insurance, migrant networks operated as an integrated macroeconomic hedge, systematically adjusting their transfers to shield domestic households from the devaluation of the peseta.

detail.abstract: Centralized procurement sharply lowers drug prices, but competitive pressure may incentivize quality deterioration-a moral hazard problem with large welfare consequences. Using China's national drug procurement rollout and universal hospital transaction data, we provide evidence of this quality-price tradeoff. Winning firms are more likely to change manufacturing processes post-award, some consistent with quality reduction. Hospitals assigned to winners that altered packaging materials exhibit greater utilization increases, suggesting compensatory dosing. Prior branded-drug users resist switching to winning generics but use higher doses when switching. Accounting for compensation, the effective price reduction is 3-18 percentage points smaller than the headline 64%.

detail.abstract: India has built strong digital public infrastructure, yet most MSMEs remain outside formal credit. This paper argues that the issue is not the lack of data, but how that data is used in lending decisions. It introduces the Digital Identity Credit Readiness Model (DICRM), which explains how business identity, transaction activity, and data-sharing systems can support credit access. The paper also highlights incidental signals—everyday activities such as transactions and tax filings that can indicate creditworthiness. It suggests that digital data translates into credit only when the broader system is ready, including clear rules, capable lenders, active enterprises, and borrower awareness.

title: Asymmetry of Meaning

detail.title: Asymmetry of Meaning

keywords: asymmetry of meaning; interpretive entropy; institutional legitimacy; consequence; systems thinking; democratic breakdown; spectacle governance; accountability; meaning making; institutional decay; rule of law; public trust; governance; social systems; political economy; civic resilience; complexity; institutional design

detail.abstract: Contemporary institutional breakdown is often explained through distrust, polarisation, technological disruption, inequality, or failed leadership. This paper argues that these visible pressures reflect a deeper structural disorder: asymmetry of meaning. The concept describes a condition in which action, consequence, accountability, and interpretation become unevenly distributed across social, political, and institutional systems. The paper develops the claim that meaning is generated through proximity to consequence, and that modern systemsthrough delegation, abstraction, optimisation, financialization, bureaucracy, metrics, platforms, and spectacle-often increase the distance between those who decide, those who absorb consequences, and those authorised to explain what has happened. The result is not immediate collapse, but interpretive entropy: systems remain active while becoming less intelligible, less trusted, and less legitimate. Using healthcare, housing, democracy, rule of law, NATO, and the United Nations as illustrative cases, the paper shows how meaning deficits can accumulate before performance deficits become visible. It also examines how wealth and power direct asymmetry, how weakened systems become probeable, and why spectacle often compensates for meaning loss without restoring consequence. The paper concludes that many contemporary institutions do not simply need more information, communication, or control. They need rebuilt consequence pathways through which action, accountability, and shared meaning can be reconnected.

title: Reconsidering "Why Do People Dislike Inflation?"
affiliations: Florida Atlantic University and Florida Atlantic University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Reconsidering "Why Do People Dislike Inflation?"
detail.abstract: In a widely-cited article, Shiller (1997) found that the public dislikes inflation to a greater extent than economists-and dislikes inflation for different reasons. We fielded a contemporary version of Shiller's survey in order to consider how economists' and the public's views on inflation have changed over time. We find that, in some respects, economists' views on inflation more closely resemble those of the public in our survey than was originally reported by Shiller (1997). But important differences remain.

title: Memory Arms Race in Q-Learning: How Memory Asymmetry Shapes Algorithmic Collusion in Sequential Pricing
affiliations: Warsaw School of Economics (SGH) and Warsaw School of Economics (SGH) - Institute of Econometrics

detail.title: Memory Arms Race in Q-Learning: How Memory Asymmetry Shapes Algorithmic Collusion in Sequential Pricing
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how memory asymmetry-differences in the depth of state representation-affects algorithmic collusion in a sequential pricing duopoly where Q-learning agents learn to coordinate. We first extend the framework of Klein (2021) by confirming that symmetric one-period memory algorithms converge to collusive outcomes in about two-thirds of simulations, establishing a robust baseline. We then introduce two asymmetric configurations: (i) one algorithm has no memory while the other has one-period memory; (ii) one algorithm has one-period memory while the other has two-period memory. In the first asymmetric case, both agents earn equal supra-competitive profits and always converge to a Nash equilibrium-a substantially more stable outcome than the symmetric benchmark. In the second, the deeper-memory agent earns a modest profit advantage, and Nash equilibrium rates remain high (over 95%), but learning is significantly slower due to the larger state space. These results reveal a positive externality: a firm's profit depends on its rival's memory depth, creating an incentive for a memory arms race-firms benefit when competitors adopt deeper memory. Yet contrary to the concern that heterogeneity undermines collusion, we find that memory asymmetry can actually stabilise collusion, shifting coordination from prices to algorithm design. This "meta-game" of algorithmic sophistication carries important implications for competition policy.

detail.abstract: This article examines the role of professional business administrators in leading and sustaining organizational change within transitional economies, with particular reference to Eastern European institutional contexts. Drawing on empirical observations from multi-sector professional practice spanning telecommunications, education, cultural institutions, and civic administration, this study identifies key administrative leadership strategies that enable organizations to navigate structural transformation while maintaining operational continuity. The findings demonstrate that effective change management in transitional environments requires interdisciplinary administrative capability, cross-functional coordination competence, and a strategic orientation that extends well beyond conventional task management. The article further argues that business administration professionals with experience across diverse institutional settings are uniquely positioned to serve as catalysts for sustainable organizational transformation, and proposes a practical framework for change leadership applicable across sectors.

title: FVI-24: A Food Value Index for Quantifying Preservation-Induced Nutritional Depletion and Additive Burden Using AI-Powered Evidence Synthesis

declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: Food product labels declare nutritional content at the point of manufacture, yet provide no information about what the consumer actually receives after preservation processing, additive treatment, or chronic cumulative exposure to food chemicals across multiple products consumed daily. This paper introduces the Food Value Index (FVI-24), a novel dual-scale scoring framework that quantifies the gap between declared and delivered nutrition while independently characterising the chemical additive burden of processed food products. The FVI score is computed as FVI = 24 × Σ(w × P), where P = Π R represents the cumulative retention of nutrient n across all preservation methods m applied to the product, and w are nutritional importance weights derived from WHO Dietary Reference Intake literature. Retention factors R are calibrated from a Bayesian meta-analysis of published food science studies across eight major preservation modalities. The output maps to a 0-24 carat gold scale alongside a percentage Delivered Nutrition Index (DNI%) for dual-register communication.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper Series

detail.abstract: We exploit the variation in the rollout of refrigerated almond milk across U.S. retail stores from 2008 through 2010 to estimate the causal effects on cow's milk and soymilk. Using monthly retail store scanner data, we find that introducing almond milk reduced retail quantities of soymilk (3.6%) and lactose-free cow's milk (3%), with smaller effects on organic (2%) and conventional cow's milk (1%). Effects are larger in stores that adopt earlier or reach higher almond milk shares. Our econometric estimates indicate significant displacement of per capita consumption of soymilk and lactose-free cow's milk, but not for conventional cow's milk.

title: THE INFLUENCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON DIGITAL BUYING BEHAVIOR

detail.title: THE INFLUENCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON DIGITAL BUYING BEHAVIOR
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has become one of the most consequential forces reshaping digital commerce, altering not merely how goods are displayed but how consumers think, decide, and act during online purchase journeys. This paper examines the mechanisms through which AI technologiesincluding recommendation engines, conversational chatbots, personalization algorithms, predictive analytics, and visual searchinfluence digital buying behavior across the consumer decision-making process. Drawing on a systematic review of peer-reviewed literature, industry reports, and empirical studies published between 2019 and 2024, we analyze both the behavioral and psychological dimensions of AI-mediated shopping experiences, with specific attention to cognitive biases that AI systems are designeddeliberately or inadvertentlyto activate. We compare pre-AI and post-AI digital buying patterns, document real-world deployments across major platforms such as Amazon, Netflix, Alibaba, and Shopify, and situate our analysis within current debates about data privacy, algorithmic manipulation, and consumer autonomy. Our findings suggest that AI substantially increases purchase conversion rates and consumer satisfaction under certain conditions, yet simultaneously introduces ethical risksincluding filter bubbles, dark patterns, and discriminatory pricingthat remain inadequately addressed by existing regulatory frameworks. We conclude by identifying critical gaps in the current literature, particularly regarding longitudinal effects on consumer agency and the crosscultural applicability of AI persuasion models.

title: A study on Sales and Promotion Strategies in the Newspaper Industry

detail.title: A study on Sales and Promotion Strategies in the Newspaper Industry
detail.abstract:
This project report, titled “A Study on Sales and Promotion Strategies in the Newspaper Industry,” focuses on understanding the sales, advertisement, and promotional techniques used in the newspaper industry, with special reference to Hindustan Times (HT Media Ltd.). The study examines how effective sales promotion strategies help in increasing newspaper circulation, attracting new readers, and maintaining customer loyalty in a highly competitive market. It also highlights the role of direct sales programs, subscription schemes, discounts, coupons, and supplementary pullouts such as HT Education, HT Café, HT Shine, and HT Weekend in improving customer engagement and boosting sales.
The research includes fieldwork conducted in Noida, where customer behavior, newspaper preferences, and market competition were analyzed through direct interaction with readers and potential subscribers. Major competitors such as The Times of India, The Tribune, The Hindu, and Indian Express were also studied to compare promotional approaches and market positioning. The project identifies key challenges faced during fieldwork, including customer resistance, preference for regional newspapers, competition from digital news platforms, and limited promotional offers.
The findings reveal that readers prefer newspapers with strong regional coverage, better presentation, and valuable supplementary content. The study concludes that improving service quality, increasing regional news coverage, enhancing promotional schemes, and maintaining strong customer relationships are essential for sustaining market leadership. This report provides useful insights into how effective sales and promotion strategies can support growth and competitive advantage in the newspaper industry.

detail.title: Building Brands for a Sustainable Future: Integrating Strategy, Consumer Response and Ethical Communication

publicationDetails.detailsText: Asian Journal of Economics, Business and Accounting, volume 25, issue 5, 2025[10.9734/ajeba/2025/v25i51800]

detail.abstract: Aims: This review aims to explore how sustainable branding contributes to long-term brand equity through the integration of strategic positioning, consumer emotional engagement, and ethical communication. It addresses issues of consumer cynicism and brand distrust in the alignment between sustainability messaging and corporate behaviour and examines how brands can foster trust, loyalty, and authenticity through cohesive, transparent strategies. Study Design: The review is structured around three core thematic domains: (1) strategic integration of sustainability into brand positioning, (2) consumer response and emotional value, and (3) ethical communication and message credibility. These domains were derived from a thematic synthesis of recent academic literature across multiple stakeholder, psychological, and communicative dimensions of branding. Methodology: A structured narrative review was conducted, focusing on peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2014 and 2024. Using databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, a refined set of keywords was applied using Boolean operators. Screening criteria excluded grey literature and conference papers to ensure academic rigor. Selected studies were coded and synthesised through thematic clustering based on recurring patterns in sustainable branding literature. Results: Findings highlight that successful sustainable branding requires embedding stakeholderbased brand equity, co-creation, and Triple Bottom Line (TBL) values at the strategic core. Emotional resonance and perceived authenticity drive consumer engagement, especially among value-driven cohorts like Generation Z. However, trust is fragile and easily eroded by greenwashing. Ethical communication, anchored in verifiable claims and cultural sensitivity, serves as a decisive factor in sustaining brand credibility. Psychological and demographic moderators significantly influence message interpretation. Conclusion: Sustainable branding demands a paradigm shift away from traditional marketing tactics toward strategic authenticity, participatory stakeholder engagement, and transparent communication. Future research should explore the roles of digital platforms, message framing, and socio-psychological variables in shaping sustainable brand equity across diverse consumer groups.

detail.title: AI-Driven Marketing Capabilities and Competitive Advantage: A Strategic Framework for Digital Commerce Firms in Emerging Economies

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing and digital commerce by enabling data-driven, personalized consumer engagement. This paper proposes the AI-Driven Marketing Capability (ADMC) Model, integrating strategic capabilities, technological infrastructure, consumer behavior, and institutional context to explain competitive advantage in emerging economies. Building on established theories, the study highlights how AI adoption generates compounding advantages while creating structural asymmetries across firm types. Using secondary evidence and illustrative cases, the findings show that sustainable advantage depends on the alignment of data capabilities, strategy, and ecosystem support. The paper contributes a policy-relevant framework and outlines directions for future empirical research.

title: Transformasi Strategik, Struktural, dan Legislatif Kesatuan Sekerja Sabah: Satu Ulasan Naratif Mendepani Hegemoni Ekonomi Digital

detail.title: Transformasi Strategik, Struktural, dan Legislatif Kesatuan Sekerja Sabah: Satu Ulasan Naratif Mendepani Hegemoni Ekonomi Digital
detail.abstract: Peralihan paradigma ke arah ekonomi digital dan integrasi Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) telah mencabar relevansi tradisional kesatuan sekerja di seluruh dunia. Artikel ulasan naratif ini bertujuan untuk menyintesis literatur semasa bagi mengenal pasti pembaharuan strategi, struktur, dan dasar yang diperlukan oleh kesatuan sekerja di Sabah untuk kekal mampan. Menggunakan pendekatan ulasan naratif, kajian ini meneroka pangkalan data akademik utama seperti Scopus dan Web of Science untuk menganalisis trend global serta realiti sosioekonomi di Borneo. Analisis tematik mendedahkan empat tema kritikal: impak pengurusan algoritmik global, kekangan infrastruktur digital di Sabah, krisis kepercayaan antara pemegang taruh, dan kelompangan kerangka perundangan buruh sedia ada. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa tanpa transformasi daripada model advokasi konvensional kepada model "kesatuan digital" (digital unionism), organisasi pekerja di Sabah berisiko menghadapi kepupusan fungsional. Implikasi ulasan ini menekankan keperluan mendesak terhadap pindaan Akta Kesatuan Sekerja 1959 dan penyediaan geran khas untuk literasi teknologi. Artikel ini menyumbang kepada korpus ilmu dengan menawarkan kerangka tindakan strategik bagi memastikan perlindungan sosial pekerja di wilayah membangun kekal utuh dalam mengharungi Revolusi Perindustrian 4.0.

detail.abstract: This narrative review examines the essential role of trust in shaping consumer purchase intentions within social commerce, particularly through mechanisms such as peer-generated content, platform security, and influencer marketing. It explores how cognitive and emotional trust interact within the consumer decision-making process and identifies practical and theoretical implications for trust-building strategies in social commerce. A comprehensive review of the literature on trust in social commerce was conducted to assess the impact of cognitive and emotional trust, and to investigate moderating and mediating factors including perceived risk, social support, and cultural differences. The review also highlights gaps in existing studies, providing recommendations for future research. The findings reveal that trust mitigates perceived risks and enhances consumer engagement, with cognitive trust supporting rational evaluations and emotional trust fostered through social interactions. Peer-generated content, secure platforms, and authentic influencer endorsements are identified as critical trust-building mechanisms, though concerns over content authenticity remain significant. Cultural and demographic differences act as important moderators, highlighting the need for region-specific trust strategies within social commerce. This review contributes to a differentiated understanding of trust in social commerce by examining the distinct roles of cognitive and emotional trust. It extends existing theoretical frameworks by incorporating elements such as social presence and cultural context, advancing the study of trust and providing actionable insights for trust management in diverse social commerce environments.

title: A STUDY ON THE CUSTOMER SATISFACTION USING DISCONFIMATION OF EXPECTATIONS WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE DOMINOS'S PIZZA

detail.title: A STUDY ON THE CUSTOMER SATISFACTION USING DISCONFIMATION OF EXPECTATIONS WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE DOMINOS'S PIZZA
detail.abstract: This research investigates the operational and psychological drivers of customer satisfaction through the lens of the Expectancy Disconfirmation Model, using the global operations of Domino’s Pizza as a primary case study. As a brand integrated across diverse digital platforms—including Twitter, Slack, and zero-click delivery apps—Domino’s provides a high-velocity environment for testing user expectations. The study evaluates how multi-dimensional factors, such as localized product variety, pricing consistency, and digital delivery efficiency, contribute to the user's perception of value. By measuring the relationship between pre-purchase expectations and post-purchase performance, this paper identifies the triggers for both positive and negative disconfirmation. The findings offer strategic recommendations for improving customer retention by narrowing the expectancy-performance gap, providing a scalable framework for service optimization in the digital economy.

title: Robotics in Retail: Identifying the Feasibility Threshold in Order Fulfillment
affiliations: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Department of Technology and Operations Management

detail.title: Robotics in Retail: Identifying the Feasibility Threshold in Order Fulfillment
detail.abstract: Offering omnichannel services such as buy-online-pickup in store (BOPS) and ship-from-store (BOSS) significantly increases the demand on in-store logistical operations. Driven by labor shortages and technological opportunities, robotic solutions can help solve the problem. As technology continues to advance, it is essential to determine the minimum robot capabilities (the ratio of articles that can be picked by such robots) to ensure economic viability. We present a novel Semi-Open Queuing Network (SOQN) approach to evaluate the impact of a hybrid robotic-human in-store order fulfillment system and analyze its effects on throughput capacity, fulfillment cost, and in-store shopper blocking. The model is solved for the steady-state probabilities using the Matrix Geometric Method and validated through agent-based, discrete-event simulation. We present results for several real-world use cases that demonstrate that even at low capabilities (only 50% of the articles are pickable by robots), the use of robots is economically beneficial. A hybrid approach of combining human and robotic resources leads to cost savings of up to 40% compared to a purely manual system. Robotic resources at high capability levels can also substantially reduce human effort. The results underscore the importance of robot pick failure rates: reliable low-capability robots can be more economical than higher-capability robots with greater failure rates. Finally, the results also show that the negative impact on in-store shoppers due to blocked shelves is limited.

title: The Longevity of Public Sector IT: Disproving the "Mega-Vendor" Incumbency Myth Utilizing Dynamic Random Forest Diagnostics on USAspending Data

detail.title: The Longevity of Public Sector IT: Disproving the "Mega-Vendor" Incumbency Myth Utilizing Dynamic Random Forest Diagnostics on USAspending Data
detail.abstract: The United States federal government spends over $100 billion annually on information technology. A prevailing industry assumption asserts that "Mega-Vendors"-the top multinational systems integratorsstructurally dominate and secure decade-spanning infrastructure deployments due to lobbying power and deeply entrenched vendor lock-in. Conversely, midmarket technology firms are historically stereotyped as providers of short-term, highly transactional agreements. This paper subjects this operating assumption to rigorous data science evaluation. By deploying dynamic Random Forest Classifiers against a longitudinal dataset spanning seven fiscal years (FY2018-FY2024), we map how the true statistical drivers of IT contract longevity shift over time dynamically. Evaluating 1,730 high-value federal IT contracts across four critical temporal thresholds (1, 3, 5, and 10 years), the models yield a mathematical repudiation of the incumbency myth. Expanding the corporate scale definition across the Top-50 largest federal integrators consistently yielded less than 6% predictive importance on 5-year and 10-year contract survival. By contrast, the initial financial scope of the primary award maintained over 90% Gini predictive importance. These findings mathematically demonstrate that mid-tier vendors are not intrinsically locked out of generational infrastructure pipelines if they scale their initial proposals.

detail.abstract: The internet is vital for schools, colleges, and businesses, but common issues like slow connections, cyberattacks, and unauthorized bandwidth use persist due to a lack of affordable oversight tools. To address this gap, we designed and developed the Network Performance Analyzer (NPA), a low-cost, Java-based system using JPcap/WinPcap to monitor and capture network traffic. Captured packets are filtered, exported to a CSV format, and visualized in Power BI (Business Intelligence) dashboards. Administrators can use the dashboards to track internet bandwidth usage and access protocols (PUA), identify anomalous behavior, and receive real-time warnings about potential risks. The tool is lightweight, easy to use, and supports a secure digital infrastructure, aligning with SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, Infrastructure) and SDG 4 (Quality Education). Future upgrades include AI-driven threat prediction, cloud storage, IoT support, and mobile functionality.

detail.abstract: Fenomena fissured workplace oleh David Weil merujuk kepada perubahan organisasi moden daripada pekerjaan berpusat kepada sistem berpecah melalui penyumberan luar, subkontrak, agensi pekerja, dan francais. Perubahan ini didorong oleh kecekapan kos, persaingan global, serta pendigitalan pasaran buruh. Kajian ini menganalisis bagaimana pengaturan kerja segitiga (pekerja–agensisyarikat induk) mempengaruhi struktur kuasa dalam hubungan pekerjaan, khususnya terhadap keupayaan pekerja menyertai kesatuan, menuntut hak kolektif, dan mengenal pasti majikan sebenar. Didapati wujud kekaburan antara “majikan formal” dan “majikan sebenar”, yang mewujudkan jurang akauntabiliti. Walaupun model ini meningkatkan kecekapan dan fleksibiliti organisasi, ia melemahkan perlindungan pekerja. Pekerja sering berada dalam pekerjaan tidak standard, menghadapi ketidakjaminan kerja, serta sukar mengakses hak asas seperti gaji adil dan perlindungan undangundang. Fragmentasi ini juga menyukarkan kesatuan sekerja berfungsi secara berkesan. Kesimpulannya, fenomena ini memerlukan reformasi dasar seperti pengiktirafan “majikan bersama”, pengukuhan perlindungan pekerja kontrak, dan strategi baharu kesatuan sekerja bagi memastikan keadilan dalam hubungan pekerjaan moden.
