title: Construction Risk Factor Management and Building Project Delivery in Akure, Ondo State, Nigeria
affiliations: Federal University of Technology, Akure, Nigeria, Federal University of Technology, Akure, Nigeria and Federal University of Technology, Akure, Nigeria

detail.title: Construction Risk Factor Management and Building Project Delivery in Akure, Ondo State, Nigeria

publicationDetails.detailsText: GVU Journal of Management and Social Sciences, Vol. 10, 2025, pp. 139–151. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18127597

detail.abstract: The current research examines how Construction Risk Factors Management (CRFM) influences building project delivery in Akure Metropolis, Ondo State in Nigeria, by adopting quantitative research design based on a survey study. The (391) identified registered professionals which included project architects, builders, engineers, managers and quantity surveyors were identified and a sample of (263) selected using purposive sampling depending on their experience in the construction industry. The data was gathered using self-administered questionnaires and therefore (219) responses were usable (an 83.3% response rate). The test was performed using the descriptive statistics, T-tests to determine the level of significance of different construction risk factors. Utilizing multiple linear regression analysis, the study quantified the contribution of these risk management practices to project outcomes. The results indicated that construction risk management explained 9.2% of the variance (𝑅 2 = 0.092) in building project delivery, demonstrating a modest but significant effect. Legal risks (Mean = 4.39) were identified as the most significant, mainly due to unresolved land or contract disputes and prolonged arbitration periods. Project management risks (Mean = 4.33), including design errors, inadequate site monitoring, and poor planning, were also found to significantly impact project delivery. Environmental risks (Mean = 4.33), caused by adverse weather, poor terrain, and insufficient waste management, posed additional challenges. Financial risks (Mean = 4.23), stemming from inflation, exchange rate fluctuations, and delayed payments, and safety risks (Mean = 4.11), linked to non-compliance with safety protocols, were also critical. Among the risk management practices, risk regulation (𝛽 = 0.191, 𝑃 = 0.043) emerged as the most influential, emphasizing the importance of compliance with safety standards and organizational policy enforcement. Risk assessment (𝛽 = 0.182, 𝑃 > 0.05) and risk identification (𝛽 = 0.054, 𝑃 > 0.05) were less impactful, likely due to their generic application rather than being tailored to specific project needs. Paired sample t-tests revealed a significant difference between internal risks (Mean = 4.58) and external risks (Mean = 4.23), with internal risks having a more substantial impact on project delivery. Despite the small effect size (Eta Squared = 0.03), internal risks such as organizational lapses, poor resource allocation, and weak communication were found to have a more detrimental influence compared to external risks. The study concludes that the legal risks were viewed to be the most common than project management, and environmental risks. Therefore, prioritizing risk regulation and enforcement of safety standards within construction firms, developing specific, project-based risk assessment and identification techniques, improving communication and resource management to mitigate internal risks, and providing training programs to enhance risk management skills among construction professionals is very essential.

title: Stingy Leaders: An Emerging Construct in Destructive Leadership
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Princeton University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Stingy Leaders: An Emerging Construct in Destructive Leadership
detail.abstract: Destructive leaders compromise the well-being and productivity of their workers. However, not all destructive leadership is directly harmful. Frugal leaders who withhold resources from workers may encourage their workers to do more with less. The virtue of being frugal can become a vice when taken to an extreme. In this paper, we argue that restricting worker access to available resources (including salary) is a novel form of destructive leadership, which we call “stingy” leadership. Stingy leadership is characterized by leaders who, despite resource availability, provide the absolute minimum resources allowed by law, for their employees. In developing stingy leadership, we drew on moral psychology to show that stingy leadership is distinct from abusive supervision and exploitative leadership because its harm is indirect and it does not stem from anger or callousness, but a misguided moral virtue. Nevertheless, stingy leadership creates compromises workplace outcomes (e.g., productivity, organizational citizenship behaviors, commitment). Because these harmful behaviors do not directly target employees, stingy leadership is harder to recognize as a form of destructive leadership. We end with practical implications for reducing stingy behavior work.

title: Automasi, Deskilling dan Polarisasi Pekerjaan: Analisis Ancaman Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif terhadap Pasaran Buruh Global dan Implikasinya kepada Sabah, Malaysia

detail.title: Automasi, Deskilling dan Polarisasi Pekerjaan: Analisis Ancaman Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif terhadap Pasaran Buruh Global dan Implikasinya kepada Sabah, Malaysia
detail.abstract: Latar Belakang: Kemunculan kecerdasan buatan generatif (KBG) seperti model bahasa besar (LLM) dan sistem automasi berasaskan pembelajaran mesin telah mempercepatkan transformasi struktur pasaran buruh global secara dramatik. Teknologi ini bukan sahaja mengancam pekerjaan rutin bersifat fizikal, malah semakin mendalam memasuki domain tugas kognitif yang selama ini dianggap eksklusif kepada kemahiran manusia. Objektif: Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mensintesiskan literatur semasa berkenaan tiga dimensi utama: (1) ancaman automasi KBG terhadap tugas kognitif dan fizikal rutin; (2) dikotomi antara augmentasi kemahiran pekerja berbanding proses deskilling; dan (3) impak polarisasi pasaran buruh, khususnya dalam konteks ekonomi Sabah, Malaysia yang bersandarkan sektor perkhidmatan dan industri primer. Metodologi: Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan sintesis naratif berasaskan analisis tematik Braun dan Clarke (2006), merangkumi 28 sumber primer yang dipilih daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar dalam tempoh 2015-2025. Dapatan: Empat tema utama muncul daripada sintesis: (i) kerangka teoritikal dualisme teknologi; (ii) bukti empirikal polarisasi pasaran buruh; (iii) kapasiti institusi dan keterbatasan respons dasar; dan (iv) inisiatif semula kemahiran sebagai strategi mitigasi. Di Sabah, struktur ekonomi yang bergantung kepada buruh intensif di sektor pertanian, pembuatan, dan pelancongan menjadikannya terdedah secara tidak proporsional kepada gelombang deskilling. Kesimpulan: Augmentasi manusia-AI merupakan trajektori yang lebih produktif berbanding substitusi sepenuhnya, namun memerlukan ekosistem dasar yang komprehensif merangkumi pendidikan, perlindungan sosial, dan pelaburan kemahiran digital yang inklusif.

title: The Need for a Neutral Exchange: A Unique Opportunity for Switzerland in the Emerging World Order
affiliations: INSEAD and INSEAD - Technology and Operations Management

detail.title: The Need for a Neutral Exchange: A Unique Opportunity for Switzerland in the Emerging World Order
detail.abstract: Rapidly evolving geopolitical and geoeconomic landscapes are creating a structural gap between diverging economic and financial systems. This gap creates the need for a widely trusted, neutral, and rules-based venue where participants from USD-centric and non-USD monetary systems can continue to interact, not only efficiently, but transparently, with legal certainty, and without the requirement of political alignment, monetary subordination, or exposure to extraterritorial legal and digital control. By history, fate, and the path it took, one country can like no other country address this growing divide between monetary systems: Switzerland. The country could host a "radically neutral exchange" providing a market-infrastructure layer that would enable issuers and investors from both systems to interact in their respective currencies under one clear legal and regulatory regime. It would require Switzerland to pursue a strategy of « principled neutrality » which be a strategic break from the country's more traditional passive and reactive postures. The proposed neutral exchange would provide continued economic exchange and mutual benefits associated with free trade, even in conditions of a disintegrating and fractioning geopolitical climate. It would move the financial and monetary world away from the current "exorbitant US privilege" to a more balanced and fairer "earned privilege" condition. By continuing conditions of mutual dependency, it would foster peaceful coexistence and reduce the possibility of armed conflict.

title: The Mediating Role of Employees' Resilience in the Relationship Between Workplace Bullying and Counter-Productive Work Behaviors (CWBs) (A Field Study on the Private Universities Employees in Damascus)

detail.title: The Mediating Role of Employees' Resilience in the Relationship Between Workplace Bullying and Counter-Productive Work Behaviors (CWBs) (A Field Study on the Private Universities Employees in Damascus)
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effect of workplace bullying on the counter-productive work behaviors (CWBs) in the private higher education sector, and examine whether there is any mediating role of employees' resilience in this relationship. To attain these objectives, data were collected from a sample of 462 employees in the private universities in Damascus. The measuring instruments included: The version of the Negative Acts Questionnaire-Revised (NAQ-R), the Connor Davidson Resilience (CD-RISC-10), and the Counter-Productive Work Behaviors Checklist (CWB, C) scales. The main findings of the study are: (1) All workplace bullying dimensions (Person-Related, Physical Intimidation, and Work-Related) significantly and positively affect counter-productive work behaviors; (2) All workplace bullying dimensions significantly and negatively affect employees' resilience; and (3) Employee's resilience fully mediates the relationship between workplace bullying and counter-productive work behaviors. This study suggests early interventions by the organizations to create a safe environment, and to develop training programs focused on employees' resilience to avoid aggressive and bullying behaviors.

publicationDetails.detailsText: GVU Journal of Management and Social Sciences, Vol. 10, 2025, pp. 23–34. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18112170

detail.abstract: This study investigates workplace norms and compliance with health and safety regulations in healthcare institutions in Akure, Ondo State, Nigeria. Workplace norms informal but influential rules within an organization are critical in determining how employees adhere to mandated safety practices such as the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), proper hand hygiene, medical waste disposal, and hazard reporting. The study employed a descriptive survey design using census sampling to gather primary data from 216 healthcare professionals, including doctors, nurses, technicians, and cleaners across public hospitals. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analysed using percentages and Pearson Product Moment Correlation (PPMC). Results revealed a strong positive and statistically significant relationship (r = 0.684, p < 0.01) between workplace norms and compliance with safety regulations. Specifically, peer influence, managerial modelling, and regular communication of safety expectations were found to increase compliance, while the normalization of unsafe behaviour reduced adherence. The study's findings align with previous empirical works such as Oluwafemi and Ajayi (2020) and Ekanem (2021), confirming that social and cultural elements within hospital environments significantly influence safety outcomes. Despite high compliance rates in PPE usage and waste disposal, hazard reporting remained a weak point, indicating a gap in the internalization of certain norms. The study concludes that promoting positive workplace norms is essential for sustaining a safe healthcare environment and recommends that hospital leadership reinforce safety through modelling, peer monitoring, and clear communication. Future research could explore the role of organizational policies in shifting negative informal norms.

title: How do Digital Technologies Mediate the Relationship Between Leaders' Moral Agency and Their Organizations? A Post-Phenomenological Approach

detail.title: How do Digital Technologies Mediate the Relationship Between Leaders' Moral Agency and Their Organizations? A Post-Phenomenological Approach
detail.abstract: Digital leadership (DL) is a rapidly developing area for theorizing and research. However, no theoretical view of morality is discussed in the literature on DL that can be helpful for both academics and practitioners. DL involves interactions between leaders with digital technologies (DTs) to perceive and interpret the world (the hermeneutic relation) and to impact the organization and its environment (the pragmatic relation). Based on the post-phenomenological approach, this paper proposes a mediated theory of leaders' morality on how DTs and human moral agency co-shape leaders' existence in their moral decision-making and actions in the digital world. The model explains how this technology can impact a leader's moral maturation capacities (e.g., moral sensitivity and moral identity) and augment or weaken conation moral capacities (e.g., moral ownership and moral efficacy). The model suggests that leaders interact with DTs to co-shape their moral processes and outcomes rather than consider the technology a distinct entity. An important part of the paper proposes some practical recommendations based on the framework provided in the paper to help educational and training professionals consider moral aspects of leadership development in their programs.

detail.abstract: Traditional demoscopy faces a structural validity crisis when attempting to categorize contemporary subjects through static, generational, or socioeconomic labels. This paper introduces a Multidimensional Ontology that conceptualizes the individual not as a fixed demographic unit, but as a system of internal tensions within a continuous state of transformation. By integrating Dynamic Clustering (unsupervised learning for real-time micro-cluster identification) and Multidimensional Narrative Analysis, we propose a "geometry of forces" to map social reality. The study demonstrates how individual concerns (micro-vectors) are pulled by systemic discourses (macro-vectors), creating resonance points that drive political or consumer action. This model transcends descriptive demographics to provide an operative capacity to synchronize with citizens amidst digital "infoxication" and shrinking attention spans.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether environmental design can support behavioral regulation during classroom transitions. Schools often absorb transition friction through teacher effort, repeated prompts, and lost instructional time while giving less attention to whether physical environments themselves shape these recurring costs. The paper proposes a regulation environment as a bounded setting designed to reduce uncertainty during transitions through repeated exposure to consistent cues and structured use. A pilot framework is presented using measures of transition length, teacher intervention, and disruptive behavior. If supported, the concept may have implications for operational efficiency, procurement logic, and category formation. If unsupported, the framework still creates value by narrowing future decisions through evidence.

detail.abstract:
In contemporary secondary mathematics education, the increasing reliance on mastery-based digital practice platforms has introduced a structural paradox: while enhancing efficiency and access to practice, these tools may inadvertently limit instructional access for students requiring guided support during complex problem-solving tasks. This study examines the intersection of instructional pacing, digital practice dependency, and student affect within a secondary geometry classroom.

Grounded in the Zone of Proximal Development (Vygotsky, 1978), Cognitive Load Theory (Sweller, 2011), and the Gradual Release of Responsibility model (Pearson & Gallagher, 1983), the case analysis identifies a critical Transition Gap between initial conceptual exposure and successful multi-step application. Two additional constructs are introduced: Breakdown Without Recovery, describing failure states within mastery-based digital environments that lack immediate instructional feedback, and Silent Failure Mode, characterized by cognitive disengagement driven by affective barriers to help-seeking.

Using a multi-modal case study approach (Creswell & Poth, 2017; Yin, 2018) that integrates instructional structure, platform interaction, and student-reported affective data, the study demonstrates how these conditions interact to produce sustained learning stagnation despite student effort. The study extends beyond conceptual analysis by incorporating a real-world classroom intervention developed collaboratively with the instructor. Implemented interventions — including a real-time support signaling system, structured scaffolding tools for multi-step problem-solving, dedicated instructional access periods, and adaptive adjustments to digital platform constraints — collectively restored instructional access at the point of need.

These findings provide applied validation of the proposed Multi-Tiered Instructional Access Framework (MTIAF), demonstrating that targeted instructional adjustments can effectively reduce cognitive load, remove affective barriers, and reestablish student learning progression. The study concludes that digital independence must remain secondary to human-mediated scaffolding, and that effective instructional design requires continuous alignment between cognitive readiness, instructional support, and classroom climate. This working paper contributes to a broader research program on instructional design, educational access, support-centered learning systems, and applied framework development.

title: Whitney M. Young Jr. and the 3 Ps of Leadership: Applied Principles for Leaders Across Sectors

detail.title: Whitney M. Young Jr. and the 3 Ps of Leadership: Applied Principles for Leaders Across Sectors

detail.abstract: Whitney M. Young Jr. is often remembered as a civil rights leader, yet his most enduring contribution may be what he modeled as a systems thinker, coalition builder, and applied leader across multiple institutional contexts. Drawing on Dennis C. Dickerson's biography, Militant Mediator: Whitney M. Young Jr. (1998), and the Leadership Lessons from Whitney M. Young, Jr. Teaching Guide (Franklin et al., 2009), this paper reexamines Young's 3 Ps of Leadership, Passion for People, Practical Solutions, and Pragmatic Thinking, not as a historical framework but as a living theory of change. Through an analysis of Young's leadership at the Atlanta University School of Social Work, the National Urban League, and the National Association of Social Workers, the paper argues that Young's effectiveness was rooted in strategic discipline, authentic identity, and the capacity to build coalitions across lines of difference without compromising his core convictions. The paper further argues that the 3 Ps constitute transferable, applied leadership principles relevant across sectors, including education, healthcare, social services, government, and community organizations. The paper concludes with three reflective questions designed to support practitioners in applying these principles within their own organizational and community contexts.

detail.title: The Meerkat Model Of Bio-Leadership: Using Biomimicry To Embody Leadership Principles In Children

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This study received no external funding. All sessions were conducted within the regular programme of Blue Blocks Montessori School, Hyderabad, India, under the research framework of the Blue Blocks Micro Research Institute.

detail.abstract: This paper reports a pilot study in Bio-leadership, which is a biomimicry-inspired learning activity. Here, the children don't just learn about nature, they step inside it and become a part of it. In this study, the 6-12-year-olds assumed roles and social dynamics within a meerkat colony. 9 sessions were conducted at Blue Blocks, Hyderabad, India. What was interesting was the missing data. There were no directions given regarding leadership, teamwork, or communication. But, even then, those very behaviours surfaced naturally, and repeatedly across all sessions as if the system knew what to do before the adults did. The activity began with a story-based introduction of meerkats, which was adapted from a biological model sourced from AskNature (Biomimicry Institute), so that the ideas were accessible across all age groups. For the older children, five separate challenge cards were introduced with ecological problems that required the group to think and act together for survival. The data for this study were collected through observation sheets and audiovisuals, which were later transcribed into text. Across 85 children some clear patterns emerged. Leadership roles were rotated without prompting by the children, they devised non-verbal signals to communicate danger and maintained the group coordination under simulated predator crisis scenarios. They started proposing design ideas for more efficient and safer colonies, which was an intuitive reaction to the biological model they were enacting. The age difference provided a different perspective, where the older children (9-12 years) showed more strategic thinking and empathy in group decisions. At the same time, the younger children (6-7 years) displayed just as much willingness to lead, but often through storytelling, social simulation, and physical expression, and not just verbal reasoning. This study comes up Blue Blocks Micro Research Institute • Working Paper with something that is simple but powerful: when observation of living systems grounds the leadership and not human hierarchies, the children seem to blend into it more intuitively. Bioleadership, as introduced here, offers a different learning point of entry, something that is embodied, ecological, and collaborative by design.

title: Predicting Employee Attrition and Organizational Performance in the Steel and Manufacturing Sector: A Study of Bhilai Steel Plant, Raipur, Chhattisgarh

detail.title: Predicting Employee Attrition and Organizational Performance in the Steel and Manufacturing Sector: A Study of Bhilai Steel Plant, Raipur, Chhattisgarh
detail.abstract: Employee attrition has emerged as one of the most critical human resource challenges in India's rapidly growing industrial sector. Despite extensive research at the national level, attrition dynamics in Tier-2 industrial cities such as Raipur, Chhattisgarh-home to over 200 steel and manufacturing enterprisesremain largely unexplored. This study investigates the key factors driving employee attrition and examines their impact on organizational performance in the steel and manufacturing sector, with specific reference to Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP). Using a descriptive and analytical research design, primary data was collected from 120 employees and HR managers at BSP through a structured 20-item Likert-scale questionnaire. The reliability of the instrument was confirmed through a Cronbach's Alpha of 0.846. Statistical tools including descriptive statistics, Pearson Correlation Analysis, and Multiple Regression Analysis were employed using SPSS. Findings reveal that lack of career growth opportunities (Mean = 2.28), salary dissatisfaction (Mean = 2.41), and excessive workload stress (Mean = 3.82) are the primary attrition drivers. The regression model explains 71.7% of variance in employees' intention to leave (R2 = 0.717, F = 46.83, p < 0.001). All six organizational performance indicators recorded mean scores above 3.70, confirming that attrition significantly erodes productivity, team morale, and operational efficiency. Both research hypotheses were accepted at the 1% level of significance. The study concludes with eight evidence-based HR recommendations for reducing attrition in the Raipur steel and manufacturing sector. This paper contributes a region-specific empirical dataset to the existing attrition literature and offers actionable insights for HR practitioners and policy makers.

title: Nepal's Current Economic Situation, Structural Constraints, and Policy Directions for a More Dynamic Economy

detail.title: Nepal's Current Economic Situation, Structural Constraints, and Policy Directions for a More Dynamic Economy
detail.abstract: This paper examines Nepal's current economic situation and develops a policy framework for making the economy more dynamic, productive, and employment-intensive. The central argument is that Nepal has regained a degree of macroeconomic stability, but this stability has not yet translated into broad-based structural transformation. Inflation has remained moderate, remittance inflows have strengthened the external position, and foreign exchange reserves are unusually comfortable. Yet growth remains below potential, private investment is subdued, employment generation is weak, and public capital spending continues to underperform. The paper therefore distinguishes between short-term stabilization and long-term transformation. It analyzes growth, inflation, revenue, trade, reserves, credit, employment, and investment conditions; diagnoses the deeper reasons behind Nepal's economic obstacles; and proposes strategies to strengthen production, productivity, and job creation. Particular attention is given to the relationship between fiscal policy and monetary policy. The paper argues that neither expansionary budgets nor accommodative monetary conditions are sufficient on their own. Nepal needs a coordinated policy mix in which credible fiscal prioritization, better capital expenditure execution, financial-sector stability, export capability, and an improved investment climate reinforce one another. The concluding sections outline practical directions for FY 2083/84, with emphasis on private sector promotion, project readiness, labour-market capability, industrial deepening, and institutional reform.

title: Frontiers in Operations: Prioritizing Disaster Recovery Under Budget Uncertainty
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Institute of Operations Research and Analytics, School of Business and Management, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, NUS Business School - Department of Decision Sciences and

detail.title: Frontiers in Operations: Prioritizing Disaster Recovery Under Budget Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Problem Definition: In the aftermath of disasters, governments must make urgent decisions about how to deploy limited resources for recovery, such as restoring roads or siting emergency facilities. However, these actions often need to be taken before the amount and timing of external funding (e.g., federal disaster relief) are known. This mismatch between the need for immediacy and the delay in budget realization poses a fundamental challenge: how can agencies prioritize recovery actions when budgets are uncertain and decisions, once made, are irreversible? Methodology/Results: We develop a practical planning framework that produces a fixed priority list of recovery actions, allowing agencies to act immediately and continue execution as funding arrives over time. The framework identifies early actions that perform well across a range of possible funding paths and preserve the value of later investments. The model is cast as a multi-scenario mixed-integer linear program with monotonicity constraints, enforcing consistency in prioritization across all scenarios. To compute such a list efficiently, while the natural LP relaxation of this formulation is weak, we introduce a pegging-based heuristic: for each scenario, we solve the optimal 0-1 allocation, fix it, and relax the remaining scenarios into a linear program. Aggregating across all scenarios yields a robust and interpretable prioritization list. Our analysis provides performance guarantees for committing to a single priority list instead of waiting for full budget information. We derive explicit bounds on the expected performance loss of any prioritization strategy relative to a full-information hindsight benchmark. These results show that, under modest assumptions, the loss from committing to a single priority list is provably small. Furthermore, our pegging-based heuristic yields approximation guarantees under mild conditions and performs remarkably well in empirical evaluations. Managerial Implications: This framework offers disaster response planners a rigorous and practical tool for making irreversible decisions under budget uncertainty. The main insight is that the best early action is not always the one that gives the largest immediate gain, but the one that positions the system best when additional funding becomes available. Through experiments on synthetic data and a real-world road network in Manhattan, we demonstrate that the proposed prioritization strategy consistently outperforms conventional heuristics and closely approximates the performance of an ideal benchmark with full budget information. The results highlight the potential of our approach to support timely, resilient, and high-quality disaster recovery planning under uncertain funding conditions.

detail.abstract:
Kemunculan ekonomi gig dan kerja berasaskan platform digital telah merombak secara fundamental definisi pekerja dalam pasaran buruh global. Artikel ulasan naratif ini bertujuan untuk mensintesis secara kritis literatur sedia ada mengenai bagaimana klasifikasi pekerja sebagai kontraktor bebas menyumbang kepada fenomena ketidakjaminan kerja (precarity), serta menilai implikasi struktur ini dalam konteks Sabah, Malaysia. Menggunakan pendekatan sintesis naratif, artikel ini menganalisis kajian empirikal dan konseptual daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar dalam tempoh sedekad yang lalu.

Dapatan analisis tematik mengenal pasti empat tema utama, yang pertama, transformasi konsep pekerjaan dalam ekonomi platform global, kedua, Mekanisme struktural yang memperkukuh ketidakjaminan kerja, ketiga,kapasiti dan batasan institusi dalam melindungi pekerja gig, dan terakhir, evolusi dasar serta perundangan berkaitan perlindungan sosial. Secara khusus, artikel ini menunjukkan bahawa klasifikasi sebagai kontraktor bebas membolehkan syarikat mengelakkan tanggungjawab sosial tradisional seperti gaji minimum, perlindungan kesihatan, dan keselamatan sosial, sekali gus mewujudkan kitaran ketidakstabilan pendapatan dan risiko pasaran yang tinggi.

Dalam konteks Sabah, faktor seperti ketidakseimbangan pembangunan wilayah, peluang pekerjaan formal yang terhad, dan penetrasi platform digital mempercepatkan kebergantungan kepada ekonomi gig. Artikel ini mencadangkan keperluan reformasi dasar yang holistik, termasuk kerangka hibrid klasifikasi pekerja, pengukuhan perlindungan sosial, dan strategi pembangunan tenaga kerja digital.

title: The Impact of Business Intelligence Systems on Supply Chain Performance

detail.title: The Impact of Business Intelligence Systems on Supply Chain Performance
detail.abstract: Business Intelligence (BI) systems have emerged as transformative tools in modern supply chain management, enabling organizations to harness data-driven insights for enhanced decision-making and operational excellence. This study investigates the impact of BI system adoption on supply chain performance across multiple dimensions, including forecasting accuracy, inventory optimization, supplier relationship management, and logistics efficiency. Employing a mixed-methods research design, data were collected from 178 supply chain professionals across manufacturing, retail, and logistics sectors using a structured questionnaire and follow-up interviews. The findings reveal that organizations with mature BI implementations achieve statistically significant improvements in demand forecasting accuracy (mean improvement of 23.4%), inventory turnover ratios, and order fulfillment rates compared to those relying on traditional reporting methods. Additionally, BI adoption is positively correlated with reduced lead times and lower total supply chain costs. Regression analysis identified BI integration depth, data quality, and organizational readiness as the strongest predictors of performance outcomes. This research contributes a conceptual framework for BI-driven supply chain transformation and offers actionable recommendations for practitioners seeking to maximize the strategic value of BI investments.

title: AI-Driven Demand Forecasting and Its Impact on Inventory Optimization Researcher

detail.title: AI-Driven Demand Forecasting and Its Impact on Inventory Optimization Researcher
detail.abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is the cornerstone of effective inventory management, yet traditional statistical models frequently fail to capture the nonlinear, high-dimensional patterns inherent in modern demand data. The emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniquesincluding Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Gradient Boosting algorithms, and hybrid ensemble models-has fundamentally reshaped the demand forecasting landscape, enabling organizations to achieve unprecedented accuracy improvements while simultaneously driving inventory optimization outcomes. This study investigates the impact of AI-driven demand forecasting systems on inventory optimization performance across manufacturing, retail, and consumer goods organizations. Using a mixed-methods research design, primary data were gathered from 204 operations and supply chain professionals through a structured questionnaire, supplemented by secondary data analysis of publicly reported inventory metrics. Findings demonstrate that organizations deploying AI-based forecasting models achieve statistically significant reductions in forecast error (Mean Absolute Percentage Error reduced by 31.2% on average), alongside meaningful improvements in inventory turnover (up 24.7%), safety stock reduction (down 19.4%), and stockout frequency (down 28.6%), compared to organizations relying exclusively on traditional time-series methods. Regression analysis identifies model sophistication, data richness, and supply chain integration depth as the primary predictors of inventory optimization outcomes. The study proposes a three-stage AI Forecasting Maturity Model and offers a prioritized implementation roadmap for practitioners. Theoretical contributions include an extension of the Information Processing Theory to the AI-augmented supply chain context and the development of a validated AI Forecasting-Inventory Performance (AFIP) framework.

detail.title: Digital Transformation and Its Influence on Decision-Making Processes in Businesses
detail.abstract: In the present-day business, this digital transformation has become one of the driving changes. Through its implementation of digital technologies, including, but not limited to, big data analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and automation, it improves organizational processes and performance. The digital transformation has had one of the biggest influences on business decision-making. Data-driven approaches are taking a larger role over traditional decision-making methods which was much more intuition-driven and based on past experience. The paper explored the concept of digital transformation and how it will affect the way decisions are made in businesses. The paper demonstrates the importance of digital tools in the reduction of the error of decision making, time and strategizing as well as others like security of the data, lack of skills and change resistance
